News.title: In ‘Possible Love,’ a South Korean auteur returns with a story of marriage, labor and class
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

There are some filmmakers who churn movies out like clockwork. And then there are others, like South Korean auteur Lee Chang-dong, who wait until they have something worthwhile to say. For movie lovers, it makes the arrival of his latest film “Possible Love,” now streaming on Netflix, something like an event.

His last film, “Burning,” a meditative thriller about three young people, was the first South Korean feature to be shortlisted for an Oscar, and was singled out by many critics as the best of 2018. And though South Korean cinema has soared at the Oscars since, Lee didn't feel rushed to get back in the mix as quickly as possible. This, he said, is not patience, exactly, but more of a pathological timidness.

“This is a big problem of mine,” the 72-year-old filmmaker told The Associated Press earlier this year, with the help of a translator. “With every film I do, I constantly ask myself, what meaning does this have? Is this a story worth telling?”

Lee was inspired by mass autoworker layoffs

This time, he found himself drawn to the story of mass layoffs in his home country. In 2009, the Ssangyong Motor Co. laid off about one-third of its workforce, which led to a high-profile confrontation between police and workers who occupied the company’s plant south of Seoul for more than two months. A spate of suicides among Ssangyong workers and family members also followed the automaker’s restructuring.

“I thought that that particular event not only was going to change the labor market of Korea, but also Korean society as a whole,” Lee said. “I thought that it was going to be, indeed, a significant turning point, and I thought it was going to fundamentally change not only the lives of those laid off workers, but also just everyday ordinary people’s lives as well.”

Others have taken on the effects of the mounting debt, unemployment and desperation in the country in fiction before, including the brutally violent “Squid Game," and Park Chan-wook's satirical “No Other Choice.”

Lee's approach wasn't going to be either of those, but he couldn’t run away from the nagging question of whether or not he was worthy to tell this story. Was there meaning, he wondered, in making it a dramatic film and not a documentary? Then, about two years ago, his cowriter Oh Jung-mi had a breakthrough: Why not connect this story with the story of a filmmaker trying to capture it? And suddenly, it started to make sense.

The story focuses on two couples, one wealthy, one not

But he’d been talking about it for so long that actor Jeon Do-yeon was a little suspicious when he reached out and asked if she wanted to be in the film. Jeon had starred in his 2007 drama “Secret Sunshine,” playing a young widow consumed by grief and anger after her son is murdered that would win her a best actress prize at the Cannes Film Festival.

“I’m personally such a big fan of his. I adore his films and I think his films are really precious,” Jeon said. “When he suggested that we work together on this film, we had been having discussions about it for about 10 years so I couldn’t actually really believe him … I kept asking for the script and only by reading the script would I truly believe that he was going to make this film.”

The script, she was happy to discover, was real, and her part was another special one: This time she would be playing Mi-ok, the optimistic spouse of a laid off autoworker, Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu). When a well-heeled documentary filmmaker Ye-ji ( “Parasite's” Cho Yeo-jeong ) approaches them about capturing their life and telling the story of laid off workers, she’s openhearted and eager to talk. Ho-seok, who is dealing with depression, is less open.

“She’s not able to get her husband the psychological help that she wants him to have in order for him to heal and recover, so she’s hoping by getting the help of the documentary filmmaker that he will get better in this way,” Jeon said.

Exploring two kinds of masculinity in South Korea

Mi-ok is also entranced by Ye-ji’s husband, Sang-woo (Zo In-sung), a handsome and wealthy businessperson who, at least on the surface, seems to be a kind of ideal. At one point, Mi-ok fawningly compares him to Steve Jobs. And while Ye-ji and Mi-ok might appear to be developing a friendship, the fact that it’s in service of a documentary makes it less pure.

Lee, though in part telling a story about himself telling a story, made his filmmaker character a woman. In South Korea, he said there are many female documentary filmmakers.

“I think they also have a stronger sense of empathy and great emotional intelligence,” he said. “I also wanted her husband to be representing that force, that power of wealth and capital.”

The film also provided a chance to talk about masculinity through two different characters. Ho-seok, Lee said, “embodies a masculinity that really belongs to the typical Korean male. He has a very heavy sense of responsibility for his family. He treats his co-workers as his brothers.”

When he’s laid off from his job and beaten by the police, his loss of identity is profound and intense.

“He finds himself feeling completely empty, that he has nothing to offer,” Lee said. “On the other hand, Sang-woo represents a new kind of masculinity, one that maybe belongs to the new era, I would say. He is very kind, very humane. He’s also very soft. He’s the ever-helpful husband to Ye-ji, he’s also a good listener. However, all of that with a very, very tightly masked sense of violence.”

‘Possible Love’ is a possible Oscar contender

“Possible Love” has been racking up accolades and acclaim since the Venice Film Festival, where it won the runner-up prize. South Korea has also selected it as its official submission for best international feature at the 99th Academy Awards.

But before the film’s premiere in Venice, Lee brushed off the suggestion that people are eagerly awaiting new films from him, saying he doesn’t think that people place that much interest in his work.

“He really said that?” Jeon asked later.

When I assure her that he did, she paused and smiled and switched, ever so briefly, to English for the first time in the interview: “Liar,” she said.

News.title: Officials search for the bear that killed a mother and daughter in British Columbia
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Selah Reed's family first knew something was wrong when the 20-year-old missed a routine Saturday night call with her sister.

When no one had heard from Reed or her mother, Jenny Balcarras, by the next morning, they asked the Royal Canadian Mounted Police to check on their home in Bella Coola on British Columbia's central coast. Balcarras' car was gone and the doors were locked. They found the car at a trailhead up the road, but Balcarras and Reed were nowhere to be found.

Family members across Canada and the U.S. started mobilizing. Jenny Balcarras' brother, Matt, headed north from Vancouver Island, and his brother left from Calgary. They met and drove through the night but got a call late Monday that their sister had been killed, likely by a grizzly.

When they arrived at the trailhead Tuesday morning, ready to join the search for Reed, her remains had also been found. The search was now a tragic recovery effort.

The killings of Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter happened only 3 to 4 kilometers (1.8 to 2.4 miles) from where a grizzly attacked a group of schoolchildren and teachers last year as they walked on a trail. Eleven were injured, two of them critically, in the Nov. 20, 2025, attack.

Jeff Tyre, an inspector with the Conservation Officer Service, said that aggressive bear was never captured, but officials were able to collect its DNA. Officials have set new traps in the hopes of catching the bear involved in last weekend’s attack and to learn whether it was the same bear from a year ago. They also are not sure whether more than one bear was involved.

Terry Webber, chief administrative officer for the Nuxalk Nation, said the killings were triggering for the families who were traumatized by last year’s attack.

“Our community is still healing,” he said, adding that they’ve imposed a curfew and are providing mental health services for the community. “Our priority is to ensure they’re safe and ensure our community is supported.”

Bear attack complicated the search

The delay in finding the remains of the two women was complicated by difficult terrain, even though it was close to the trailhead, and the grizzly bear's behavior.

Searchers found Jenny Balcarras first, then her daughter. The search was helped by more resources and a cadaver dog, Matt Balcarras said.

Searchers found his niece's remains in a bear cache — a place where bears stash food, sometimes by digging a small hole and covering it with branches and vegetation to keep other animals and birds away.

“Even though it was within 100 or so meters (330 feet), locating remains in a cache is difficult,” he said.

By the time officials located his niece, she could only be identified by her clothing, he said. His sister was in a similar condition, but they knew who she was thanks to several tiny tattoos, he said.

“There's no obvious body to identify,” he said. “The coroner’s investigation will include DNA and dental work. But there is no doubt that the remains that were found are theirs.”

Balcarras was comfortable in challenging environments

Grizzly bears are common in the area surrounding the Bella Coola community, officials said. Conservation officials maintain a hotline where people can report problem bears, but no calls had been received recently, Tyre said during a media briefing.

Balcarras, an art therapist, had moved to Bella Coola during the summer. She had previously lived in Alaska, where her children were born, and was “the central organizing person in our family,” Matt Balcarras said.

“In classic, strong single-mother style, she scraped together a career and a life for herself and her kids,” Balcarras said. She was small in stature but strong in character and physical abilities, he said.

She was comfortable living among the wildlife, he said.

“She lived in the Bush when her kids were babies," he said. “She and my niece were not naive or foolish or uninformed. They’ve lived in these areas and have been around animals of countless types for years and years and decades.”

News.title: 25 years after 'Britney,' 5 new Britney Spears songs showcase a pop icon at a transformative moment
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Britney Spears was at a crossroads — and not just because the film “Crossroads” was soon to be released, marking her acting debut.

The year was 2001. Spears, then just 19, was one of the most famous people on the planet, championed as the ultimate teen dream by legions of fans across the globe and a leering celebrity industry. That year, she'd performed during the Super Bowl halftime show and changed the course of fashion forever — first, showing up with beau Justin Timberlake in matching denim at the American Music Awards and then with an albino python around her neck during her performance at the MTV Video Music Awards.

She was entering adulthood, full steam ahead, after enjoying a meteoric run with her first two albums, 1999's “… Baby One More Time” and 2000's “Oops! … I Did It Again.” Her third album, “Britney,” was being released just ahead of her 20th birthday and would prove transformative.

Legacy Recordings on Friday is releasing “Britney (25th Anniversary Edition),” an expanded reissue of her pivotal record, which went quadruple platinum in less than two months. The collection features two remixes and five previously unreleased songs from that era, her first new (or is it old?) music since she announced she would “never return to the music industry” in a 2024 Instagram post.

The release is an opportunity to reflect on the album and Spears' unique position in popular culture's imagination — particularly following the news of the last few years. In 2021, she was released from a court conservatorship that controlled the pop singer’s life and money for nearly 14 years. And in February, it was announced that she had sold the rights to her music catalog to Primary Wave for an undisclosed sum.

Listening to ‘Britney,’ 25 years later

The album opens with a spoken-word declaration. Back in 2001, it was considered a provocation — as it often is when a young woman expresses her own prerogative.

“I know I may be young,” Spears seduces over choppy R&B production, courtesy The Neptunes, the award-winning duo of Pharrell Williams and Chad Hugo. “But I’ve got feelings, too.”

The song is the single “I'm A Slave 4 U,” where Spears made it clear that the bubblegum pop of her previous releases had been traded in for something decidedly more mature. And that's true even of the album's songs written and produced by previous collaborators Max Martin and Rami Yacoub — tracks like “Bombastic Love” still sparkle, but with newfound edge.

If Spears was borrowing from the teen-to-adult pop star trajectory laid forth by forebears like Madonna or Janet Jackson on “Britney,” she did so while keeping it PG-13 — hinting at developed sensuality as a means to express self-definition, but remaining accessible and agreeable to her younger audience. To put it another way, she toes the line: “I'm not a girl, not yet a woman,” as the single goes.

That's all while proclamations of autonomy — sexual and otherwise — punctuate the album. “Say hello to the girl that I am,” she invites on “Overprotected.” “Now I live for me,” she flips the script on “Lonely.” “She's in control,” on the funky, erotic “Boys.”

A sense of self-reflection is amplified by the fact that the album is self-titled, and that Spears co-wrote five songs on the original album: “Lonely,” “Anticipating,” “Let Me Be,” “That's Where You Take Me” and the spiky “Cinderella.”

The previously unreleased ‘Britney’ songs add to Spears' mythology

The first of the five archival tracks is “She’ll Never Be Me,” co-written with Timberlake, her then-boyfriend, who also sings background. Timberlake cowrote a track on the original album, but the new release comes after Spears wrote about their relationship in her 2023 memoir, sharing deeply personal details about a pregnancy, abortion and painful breakup.

As far as how it fits in with the rest of the album, the song slots in nicely with its vocal effects and propulsive Y2K production — by any measure, it makes for a fine B-side.

The same could be said of the rest, from the slow-burn fake-out “Am I A Sinner" and Latin pop-informed rhythms of “Right Now (Taste the Victory)” to the glitchy, proto-hyperpop “When I Say So” and soulful, unusually lengthy “My Big Secret,” which features Spears' strongest vocal performance of the whole album. It's a stunning falsetto.

Thematically, a number of these tracks could be read as a response to the tabloid press' obsession with Spears' virginity at the time of its release. “I don't want to mislead you,” she sings on “When I Say So.” “You'll get some when I say so.”

And on “Am I A Sinner” she may very well be reflecting back on an unjust media — or any bad relationship: “Tell me, am I a sinner? / Tell me, am I wrong? / Something's wrong with the picture / This is not my fault.”

Since the release of her bestselling memoir, “The Woman in Me” — which details her childhood, rise to stardom, marriages, motherhood and conservatorship — fans have worked to recontextualize how Spears was portrayed early on in her career. These songs will no doubt inspire more detective work. But others may approach it more simply, through the rose-colored glasses of easy nostalgia.

In the end, it is an album written and recorded in the space between adolescence and adulthood, from the woman a generation looked to for guidance on doing the same.

News.title: Uninsured and flooded out, a Colorado man worries if life will be normal again
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Matthew Martinez has lived nearly all of his 60 years in a canyon on the Navajo River and never saw severe floods.

Then twice over the last two weeks the river surged through his home and outbuildings in far southwestern Colorado, about 25 miles (40 kilometers) south of the resort town of Pagosa Springs. Now he's missing a horse, his barn is damaged and the river swallowed a corral. The house is strewn with mud. His tools washed downstream.

“We’re in trouble, all of us are. Not just me, everybody,” Martinez said through tears during his first visit back on Wednesday. He said several families that go back 100 years in the same canyon had similar damage. “Nobody expected this.”

The Navajo, San Juan and Animas rivers were just a few of the streams to surge beyond their banks when round after round of storms dumped heavy rain across the Four Corners region of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah.

Scientists say a supercharged El Niño event — when warm water in the Pacific disrupts weather patterns — is making heavy rains more likely and intense across the Southern U.S.

Recent flooding has struck Flagstaff, Arizona; Pagosa Springs and Durango in southwestern Colorado; Farmington in northwestern New Mexico; tiny Bluff in southeastern Utah; parts of the vast Navajo Nation and Sedona and Tucson in Arizona.

With a break in the weather at last, evacuees are returning home.

For Martinez, who was out of town for knee surgery, getting back meant navigating a mucky mess with a four-wheel drive vehicle and a lot of patience over beaten gravel roads. And he's finding his struggles may have just begun.

Martinez didn’t have flood insurance. He couldn’t get it with his house so near the water. He estimates some $200,000 in losses, at least.

He and his fiancee were staying with one of his sons and then in a hotel, but both places have since flooded. Now they're in an Airbnb, but he worries they could end up homeless after his emergency voucher runs out in a few days.

"The government spends, you know, just millions and billions of money on overseas and everything. Right now we need that money on this side,” he said. “We need to get this, you know, all this put back together.”

A FEMA representative came to his property and took photos after the first flood. The second flood hit three days later and was twice as bad, he said.

“I know we’re on some list right now,” Martinez said. “So we’ll listen every day and we’ll see what options we have and go from there.”

As he heals from the knee surgery, he's considering whether it's worth it to ask family and friends for help cleaning up.

Hauling debris to the dump would cost $300 a load and total thousands of dollars he doesn’t readily have, he said.

The flooding did help end months of drought in the Four Corners area, but the raging torrents washed away rich topsoil on his land, leaving just sand and rock. Now he wonders how he'll feed his remaining animals without pasture next year.

“The normal might not ever be normal again,” Martinez said.

___

Gruver reported from Fort Collins, Colo.

News.title: US stocks plummet as Democrat victory sparks investor panic
News.content:
Wall Street suffered its worst sell-off since Donald Trump’s tariff rollout amid fears the Democrats will derail the AI boom.

The Nasdaq 100 plunged more than 6pc on Thursday - the biggest fall since April 2025 - with shares in semiconductor makers the hardest hit.

The downturn was the worst since Mr Trump’s so-called “liberation day”, when he rolled out tariffs to countries around the world.

Investors fear the Democrats’ midterm election victory will usher in tighter restrictions on AI companies, whose valuations have grown rapidly under Mr Trump.

Nvidia, which is the world’s most valuable listed company, fell by more than 6pc while rivals including AMD and Micron plummeted 13pc and 11pc, respectively.

News.title: Can the UK handle an Ebola infection?
News.content:
A British man who has tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is being flown back to the UK for treatment.

The patient, whose identity has not been revealed, but is believed to be a healthcare worker, is said to be in a stable condition.

They will be transferred to a specialist ambulance and then on to the Royal Free hospital, a rare diseases specialist hospital in north London, which houses the UK’s primary high level isolation unit.

Yesterday, a UK government spokesperson said there were “well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this” and that the risk to the public “remains low”.

It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DRC. The first cases of the Bundibugyo strain of the disease were reported in May, and there have so far been more than 10,000 cases and 5,000 deaths, making it the second largest outbreak in history.

How will the British patient be treated?

The immediate priority will be to assess their condition.

On average, symptoms appear between eight to 10 days after exposure, but they can arise as soon as two days and as many as three weeks after infection. Doctors will have to determine how far the virus has progressed and identify any complications that require treatment.

Ebola can cause severe fluid loss, through profuse vomiting and diarrhoea, electrolyte imbalances and in serious cases organ failure. Experts will closely monitor his vital signs and fluid balance, bloods and organ function, providing intravenous fluids and other supportive treatment.

News.title: Bank of England raises interest rates for first time in three years
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The value of the pound has risen to its highest level in two months as the Bank of England prepares to raise interest rates.

Sterling climbed 0.2pc against the dollar to nearly $1.35 on Thursday, its highest level since September.

It came as traders responded to the likelihood that the Bank of England will increase rates for the first time in three years on Thursday.

This reflects the Bank’s attempt to keep inflation under control after the Iran war energy shock pushed price rises to an 11-month high.

Typically, higher borrowing costs strengthen the pound by boosting demand for UK interest-bearing assets among foreign investors.

The pound was also buoyed by a weaker dollar after the Democrats swept to victory in the US midterms on Wednesday.

Political upheaval hit the dollar as traders bet that deadlock in Washington will lead to curbs on Donald Trump’s runaway spending.

This brought down the cost of US government borrowing, which in turn brought down the dollar.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “The prospect of a divided government eased concerns about the fiscal trajectory, given it’ll now be more difficult to pass tax cuts or spending packages.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Burnham makes new North Sea drilling illegal | Energy independence bill would prevent future ministers from easily reversing exploration ban

2) Blue wave threatens to derail America’s AI boom | Democratic candidates swept to power amid voters’ growing resentment toward data centres

3) Majority of London’s bridges are falling down | Advisers warn 24 Thames crossings are in poor condition and require urgent repairs

4) Silicon Valley investor shuts London office as US dominates AI | Firm known for early backing of Apple and Google doesn’t ‘see the need’ for presence in Britain

5) Trump rages at Fox News as Republican voters switch off | Once a powerful force in US politics, the Murdoch TV channel’s influence is fading

What happened overnight

Oil, chip stocks and the dollar were under pressure in Asia ​after ‌the Democrats swept to a series of stunning midterm election wins.

Brent crude dived nearly 9pc overnight, falling below $100 a barrel, and has dropped by about 20pc so far this week.

If sustained through to Friday’s close, it would make for the largest weekly drop in oil prices since April 2020 when US crude briefly fell into negative territory.

Tumbling energy prices encouraged a rally in bonds, which lowered yields, pulled the dollar to a one-month low of $1.1273 per euro, and helped stocks. The yield on the benchmark 10-year note fell to a two-month low and was last at 4.85pc.

Broad stock indexes climbed on the clear outcome, with the S&P 500 closing 1.6pc higher and European shares notching a two-month high, although tech stocks struggled as investors fear greater scrutiny over AI infrastructure build-out.

European stocks were on track to open 0.2pc higher, while the Nasdaq in the US fell 1pc in premarket trading, indicating investor angst over chip and data centre stocks.

Democratic data-centre ⁠opponents who campaigned, in part, on moratoriums on data centre construction won stunning victories in Texas and Georgia in a sign public opinion is shifting on AI.

South Korea’s chipmaker-heavy Kospi sank nearly 6pc and remained within a whisker of a new seven-month low. Taiwan’s benchmark index fell over 3pc, poised for an 8pc weekly decline, its worst weekly performance since April 2025.

Tech equipment suppliers dragged on the Nikkei, which ​fell 2pc, although the broader Topix was 0.8pc higher, underscoring the divergent ‌market reaction to the decisive election results.

News.title: Is America on the brink of sparking a new flu pandemic?
News.content:
Of the 75 human cases in the US, at least 50 have been linked directly to cattle farming, meaning the outbreak in cows has become the main route by which the virus is reaching people.

Most human cases linked to cattle have been mild, and far less dangerous than historic cases linked to infections from wild or farmed birds. Of the roughly 1,000 human cases of H5N1 linked to birds since it first emerged in China in 1997, around half have died.

But on November 1, the first person to be infected with the cow variant of H5N1, known as genotype B.13, was confirmed to have died.

The individual, who worked on a farm in Washington where at least 40 herds have been infected with H5N1, had underlying health conditions, which may have exacerbated the disease, and died shortly after becoming sick – but the development is still of concern, say experts.

“This goes against the pattern of mild disease when infected from dairy cattle, versus severe disease when infected from birds, which is worrying given the circulation in cattle,” said Dr Sridhar.

Reassortment risks

One of the biggest fears among scientists is that bird flu could combine with ordinary seasonal influenza to create a new strain capable of spreading easily between people.

“This is a time of year when we can expect to see more circulation of [human] seasonal influenza,” said Dr Marion Koopmans, professor of public health virology at Erasmus MC Medical Centre in the Netherlands.

“A bad scenario would be that someone working with cattle brought the ‘regular’ human flu in, got [H5N1] on top of that, and that develops into a mix that can spread but to which people have less immunity.

“The chances of such an event are very low, but it is a concern shared among virologists.”

The process, known as reassortment, occurs when two flu viruses infect the same animal or person and exchange genetic material, potentially creating a new strain.

Scientists are particularly concerned as H5N1 spreads beyond cattle and into other mammals – chiefly mink.

For more than two months, an outbreak has raged on a Utah farm housing thousands of mink, according to an investigation by US news outlet ProPublica.

Mink farms have previously been described as potential pandemic “time bombs”, because their respiratory systems are similar to those of humans, meaning viruses spread easily between them and people.

Despite calls for the animals to be culled, Utah officials have so far refused to mandate action, ProPublica reported.

The investigation also suggested that state officials were prioritising the financial interests of the fur industry, which exports much of its produce to China and Russia, while federal authorities had failed to intervene.

News.title: Attacks on water infrastructure intensify in conflict zones, warns Unicef
News.content:
Water infrastructure is coming increasingly under attack in conflict zones, leading to disease outbreaks and forcing civilians to make dangerous journeys to fill buckets, according to a new report.

Water Under Fire, published by United Nations children’s agency Unicef, found that attacks have become “more frequent, varied and geographically widespread”.

It said the number of attacks that damaged or destroyed water systems tripled between 2021 and 2025.

Recorded incidents, ranging from strikes on water plants to restrictions on access to water treatment chemicals, rose from less than 45 in eight countries in 2021 to more than 135 in 15 nations by 2025, according to data from Insecurity Insight, a Geneva-based humanitarian organisation that tracks threats facing people in conflict.

Maia Giorgio, humanitarian policy specialist at Unicef, stressed that the report only covers documented attacks, warning that it may be “just the tip of the iceberg”.

“It’s a global phenomenon, and unfortunately, it’s under-documented,” she said.

“Without water, you don’t have a functioning healthcare system. Without water, you can’t prevent infectious disease, and we know that children are particularly vulnerable,” she added.

News.title: Man City have a striker who will not be stopped and a defence that cannot be trusted
News.content:
“You can look at it that it’s difficult to keep concentrated for 100 minutes or you can look at it like it’s only 100 minutes you have to stay focussed to get a chance – you can look at it in a few different ways and I look at it in the second option,” Haaland added.

This was a victory to bounce back from losing in the Premier League at the weekend, but the question will be how can City mount a title challenge with such a brittle defence. Champions League winners do not leave themselves open at the back like this, and City have now gone seven games without a clean sheet.

Maresca insisted last week that his starting line-up is Donnarumma plus 10 others, but the reality is that Haaland is the guaranteed name on the team sheet. And his goalkeeper’s errors are becoming a problem.

This one added to the goals against Aston Villa and Paris St-Germain that were also on his watch. He could have claimed the cross that led to Brighton’s winner at the weekend too.

Here he went from hero to villain in the space of a few minutes at the start of the second half. Firstly, from kick-off Christoph Baumgartner got close with his angled drive heading towards the top corner until Donnarumma’s fingertips turned the ball around the post. It was a save that had the Italian celebrating like he had scored a goal.

But he had his head in his hands after Leipzig’s next move. Nico O’Reilly could have done better after losing the ball in midfield, then failing to track the overlapping run from Baku. With Red Bull Arena waiting for a cross, Baku had spotted Donnarumma slightly out of position and beat him at the near post. It was superb improvisation, but without doubt a goalkeeping error.

News.title: Gyokeres the creator and executioner to see nervous Arsenal past Slavia Prague
News.content:
“Really good,” said Arteta of Gyokeres. “Not only the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s great news, because I think he needed that performance.”

Those two moments in the first half eventually ensured another European victory for Arteta’s side, but the manager was far from impressed with the second-half showing. So smooth at first, Arsenal became remarkably ragged by the end. Slavia were deserving of their goal, scored by Wiktor Nowak. It looked like complacency had infected the minds of the Arsenal players, and you could feel Arteta’s fury radiating from the touchline.

“We scored two goals and it should have been three, four or five,” said Arteta. “And at half-time the message was clear: there is still a lot to do in this game. Right from the beginning of the second half, we were extremely far from our standards in everything that we have to do, in every basic, in every concept, and in everything we discussed. So much to improve and I take full responsibility for that.”

Without Gabriel Magalhães and David Raya, who both made dramatic stops on the goal-line, this could have become an ugly night for Arsenal against one of the weaker teams in the Champions League. The Czech side have now gone 23 games without a victory in Europe’s premier competition, which equals the longest winless run in European Cup history.

It was a remarkable coincidence that this game fell on November 4, the exact date as the same fixture last season. On that occasion Arsenal were comfortable 3-0 winners, with Mikel Merino scoring twice, and they seemed to be heading towards a similar night when Madueke scored the early opener.

The goal was made by Gyokeres, who held off a defender and then hooked an excellent pass into Madueke’s path. The Arsenal winger had already established his dominance over Oskar Kubiak, his opposite number, and he reached fifth gear before the Polish defender had even reached second. Madueke then slid his finish beneath the body of Nazar Domchak, Slavia’s teenage goalkeeper.

News.title: Liverpool calamity hands Iraola his most chastening night yet
News.content:
Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

“Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found issue had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish’s England career was over ‘a long time ago’ with star having a ‘Gazza stroke’, says Alan Shearer
Sports.content:
Next

ALAN SHEARER says Jack Grealish has similarities to Paul Gascoigne after the “loveable rogue” was dropped by Everton.

The Newcastle legend Shearer weighed in on the situation after Grealish got himself into hot water with boss David Moyes.



The troubled winger, 31, hasn’t played for the Toffees since their defeat to Chelsea on October 17.

Moyes took action after a breach of discipline and he did not feature in either of their recent games against Newcastle.



He won’t play in Everton’s home clash against Coventry on Friday night either.

It later emerged that Grealish had reportedly failed to attend a scheduled training session without permission, prompting the club to take action against the former Aston Villa captain.



SunSport subsequently revealed that Grealish had enjoyed two nights out in London and Cheshire in the days leading up to his disciplinary punishment.

Shearer said the on-loan Man City star had a “Gazza stroke” about him – because he was a “loveable rogue”.

He backed Grealish’s ability and said there was still time for him to earn Moyes’ trust back again.

Speaking to Betfair, he said: “[Grealish] is a talented maverick. I’m not comparing him with Gazza at all, but he’s got a Gazza stroke, he can produce a piece of genius, and he’s also got a slightly Gazza mentality off the pitch.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“He’s a loveable rogue. Grealish knows what he needs to do to get back in David Moyes’ good books.

“All will be forgiven if he can get back on the pitch and start producing magic and pieces of brilliance that help Everton climb the table.”

However, he admitted the player’s England career was over and had been for some time.

He added: “I think Grealish’s England career was sealed a long time ago.



“There are too many others in his position who are playing well, so I don’t expect him to win a recall to the England squad.”

Shearer added that the situation was “not a good look” for Grealish and urged him to focus on football.

The legendary striker said: “Football is such a short career that you have to give it your best shot.

“Look, I get everyone wants to have a good time and I see no harm in having a good time and a fun time when the time is right and having a drink.

“But there is a time and Jack seems to like to party and have a drink. It has got the better of him at times.



“He’s such a likeable character and does a lot for charity. But you also have to understand that football is your main business, and it can’t happen too many times and at the minute it’s not a good look for him.”

Grealish has made five appearances in all competitions for Everton this season.

He was initially a big hit during his first loan spell with the Merseyside club last season before a crushing injury ended his campaign.

Grealish has previously won three Premier League titles with City, as wel as the FA Cup and Champions League.

Sports.title: ‘Concerned’ Leicester City release statement after club’s main sponsor name porn star as ambassador
Sports.content:

LEICESTER CITY have released a statement admitting “concerns” after their main sponsor named a porn star as an ambassador.

The Foxes initially signed a deal with online casino platform BC Game in the summer of 2024.



The company has Leicester City‘s shirt sponsor ever since through the last three seasons.

But there has been anger from fans about BC Game partnering with adult film star Eva Elfie.



The club’s supporters group The Foxes Trust expressed its “dismay” about the news.

Leicester have addressed the situation and said they were looking to find a “mutually acceptable resolution”.

Their statement read: “Leicester City Football Club recognises the concerns raised about recent developments involving our Principal Partner, BC.GAME.

“We have raised these concerns directly with BC.GAME and are continuing discussions with the company to explore a mutually acceptable resolution.“

The fans group initially said: “Most Leicester City supporters will know by now the trust’s dismay and discontent with BC Game being our front of shirt sponsor.

“BC Game have now announced a new partnership with ‘international content creator and esports personality’ Eva Elfie… who just happens to be an international porn star.

Sports.title: England face battle to keep hold of Shea Lacey, 19, as rival international manager targets in-form Man Utd star
Sports.content:
Next

REPUBLIC OF IRELAND boss Heimir Hallgrimsson is eyeing Shea Lacey.

The Manchester United winger was born in Liverpool and is an England youth international but is eligible for Ireland through his dad Paddy.



Lacey, 19, set up Matheus Cunha’s winner in the midweek 3-2 Champions League comeback victory against Roma.

Asked if he has been in contact with the teen ahead of next week’s Nations League clash with Austria, Hallgrimsson said: “That would be for other guys in the association.



“But it was interesting looking at his Irish connection.”

Lacey has represented England from Under-15 level through to the Under-20s.



He made his United full first-team debut in the Carabao Cup 3-2 loss to Brighton in September, but he scored the opener after just seven minutes.

Hallgrimsson’s Ireland assistant manager is Old Trafford cult hero John O’Shea.

The Icelandic gaffer also revealed ex-Everton full-back Seamus Coleman will work with Ireland in a coaching role.

Lacey started out at Man Utd’s academy before making his debut in December 2025.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The winger has since amassed a total of one goal and one assist in ten appearances across all competitions.

The forward came on for the final 16 minutes on Tuesday against Roma at Old Trafford and quickly made history.

Lacey set up Cunha’s brace and became the youngest United player to assist a Champions League winner.

Sports.title: Mathys Tel’s incredible turnaround continues with Tottenham forward ‘in line for shock call-up to France national team’
Sports.content:
Next

MATHYS TEL could be in line for a shock call-up to the French national team.

The forward has been experiencing a rich vein of form with Roberto De Zerbi‘s resurgent Tottenham side.



Spurs have won three league fixtures in a row, with Tel starting the latter two on the left wing against Chelsea and Crystal Palace.

His glorious solo run and finish to seal the three points at Stamford Bridge was even nominated for the Premier League Goal of the Month award for October.



The former Bayern Munich youngster has not had the smoothest of transitions to the English game since arriving on loan with an option to buy in February 2025.

But he seems to have found his feet now, and has done enough to reportedly find himself in international contention.



According to L’Equipe, the 21-year-old is being looked at by new France boss Zinedine Zidane for a spot in his 23-man squad, set to be announced on Friday.

The French unit will take on Turkey and Italy in the Nations League, with Les Bleus currently top of Group A.

The Real Madrid legend is without first-choice options Ousmane Dembele and Esteban Lepaul in forward areas, with Tel able to deputise in the No9 role when called upon.

He is no stranger to international football, having featured for a number of age groups right up to U21.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Last month he scored a hat-trick while captaining the side against Switzerland U21, which has helped boost his chances of breaking into the first team alongside his club performances.

But he still faces stiff competition from the likes of Inter Milan attacker Marcus Thuram.

The towering forward has been a regular in the French national side in recent years, and starred for the team at the last two World Cups.

He has scored five times and assisted twice in the opening nine games of the Serie A season, and boasts 35 caps for his country.



But if there was ever a time to experiment, now would be the time.

Zidane has had just one international break with the team before now – and with a healthy lead on his Group A rivals, now would be the moment to see who else could fit into his future plans.

Sports.title: Three transfers Man Utd could target in January including Man City outcast and Fulham back-up with funds limited
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED are open to bolstering their defence and attack in the winter transfer window.

United failed to bring in a left back or a back-up striker in the summer and there is a private acceptance that they fell short with their squad strengthening.



Left back Luke Shaw will not return until after the international break, having played in just five of their 14 games this season. Striker Benjamin Sesko is sidelined until January with a shin injury.

United have limited funds and have resorted to frugal deals in recent January windows. The club finalised loan moves for Jack Butland, Wout Weghorst and Marcel Sabitzer in 2023 and did deals for up-and-comers Patrick Dorgu and Ayden Heaven in 2025.



The possibility of a change of head coach would not have a major bearing as director of football Jason Wilcox is in charge of recruitment.

Fulham centre forward Rodrigo Muniz is a short-term option as he has only started in the League Cup for the Cottagers this term.

Muniz, 25, played for Michael Carrick during a loan spell at Middlesbrough, where he started once under the United head coach due to a four-month lay-off.

Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri was offered to United on transfer deadline day but the club passed on a deal.

Ait-Nouri, 25, has made one start under Enzo Maresca – in the League Cup. City were seeking a loan deal with an obligation to buy from United, who had no interest in a permanent deal.

Lewis Hall signed a new contract with Newcastle in September but is considered a realistic target by United for the summer.



Fellow left back Tyrick Mitchell, 27, is about to enter the final six months of his Crystal Palace deal and would be a cost-efficient alternative in January, but he is outside United’s preferred age range of 22-26.

Any mid-season incomings at United would also likely be contingent on departures, with Joshua Zirkzee and Harry Amass two players who could make way for new recruits.



United blocked a deadline day move to Everton for Zirkzee, who has still not started a game this season and mustered three club goals in the past 18 months.

Zirkzee has generated interest from Italian clubs in the two winter windows he has spent at United, having joined the club from Bologna in 2024.

Amass has changed agents twice already since the start of the season as he looks to secure a permanent switch in the new year. The 19-year-old has not started once, despite Shaw’s lengthy injury lay-off.

Carrick has started winger Dorgu, right backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui, as well as centre back Heaven at left back ahead of Amass.

United are set to release the injury-prone Shaw, who is into his 13th season with United, when his contract expires in June.

Sports.title: Brighton fans rage at tiny away allocation as impressive European victory played in front of empty stands
Sports.content:
Next

BRIGHTON fans were left fuming after being given a tiny allocation for their trip to Getafe where they won 1-0.

The Seagulls jetted out to Madrid for their Conference League away day this week as they continue their bid to reach the knockouts.

Brighton supporters turned out in the droves to inspire their team in the Spanish capital.



But after selling out their allocation, they were stunned to find out they had only been allowed 562 tickets.



A shocking image circulating on social media shows the Brighton supporters boxed into a very small stand behind the goal.

Getafe’s Estadio Coliseum has a capacity of 16,500 and swathes of empty seats were seen dotted around the ground.

And some fans were fuming after seeing an entire section above the away end had been left completely unfilled.

A number of them couldn’t hide their frustrations after the eye-catching picture came to light.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

One said: “Give that allocation to us we all win – Getafe get the money we get the seats, diabolical.”

Another claimed: “Hundreds of us stuck in bars in Madrid as Getafe refused to sell more tickets.”



A third added: “Loads of us sat watching thinking how didn’t we get more tickets!!!”

And a fourth backed up the claims from the Brighton supporters as he said: “Wouldn’t sell us anymore despite there being tons available.”

One football fan wrote: “Absolutely ridiculous, at least give them the upper tier as well.”

According to Uefa rules, clubs only have to give an away team five per cent of their stadium capacity.

And with Getafe’s capacity currently reduced to 11,000 amid renovations, the LaLiga side were entitled to provide the allocation that they did.



The Brighton fans that were in attendance ended up having a top evening as Fabian Hurzeler‘s men triumphed 1-0.

Malick Yalcouye netted a superb header mid-way through the second half and that was enough for all three points.

The Seagulls are now fifth in the Conference League standings after two wins, one draw and zero losses.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo vs Lionel Messi compared on & off pitch from Wags to riches as both retire from international football
Sports.content:
Next

IT’S the end of the era for two of the game’s great.

Just weeks after Lionel Messi hung up his international boots, Cristiano Ronaldo has done the same.



The Portuguese legend, 41, will no longer play for his country after walking out on the team following a bust-up.

He shared the news in an emotional video on social media, in the wake of clashing with manager Jorge Jesus.



In comparison, Messi, 39, went out on a high with a fairytale friendly against Benin in a packed Buenos Aires stadium.

He scored once and provided two assists, as he waved farewell to his adoring fans.



Off the pitch the pair have amassed incredible wealth, thanks to glittering football careers and successful businesses.

They’ve also managed to combine an insane work ethic with married life and big families.

On the international stage

On the international stage, Ronaldo and Messi have been goal machines.

Fuelled by a desire to lift major trophies, their rivalry continued as they became elder statesman of the sport.



Messi made his debut aged 18 in 2005 for Argentina against Hungary, although he was sent off just 47 seconds after coming on as a sub.

Ronaldo’s debut was a real passing of the baton. Also 18, he replaced Portugal legend Luis Figo on the left-wing at half-time in a match against Kazakhstan.

Messi would earn a staggering 208 caps for the Argies, scoring 126 goals across his international career.



Ronaldo trumped Messi’s numbers, with 234 caps and 146 goals for Portugal.

However, Messi achieved a feat that alluded Ronaldo – lifting the World Cup in 2022.

Ronaldo’s biggest international honour came in 2016, when Portugal won the Euros in a 1-0 win over France.

On a personal level, Messi was recipient of the Ballon d’Or a record eight times, while Ronaldo has a mere golden balls in his trophy time.



Business acumen

Both players have received huge salaries from their clubs, including Barcelona, Manchester United Real Madrid, Juventus and Al Nassr.

But, it’s Ronaldo’s contract with the Saudi Arabia team that’s simply insane.



In 2025, he signed an extension on his deal worth a minimum £492million across two years.

It was the most lucrative contract a footballer has ever been given, and pumped his net worth up to over £1billion.

Earlier this year, Messi was also said to have joined the billionaire club, although his fortune was more due to savvy business interests.



His global business empire is said to be worth around £830million alone.

He has stakes in four clubs, Spanish sides, UE Cornella and CD Eldense, Uruguayan’s Deportivo LSM, as well as Inter Miami, when he retires.

His property portfolio boasts several hotels in places including Ibiza and Andorra.

Adidas also signed him up to a lifetime deal that will only serve to make him even richer.

Messi told the America Business Forum last year: “Business is something that interests me. I would like to keep learning because I know nothing and I am just starting out.”



Ronaldo recently invested his money in second-tier Spanish football team, Almeria.

But, he has his finger different pies. In 2025, he teamed up with British filmmaker Matthew Vaughn in setting up film studio, UR•Marv.

In 2024, before he had aspirations of becoming a movie mogul, Ronaldo launched his official YouTube channel, UR•Cristiano.



Since it began life, Ronaldo has featured in clips with Mr Beast, discussed football with Rio Ferdinand, and given fans a glimpse into his life as the world’s most famous footballer.

Ronaldo also has a global hotel chain. His Pestana CR7 hotels already boasts luxury sites in Lisbon, Funchal, Madrid, New York and Marrakech.

In 2027, they are planning to open resorts in Paris, Riyadh and the UK.



Cars

Ronaldo has splashed a large part of his wealth on an incredible car collection.

At last count, his garage was said to be worth around £100million.

Motors include an ultra-rare Bugatti Centodieci, worth a mind-boggling £12.5million.

With only ten ever built worldwide, the 1,600-horsepower beast shares space with his £5m Bugatti Chiron and a £2.5m Bugatti Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse.

The former Man Utd superstar also snapped up a breathtaking Ferrari SP3 Daytona, valued at up to £6m, alongside the open-top Ferrari Monza SP1, worth around £5m.



There’s also his everyday family runaround — a £500,000 Ferrari Purosangue SUV — and a classic Ferrari 599 GTO, which would have set him back around £1m.



If that wasn’t enough to make petrolheads weep, Ronaldo also squeezed in his track-ready Mercedes-AMG ONE — a £2.4m monster powered by a Formula 1 engine.

Messi’s car collection is believed to be worth around £500million, and features a very rare Pagani Zonda worth £4million.

But the most impressive motor in his fleet is a Ferrari 335 S Spider Scaglietti that he picked up for £28million.

He reportedly beat Ronaldo to buying it too, as their rivalry spilled from the pitch to the auction room.

Alongiside those supercars, Messi also favours car manufacturers like Audi, Land Rover, and Mercedes.



Wags

Messi and his wife Antonela Roccuzzo met when they were children, growing up in their hometown of Rosario, Argentina.

Their paths would cross again in 2000, when a friend of Antonela’s died in a car accident.



Upon hearing the news, the then 19-year-old Messi flew back to comfort Antonela and a romance soon blossomed.

They tied the knot in 2017, in a ceremony the Argentinian media called the ‘Wedding of the Century’.

They have three sons, Thiago, Mateo, and Ciro together, but Antonela has carved out her own career.

In 2014, she launched premium children’s clothing brand Enfans, while she has appeared in fashion campaigns for Alo Yoga, Tiffany and Co, Luis Vuitton, Guerlain & Lancôme.



Ronaldo met his missus, Georgina Rodriguez when she worked in a Gucci store in Madrid in 2016.

She has since branched out from sales assistant to become the world’s most recognised Wag, thanks in part to the Netflix reality show, I Am Georgina.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In August, the couple finally married in a highly private ceremony at their home in Cascais, attended by just their children and four witnesses.



Together, they raise their five children in Riyadh: Cristiano Ronaldo Jr, twins Eva and Mateo, and daughters Alana Martina and Bella Esmeralda.

Sports.title: Hearts bruised by Thun in self-inflicted Conference League defeat
Sports.content:
Depleted Hearts' Conference League bruising was almost totally self-inflicted in a 3-1 defeat by Thun in Switzerland.

Belgian boss Wouter Vrancken was without 10 players through various ailments and the Scottish team were dealt another blow in the 22nd minute when defender Jamie McCart put through his own goal in calamitous fashion.

Thun doubled their lead in the 33rd minute through striker Brighton Labeau after more poor defending, this time from skipper Stephen Kingsley - who went off later with an injury - and then Furkan Dursun grabbed a third in the 56th minute before Jambos defender Stuart Findlay reduced the deficit in the 82nd minute with a header.

Hearts are left with one Conference League point out of nine following a 1-1 home draw against Nordsjaelland and a 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

Thick smoke from a pyro halted the game soon after kick-off but when play resumed after a lengthy delay - there were nine minutes added on at the end of the first half - Hearts winger Josh McPake drew a save from Niklas Steffen with an angled drive that lacked real power.

In the 20th minute McPake's effort from 25 yards after he had drifted in from the left had the power but was beaten away by the Thun 'keeper.

There appeared to be nothing untoward on the horizon but then came a Hearts horror show.

There was no real pressure on the Jambos goal when a long ball came into the box but with Lucien Dahler at his shoulder, a simple pass back from McCart somehow evaded Hearts 'keeper Beau Reus and slipped into the corner of the net.

Thun's second goal was also gift-wrapped.

The home side broke clear and with pace following a Heart set-piece and when Nils Reichmuth crossed into the box from the right, Kingsley stuck out a leg to clear but the ball went straight to Labeau who swept it into the net from 10 yards out.

Dursun was shown a yellow card for a forearm challenge into the face of Findlay, and it perhaps deserved more punishment.

Image: Flares set off in the crowd stopped play early on

The interval gave the Tynecastle side time to reset but, three minutes after the break, Reus made a diving save from Dursun and an even better one from Reichmuth moments later.

However, the 'keeper was beaten once again when Dursun got his toe to a Reichmuth cross.

On the hour mark, Nico Maier raced clear of the Hearts defence but although his chip beat Reus, it sped wide of the target.

The night got worse for the rattled visitors as injured Kingsley was replaced by 19-year-old Matthew Gillies, called back from a loan spell at Stenhousemuir.

Hearts were sporadic in their threat.

Malachi Fagan-Walcott's header from a Jordi Altena free-kick was brilliantly saved by Steffen.

In the 78th minute Jan Bamert had the ball in the net after Steffen tipped a free-kick from substitute Nassim Zoukit on to the bar but was ruled offside, before Findlay headed in a consolation from another Altena free-kick.

Vrancken demands unity as Hearts seek to bounce back

Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken:

"We have to stick together now. We know which situation we're in with all the circumstances.

"And there's only one thing that you have to do now and that is stick together and keep working hard.

"In general, it was not good enough in quality and can you blame them?

"Yeah, on one hand you can because you want to always expect the best and want the best.

"On the other hand, I'm still proud of what they did already in the run-up games."

Sports.title: Anderson in talks with Surrey after Lancashire release
Sports.content:
James Anderson is in talks to join Surrey next season and extend his career in county cricket.

Anderson, 44, was released by boyhood club Lancashire in October after over 25 years of service, a decision he said left him "sad" and "quite shocked" and made him question if there was something "fundamentally wrong with me as a person".

England's all-time leading wicket-taker told his BBC podcast Tailenders last month that he had not decided whether to pursue a deal elsewhere, but Sky Sports News understands he is in negotiations with Surrey and could play at The Kia Oval, a venue where he claimed 50 wickets in 16 Tests between 2003 and 2023.

Anderson, who turns 45 in July of next year, could now get the chance to increase his haul of 1,193 first-class wickets and perhaps add more silverware to a glittering CV that includes four Ashes series victories and the 2010 T20 World Cup in the Caribbean.

Anderson let go by Lancashire despite prolific season

The Burnley-born bowler picked up 50 wickets at an average of 17.68 in County Championship Division Two for Lancashire in 2026.

His exit from Old Trafford came as the hierarchy, including new director of cricket Paul Farbrace, plot to build an attack for the future after a poor few seasons in red-ball cricket.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Anderson's final wicket for Lancashire back in September, against Kent in the County Championship

Anderson captained Lancashire last term as the county finished second bottom of the second tier, ahead of only Gloucestershire.

The seamer - who is poised to play in the Italia T10 for Napoli Knights later this month - was forced into international retirement by England in 2024.

Anderson took four wickets in his final Test, against West Indies at Lord's, to end with 704 wickets across 188 games in the longest format, at an average of 26.45.

He is the most prolific pace bowler in Test history, with only Sri Lankan off-spinner Muttiah Muralitharan (800) and Australian leg-spinner Shane Warne (708) taking more wickets.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Talking on the 'For the Love of Cricket' podcast, Stuart Broad branded Lancashire's decision not to renew Anderson's contract as 'disrespectful' (Credit: For the Love of Cricket)

Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast recently, Michael Atherton disagreed with the views of some that Lancashire had handled Anderson's release badly.

"When somebody like Farbrace comes in as director of cricket at Lancashire, or in England's case Rob Key, when they've decided to move on, how do you do that?" said Sky Sports pundit and former England captain Atherton.

"In both instances, Anderson was told face to face. It wasn't done behind his back.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain and Kumar Sangakkara reflect on Anderson's Lancashire exit

"Lancashire told him the rationale and then when the members meeting was held, I think Farbrace was abroad, but he dialled in and didn't hide behind the decision.

"He took full accountability for it, so I don't think you can say it's been handled badly."

Anderson made his Lancashire debut in List A cricket in 2001 before a maiden first-class appearance followed a year later.

Sports.title: Hamilton: Leclerc more aggressive racing me than he was Verstappen
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc races against him harder than he does other drivers on the Formula 1 grid.

Hamilton and Leclerc's clash on the opening lap of last Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix cost Ferrari a likely victory, and potential one-two, with Max Verstappen instead ultimately profiting to claim victory for Red Bull.

Speaking after the race, Hamilton said the team needed "serious talks" to discuss the way forward to avoid a repeat in future, while also calling Leclerc's approach to such battles into question.

Some pundits have since suggested that Leclerc appears to race Hamilton particularly aggressively, comparing what happened in Mexico to the first corner at the Singapore Grand Prix last month when the Monegasque went head to head for the lead with Verstappen.

Asked on Thursday ahead of this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix if he also saw it that way, Hamilton replied: "Yes.

"I see what you see. Singapore, he was fully [alongside Verstappen], wheel to wheel, fully on the inside for the lead at Turn 1 Singapore, and I think it was definitely different.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the start of the Singapore Grand Prix when Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc vied for the lead

"But, I mean, if you look at the team-mates, it was the same with Sebastian [Vettel], it was the same with Carlos [Sainz]."

Hamilton and Leclerc have largely appeared to enjoy a friendly relationship off track during their first two years as team-mates, but there have been flash points in racing combat this season with the pair often in close company.

They included a costly incident on the first lap of the team's home race at Monza in September, when Hamilton was forced onto the gravel as the two cars went side by side at the first chicane in a clash his team-mate subsequently apologised for.

On Leclerc, Hamilton said: "He's been here a long time, is it eight years?

"He is very much embedded within the team, and I knew that it would always be a challenge.

"I've always respected that when I've approached the team. I've really worked hard to build a good relationship with Charles and bridge the gap and make sure that we're harmonious and we work hard together.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater outlines what has been the aftermath at Ferrari after Hamilton and Leclerc's controversial opening-lap incident in Mexico City

"I've always tried to be respectful, and so naturally it's not so easy having someone like me come into a team because I'm very outspoken and I push and push and push, push for so many changes, and I'm going to be pushing for more.

"And as long as I'm here, that's how it's going to be. I'm here to win, and to be able to win, you have to work with everyone around you.

"We're all rowing, trying to get everyone to row at the same pace and also the same strength. And you have to push, and I have to push, I have to be pushed also to elevate. We all can always elevate and be better.

"And I truly believe that this team can be fighting for the championship next year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hamilton was furious after Leclerc overtook him on the opening lap while leaving the track but was only given a five-second penalty for the infringement

'I was frustrated and I'm still frustrated' - Hamilton eager for meeting

F1 is swiftly back in action in Sao Paulo this week to complete the season's latest triple-header.

However, with team boss Frederic Vasseur having briefly flown back to the team's headquarters in Italy, and Leclerc returning home to Monaco for the birth of his first child, after last Sunday's race in Mexico City, Hamilton said they had not yet had the chance for in-depth discussions about the way forward.

The Briton was therefore the only Ferrari driver present to speak to the media at Interlagos on Thursday, with Leclerc not arriving at the track until Friday.

Hamilton said that "naturally I was frustrated and I'm still frustrated" about what happened in Mexico and "so the conversations need to be had, so we will have those when the time permits".

On whether anything was yet in place for this weekend, Hamilton said: "There isn't a plan at the moment because we haven't had a time to sit down, all face to face because Fred's been back in Maranello, and Charles has been back in Monaco, but we will have a sit down.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hamilton criticised Leclerc over the lap-one incident that cost Ferrari a likely victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix

"I don't think everything's going to get squashed and sorted out in one meeting, but it is important what we build now will put us in the right position for next year.

"In some ways, I'm glad we've had that experience. Of course, I'd rather we had won and had a one-two but from that you can learn, and we can only really get stronger from that.

"In the background, we've got these incredible people that are working so hard in the background.

"We've been on a bit of the back foot on power this year, but the actual car has been phenomenal all the year, great reliability, and every day I go out on track, I'm always thinking of getting the absolute maximum for them.

"I don't always achieve it, and from that you learn. But I think with the years and experience, you understand the bigger picture when you're getting to work with such a large group of people, and that's, I would say, the privilege of the years that I've spent here and the teams that I've got to work in.

"I really do believe that next year we could win. We could be fighting for the world championship. That is the sole goal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Karun Chandhok says Ferrari should have made it clear how Hamilton and Leclerc were to race as they squandered the chance to win the Mexico City Grand Prix

"Right now, in the background, my focus is on continuing to hold on to the performance we've picked up in the last few races in terms of execution, and then working on next year's car. I obviously can't do anything about the engine except for to just push them, and they'll continue to push in the background. I believe they are.

"With the car, it's steering it, making sure we're steering it in the right direction, and making sure we arrive next year on the right foot.

"Then Fred's job is to make sure that we are all running in the same direction. Of course, we're going to race hard but fair, and making sure that we get the maximum and the best result for the team."

Asked how he would approach discussions with Vasseur and Leclerc, Hamilton said: "I think it's about communication. It's about understanding.

"I haven't really tried to think what the meeting will be like, how it's going to go. You never ever know.

"But what I will do is I'll make sure I'm always just authentically me, and I won't back down from taking responsibility for any part that I play and any decisions that I make for the team, and just continue to push."

'I'm not going to be silenced'

Hamilton said he would continue to push for the changes he believes will help Ferrari return to title-winning ways.

And while he denied claims some of his radio messages about the incident during the race in Mexico had been "calculated", he said he would not stop expressing his views openly and honestly.

"I don't really care how everyone feels about what I said," said Hamilton. "I wear my heart on my sleeve when I say how I feel in the moment.

"I think one thing that I would like to... I did see something that someone was saying, that it's calculated, the things that I'm saying. And I just want to combat that with the fact that when you're in the race, your heart rate is like 170, you're driving at 200 miles an hour, you don't have time to be calculating what you're saying and thinking what you're saying and what the media are going to write about.

"You don't think about that.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the most heated clashes between Ferrari team-mates Hamilton and Leclerc this season

"Usually, your frustration comes out towards the people in the team, particularly the bosses about decisions.

"And also, the stewards have always asked us to voice if there's an issue on track. For example, if you get held up, you get blocked, they ask you to voice it.

"An example is if you look in Mexico, one of the practice sessions, Hadjar backed off on the racing lines into Turn 1, I didn't say anything about it.

"If I had spoken and said, you know, like, throw my hands up, for example, they would have investigated and he would have had a penalty, because it was impeding.

"And so it is important to make sure you're open. Of course, there's sometimes you say things and maybe you might regret it afterwards. I don't. I've never apologised for being authentic and real.

"And I'm not going to be silenced. I've not been asked to not say anything, and that's just the way it is."

Sports.title: Russell questions frequency of 'atrocious luck' during 2026 F1 season
Sports.content:
George Russell has questioned the frequency of the "atrocious luck" he believes he has suffered during the 2026 Formula 1 season.

The Mercedes driver's team-mate Kimi Antonelli was crowned world champion at Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, with Russell falling to fourth in the standings behind Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.

Russell had qualified second on the grid but suffered the latest in a series of unfortunate moments that have plagued his campaign as a software glitch ruined his start, resulting in the loss of several places on the opening lap.

While Russell has accepted on multiple occasions that he has been outperformed by Antonelli, who he trails by 130 points, the Brit also appears to want answers from his team as to why he has been struck by so many technical issues.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch some of George Russell’s unlucky moments during the 2026 Formula 1 season.

"My focus had just been trying to win races, trying to improve performances, and Mexico it felt like a moment I could regain a bit of confidence and momentum," Russell said ahead of this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

"I qualified on the front row, basically on pole as I was so close with Lewis. Then just to have basically the whole race taken away from me because of a software glitch was incredibly tough to deal with when we've just had so many of these little issues in the whole season.

"This season hasn't meant to be. The performance hasn't been good enough. It's been atrocious luck. We need to question, is it luck because it's happened too often?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle believes Kimi Antonelli winning the world title could trigger an 'overdrive' for George Russell, or it's 'game over' for the Mercedes team-mate.

"We need to question, is there something we're overlooking because we can have bad luck once, twice, three times, four times? But it's been too many times.

"We're all having this internal conversation, and collectively as a team, we know we need to do better if we want to fight for next season."

Why Russell avoided media in Mexico

Russell was excused by Mercedes from fulfilling his media obligations following the race in Mexico, with team principal Toto Wolff explaining that he had found Russell "distraught" shortly after the chequered flag.

The 28-year-old, who started the year as clear title favourite before being unexpectedly outpaced by Antonelli, posted on social media congratulating the Italian and explaining his feelings following the race in Mexico.

Speaking to the media for the first time since, he offered a further explanation of why he had left the track swiftly on Sunday, which resulted in Mercedes being fined €5,000.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli became the youngest ever Formula One world champion after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

"I don't think I've ever had this many setbacks in my career," Russell said.

"I went through after the race with my engineer, the season, race by race, and we realised we had six races this season with no issues, and 14 races where we've had an issue of some sort.

"To give perspective, in the years gone by, we would maybe have two races where there's issues, or I think in 2023 we had four races where we had issues. This season we've had 14 races, and as I said, I've always sort of picked myself back up.

"As much as I love talking to you (the media) after the race, I didn't really fancy it on this occasion.

"So, I was like, 'I'm gonna just get out of here and go for a nice dinner and think about something other than the rubbish season we've had'."

'You need to look at yourself in the mirror'

Despite disappointment as his lack of fortune, Russell insists he also continues to focus on where he can improve his own performance.

"I think it's also important not to be naive and just blame luck on not being victorious," he added.

"I think you need to look at yourself hard in the mirror, think where you could have done a better job.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Karun Chandhok was full of praise for Kimi Antonelli as he became the youngest Formula One champion ever in just his second year on the grid.

"If these issues have been any contribution of lack of preparation on your side, I don't believe it is, but we need to go through that with my team. And things will come good again, I've got no doubts about it."

"I probably just feel a bit exhausted this season of constantly picking myself back up. When you get kicked to the ground, you pick yourself back up, and then you get kicked down again, you pick yourself back up.

"And I was hoping to do that maybe twice in the season, not every other weekend really. I think when you get to a point of this season, you're away from home for three weeks in a row and you have another race like what happened in Mexico where a chance of victory, a chance of the podium just disappears totally outside of your control, it's tough to deal with, you know. It's very tough to deal with."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On this day in 2022, George Russell secured his maiden Formula One win as the Mercedes driver triumphed at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Russell's maiden Grand Prix victory came at Interlagos in 2022, but he admits that the way the season has gone has left with him with limited expectations for the race.

"Brazil is a place that I love, I've got great memories of," Russell said.

"Do I come in with high expectations? Honestly, no, to be honest. But looking forward to next year for sure and we'll just continue to work on the things that I can control and pray the things outside of my control sort themselves out."

Sports.title: Alcaraz into Paris Masters quarter-finals after Berrettini withdraws
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz made it through to the quarter-finals at the Rolex Paris Masters without taking to the court after his scheduled opponent Matteo Berrettini withdrew from their third-round match.

The pair had been due to play on Thursday evening in the French capital but Berrettini suffered another injury setback, pulling out due to pain in his arm.

Alcaraz, who is chasing his fifth tour-level trophy of the season in the French capital, will face Taylor Fritz in the last eight at the ATP Masters 1000 event on Friday after he beat home favourite Arthur Fils 6-3 6-4.

Fritz must beat Alcaraz to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin, with the last spot currently held by Spaniard Rafael Jodar, who lost in the second round earlier this week in Paris.

Alcaraz will be bidding to reach the semi-finals on the indoor hard courts of Paris for the first time in six appearances.

An official social media announcement from the tournament read: "Matteo Berrettini has to withdraw from the Rolex Paris Masters. Wishing you a speedy recovery Matteo. Carlos Alcaraz is qualified for the quarter-finals."
