“It is to be hoped that this recent turn of events, clearing Mr Mendes of the allegation of rape, attracts the same level of media attention as the original reporting.”

The 36-year-old Mendes is Cape Verde’s most capped player, having made 103 appearances since his debut in 2010. He currently plays for RS Berkane in Morocco.

Sports.title: Fifa wants talks over restricting women’s Olympic football to under-23s
Sports.content:
Fifa wants talks with the International Olympic Committee over restricting the Olympic women’s football tournament to under-23s owing to concerns over fixture congestion and the workload of senior players.

The eligibility criteria for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles has been set, with qualification tournaments having begun in some regions, so no change can be made until Brisbane 2032 at the earliest, but sources at both organisations have said that they are open to dialogue.

Although no formal proposal has been made, Fifa is understood to be interested in examining the matter in talks with the IOC and other key stakeholders, such as the players and leading member associations whose national sides routinely qualify for the Games.

A move to bring in age restrictions would dramatically alter the nature of the event and require careful analysis, consultation and consideration through Fifa and IOC processes.

Such a change would be controversial and could provoke a backlash from leading international players because the Olympics has long been regarded as one of the highlights of the women’s calendar, with Emma Hayes’s United States team securing gold in Paris two years ago. The Olympic title has been contested eight times and the US have won five.

Women’s football also has a major commercial appeal for the IOC, particularly in markets such as the US, Europe and Australia, so it may resist Fifa’s overtures.

Women’s football was introduced to the Olympics at Atlanta in 1996, and as an amateur sport at that time never had eligibility requirements, in contrast to the men’s game.

After admitting football to the Olympic programme in 1908 the IOC did not permit professionals to take part until 1984 owing to Fifa’s insistence on maintaining the primacy of the World Cup, as well as the demands on players from a congested calendar. Under pressure from Fifa the IOC introduced an under-23 age restriction in 1992, although three overage players have also been allowed in each squad since 1996.

The huge growth and professionalisation of the women’s game over the past decade has created increased fixture congestion, with the 2028 calendar the most bloated yet.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Fifa is to a large extent culpable for this because the world governing body has chosen to launch the Women’s Club World Cup in an Olympic year, with the US to stage the 16-team competition between 5 and 30 January, six months before the Games.

The Women’s Club World Cup will cause major disruption to the European club season, with Arsenal and Chelsea or Manchester City likely to be absent from domestic competition for up to a month if they reach the latter stages, missing four Women’s Super League matches and the FA Cup fourth round. The importance of the sport to the IOC is shown by the fact that the women’s football tournament will be bigger than the men’s for the first time in LA, featuring 16 teams to 12, in a reversal of the numbers at Paris 2024.

Fifa and the IOC declined to comment.

Sports.title: Japan FA’s Kozo Tashima to stand against Infantino for Fifa presidency
Sports.content:
The Japan Football Association’s honorary president, Kozo Tashima, has announced his intention to stand against Gianni Infantino in March’s Fifa presidential election.

Tashima is the second challenger to declare in advance of the 18 November deadline after the former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega, although it remains unclear whether Vega has the backing of five of Fifa’s 211 member associations, which is required to take a place on the ballot in Rabat.

The widely respected Tashima will have no problem in securing the nominations and is understood to have acted with the blessing of Uefa, which has led the opposition to Infantino after his failed attempt to sell off a 20% stake in Fifa’s commercial rights this summer. The former Japan international has many allies in Europe and had talks with Uefa officials at last month’s Asian Football Confederation (AFC) congress in Tokyo.

“I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association,” Tashima told the Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon. “It’s not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What Fifa needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order ‌to make this appeal to the world.”

The declaration is an intriguing development after the AFC congress concluded with its president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, publicly endorsing Infantino in a major U-turn, having previously sided with Uefa and Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – in attempting to depose him.

Tashima could split the AFC vote and is certain to pick up votes from Europe and Concacaf, although other candidates could emerge.

Quick Guide How do I 

Uefa has spent months attempting to find a candidate to stand against Infantino, but may have concluded that a non-European challenger will fare better owing to widespread resentment about its perceived dominance of the sport.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Infantino has the backing of several leading countries in the AFC, such as Qatar and Saudi Arabia, and of Africa and South America, so is expected to canter towards the 106 votes required to be re-elected for a fourth term.

Sports.title: Premier League title winner with Chelsea tipped to succeed Alonso as manager
Sports.content:
Cesc Fabregas has been tipped to be the next Chelsea manager after Xabi Alonso.

The former Blues and Arsenal midfielder is winning plenty of fans for the job he is doing as boss of Italian side Como.



3 Fabregas has been linked to some of the top jobs around Europe Credit: Getty

They smashed Lens 9-1 in the Champions League on Wednesday night and look certain to progress to the knockout stage.

Como are also just two points off the top of Serie A and have lost just once all season.

Their rise in the last decade has been staggering, with the club playing in the fourth tier of Italian football as recently as 2019.



In 2022, Fabregas was revealed as a new Como player as the club sat in Serie B.

He invested a minority ownership share when he joined, partnering alongside former Barcelona teammate Thierry Henry with the exact percentage not being publicly disclosed.



Where could Fabregas go next?

Alonso was only hired as Chelsea manager this summer on a four-year contract.

But when has that stopped there being a swift change in the Stamford Bridge dugout?



The Blues are currently fourth in the Premier League, but some fears have been raised early on in his tenure.

This came to the fore in the 2-0 defeat to Tottenham at home with his team selection coming under fire.

Now 50-cap England women's striker Lianne Sanderson believes Fabregas could be the man to eventually replace him.

3 Fabregas' Como have scored 19 goals in four Champions League games Credit: Getty



Sanderson told talkSPORT’s Kick-Off: “There's a lot of conversation about Cesc Fabregas. When you're a good coach, good manager, he's going to be linked to different teams.

“My hot take was he'll be the next Chelsea manager after Xabi Alonso.”

Fabregas at Como

Italian journalist Daniele Fisichella joined the show and admitted he was surprised that Fabregas was still at the Italian club.

He said: “I think we are blessed in Serie A having had him for three seasons already. I thought last summer he would have gone because he received so many criticism in Italy for the way his Como team played.



“Como don't always win games, but they always play on the front foot. And Cesc made the mistake of telling the Italians, well, you are all about the results and you don't care how teams play.

“There's been a lot of criticism because people get a little bit twitchy about it, but then he had the last word last season.

3 Como are one of the most exciting teams to watch in Europe this season Credit: Getty

“I thought that after all this, so much criticism, he would have gone to the Premier League or maybe to La Liga but he actually stayed.



“But I am under no illusion. I think this next summer he moves to a bigger club with no disrespect to Como and so does Nico Paz, so does ‘Tasos’ Douvikas and probably Lucas da Cunha, who's already played for the French team.

“Cesc is the real deal. He's got a stronger playing philosophy, but he's not a fundamentalist. I think he's taken a leaf out of some of the Italian managers' books as well.

“This season Como managed games better than last season. Sometimes they're even happy to defend in a low block.

"He's not just attack, attack. He's also a little bit of a pragmatist.”



Fabregas' budding managerial career follows his stellar playing days which saw him play for elite sides of world football.

The Spaniard controversially moved to Chelsea from Barcelona having spent the first eight years of his career at Arsenal.

But Fabregas enjoyed huge success at Stamford Bridge as he won five trophies, including two Premier League titles.

As well as winning a plethora of trophies at club level, Fabregas was part of the all-star Spain squad that won Euro 2008 and 2012 as well as the 2010 World Cup.

Sports.title: $384bn Jeff Bezos has two options to take full ownership of Liverpool from FSG
Sports.content:
$384bn Jeff Bezos has two options to take full ownership of Liverpool from FSG

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ consortium has two options to increase its stake to take control of Liverpool, according to reports.

Bezos’ K5 Global sports fund is the largest investor in 1892 Holdings, who bought a 38 per cent stake in the club from Fenway Sports Group (FSG) in August.

3 Bezos is the largest investor in 1892 Holdings Credit: AFP

The Amazon mogul is said to be worth in the region of $384billion and is the second richest person in the world.

1892 Holdings is led by Amit Bhatia, who was an owner and director of QPR for 19 years.

The Athletic report that it can increase its stake in Liverpool once it has been ratified as a part-owner by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR).

The report adds it can increase to around 69 per cent, or potentially even complete a 100 per cent buyout, as part of the agreement.

The group could end up with full control of Liverpool in as little as 12 months.

1892 Holdings’ initial investment in Liverpool is worth more than £2billion.

Will FSG leave Liverpool?

All indications are that FSG will cede full control of the club, which may lead to a full exit in due course.

FSG, then New England Sports Ventures, bought Liverpool from the much maligned American owners Tom Hicks and George Gillett for £300m in 2010.

Since then, the Anfield club has been restored to one of the powerhouses in English football.

They won the Champions League, the sixth European crown in their history, and have twice been Premier League champions.

3 John W. Henry is the principal owner of Liverpool Credit: Getty

FSG also has stakes in the Boston Red Sox, the Pittsburgh Penguins and RFK Racing.

It also is said to be considering investment in the Cadillac Formula One team.

Bhatia on Liverpool

Speaking when Bhatia’s 1892 Holdings joined the ownership group of Liverpool, he said: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners.

“We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.

“I’m just the biggest admirer of everything that is associated with this football club, whether it’s the history and the culture, the supporters, the journey of this club, the owners in FSG, the management team at Liverpool.

“There’s just so much to admire, so much to frankly be in awe of.

3 Liverpool have won two Premier League titles under FSG Credit: AFP

"And so to have the opportunity at this point in time, to hopefully potentially – I want to just be very clear, subject to all kinds of regulatory approvals that we’re going through the process [of] now – but the simple fact that we’ve been potentially welcomed in by FSG to be part of such an incredible football club, a historic football club, an iconic football club like Liverpool, frankly it’s the stuff of dreams. And it is the greatest honour I think that anybody can have.”

Sports.title: Pierre Sage gives cryptic reply as £38.5m player dropped from Crystal Palace squad completely
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage gives cryptic reply as £38.5m player dropped from Crystal Palace squad completely

Pierre Sage was tight-lipped on his decision to omit Axel Disasi from the Crystal Palace squad against Hoffenheim.

The centre-back was not part of the matchday selection for their 1-1 draw in the Europa League on Thursday night.



2 Disasi was left out of the matchday squad for Palace against Hoffenheim having missed a team meeting Credit: Getty

Disasi, who is on loan from Premier League rivals Chelsea, played in all three of their previous European fixtures.

Speaking to TNT Sports before the match, Sage said: "It's a decision I took this afternoon."

When asked if there was any particular reason for the decision, the Palace manager simply said: "No, thank you."



Disasi's absence was also raised in his post-match press conference, where Sage remained hush.

"The reason why he isn't playing was an internal decision. I don't want to speak on it anymore," Sage said.



However, Sage confirmed to TNT that Disasi, who joined Chelsea from Monaco in a £38.5m deal, is available for Palace this Sunday when they host Liverpool.

Why was Disasi not in the Palace squad?

News of Disasi not being able to feature against Hoffenheim came as a surprise to the Palace faithful.



However, talkSPORT understands that the 28-year-old was dropped because he was late for a team meeting.

Disasi has made nine appearances for Palace this season, but missed three in the Premier League due to his red card suspension.

Palace do not have a buy option or obligation for the Frenchman, a £38.5million signing for Chelsea from AS Monaco in 2023.

2 Sage was asked about Disasi's absence by the media, but chose not to say too much on the matter Credit: Getty



Palace leave it late against Hoffenheim

With one win from six in all competitions prior to Thursday evening's clash, Palace needed to provide a winning response.

However, they fell behind inside seven minutes at Selhurst Park when Alexander Prass netted for the German visitors.

Dean Henderson appeared to save his strong effort, but the ball ended up slipping underneath him and trickle over the line.

Adam Wharton was sent off for a second yellow card on 77 minutes to leave Palace with a one-man disadvantage.



They managed to rescue a point in stoppage time as Daichi Kamada rolled the ball through the legs of the goalkeeper.

Palace have five points from four games in the Europa League league phase and currently sit in the play-off spots.

Sports.title: Argentina set to make symbolic Lionel Messi gesture in first game since retirement
Sports.content:
Argentina set to make symbolic Lionel Messi gesture in first game since retirement

Argentina will not hand out Lionel Messi's iconic No.10 shirt for the upcoming international break.

La Albiceleste will begin the post-Messi era in November following his retirement from the national team.

3 Messi was emotional as he waved goodbye to Argentina Credit: AFP

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner was given a monumental send-off in a 208th and final appearance in October.

He scored 126 goals and won the World Cup in his illustrious international career.

The 39-year-old scored in a 3-0 win over Benin in front of a packed out crowd in Buenos Aires.

But a report from Tyc Sports in Argentina says no player will wear his No.10 shirt in their upcoming games.

Lionel Scaloni's side will face Uruguay and Costa Rica in two friendlies later in November.

Argentina will symbolically omit a No.10 from their squad list as they decide on who to give it to long term.

One of their major contenders is Como's Nico Paz, with the 22-year-old lighting up Serie A and the Champions League this season.

Premier League stars Enzo Fernandez and Alexis Mac Allister are also options.

Can Argentina retire Messi's number?

The short answer is no and that is because of FIFA rules.

For major competitions, such as the World Cup, teams are required to register players in consecutive numbers.

3 After 208 games and 126 goals, Lionel Messi's Argentina career is over Credit: AFP

This means there can be no numerical gaps in the numbering.

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) have already attempted to do it previously.

They tried to retire the No.10 jersey following the international retirement of Diego Maradona ahead of the 2002 World Cup.

However, this was blocked by FIFA.

The same rules do not apply to international friendlies, meaning Argentina can wait before naming their official heir to Messi.

Messi's Argentina retirement

Messi scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina including eight goals at this summer's World Cup.

3 Messi's No.10 will not be handed out just yet Credit: Getty

In a message posted on his Instagram account, Messi said: "After the time that has passed since the final, and after giving it a lot of thought, I want to let everyone know that I am retiring from the national team.

"It was a decision that hurt — and still hurts deep down — but I understand that the time has come.

"I swear to you that I always gave it my all — not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too; I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football.

"Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, have loved, and will always love being part of the national team.

"I’ve given everything I had; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some great young players coming up who deserve to be here.

"Thank you for all the affection over these past 20 years. I will miss hearing you from the pitch so much. Now I’ll be just one of you, cheering and supporting from the outside (through the good times and the bad — especially the bad).

"Thank you to my family for always being there, for accompanying me on this journey — so beautiful, yet so difficult.

"Thank you to every coach, teammate, and official I’ve shared this path with. I take with me unforgettable memories and moments.

"I leave with the peace of mind and pride of having given you—alongside my teammates — moments we once only dreamed of. It was an incredible experience to live this with you all. I love you!

"Thank you, God, for making me Argentine. Let's go, Argentina!

"*I wrote these words on July 21, two days after the final. Today, after what happened with my dad, I am even more convinced than before."

Sports.title: Blackburn star chose GCSEs over Chelsea and is reaping rewards of Fabian Hurzeler coaching
Sports.content:
"It's up to us to be ready for any opportunity that comes."

Without any context, Dapo Afolayan could be referring to any point of his unique journey from the ninth tier to the Championship - with stints in the Bundesliga and Loughborough University in between.

9 Despite his impressive individual stats, Afolayan claimed his 'biggest thing is about helping Blackburn become a winning team' Credit: Getty

As it is, the Blackburn Rovers star is discussing the dramatic turnaround in his own situation at Ewood Park to talkSPORT.com.

Afolayan started just one game for the club last term after signing in January as they finished 20th in the Championship.

However, the return of Tony Mowbray as manager in June after Michael O'Neill left Blackburn have seen his fortunes transformed.

Afolayan has started all 14 league games for Rovers this season, and rewarded the 62-year-old's faith with four goals and two assists.

"The gaffer's great here, because he's really honest," Blackburn's No.21 told talkSPORT. "He loves football. He's a passionate man.

"I think if you sit down with him, you'll hear his passion, you'll feel his emotion - we're quite similar in that way.

"I think for me, I went over to Germany, and I improved so much as a player. I was obviously playing at a high level, playing in the Bundesliga there, was something that was a dream for me.

"And, to come back here, for me, it was always just a matter of being able to play and have the opportunity to play.

"The gaffer's given me that, and I always see it as players: It's up to us to be ready for any opportunity that comes, and when the opportunities do come, to take it.

"I feel like I've tried to do that this year, and I will keep trying to do that if I'm picked to play.

9 Mowbray recently challenged 'intelligent' Afolayan to keep improving

"The gaffer's emotion and the way he talks about the game and the feeling I'm similar to him, so you want to repay him and repay that faith that he's had in you.

"It's been really good this year, the confidence that he gives me to go out and to perform and to use my strengths."

Mowbray's belief in Afolayan's ability will always be second to the one shown by the Harrow-born winger in himself.

The EFL star who rejected Chelsea for GCSE's

When he was 14 years old, an age when most young players are terrified of losing an elite academy spot, the former Chelsea starlet left the Blues youth set-up to continue his education.

With no guarantee that a pathway back to the promised land would be achievable, Afolayan developed an emotional resilience beyond his years.

"For me, it was good to have that lesson early on in my life, so when I did encounter any other setbacks in my footballing career, or life for that matter, I was able to push through them, and I knew how to deal with them," Afolayan continued.

9 Afolayan has started all 14 Championship games for Blackburn this season Credit: Getty

"Obviously, experiencing that stuff at an early age, as you say, it's difficult for a lot of young lads.

"When you're young, you want to play at the top of the academies in the country - You want to play for the best clubs.

"When you're at one, then leaving that, it's a difficult period.

"I've seen some lads not recover from that, really.

"I think at an early age, it was really good for me to learn that and it obviously helped me in good stead for the rest of my career."

Within 24 months of his decision, Afolayan's family relocated to Canada, where he had the opportunity to join MLS side Toronto FC.

9 Afolayan speaking to talkSPORT about a potential first call-up for Nigeria

After training with the likes of Jermain Defoe, Jozy Altidore and Sebastian Giovinco, he returned to the UK as he came of age.

Afolayan resurfaced in the National League with Solihull Moors while he also pursued a degree in civil engineering at Loughborough.

His form for the West Midlands side saw him plucked from the bottom of the fifth tier by then-Premier League giants, West Ham.

He scored on his debut for the Hammers under David Moyes in a 4-0 FA Cup fourth-round win over Doncaster in January 2021 before joining Bolton; first on loan and then on a permanent deal.

Afolayan made himself a hero that May when he opened his account for Wanderers in a final-day victory away to Crawley Town that earned Ian Evatt’s side promotion from League Two.

The following campaign, he won the club’s Player of the Year award after finishing as top scorer with 14 goals.

9 Afolayan won Bolton’s Player of the Year award in the 2021/22 campaign before a change in system left him in limbo Credit: Getty

Six months later, Afolayan was convinced by now-Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler to join St Pauli in the Bundesliga 2.

Hurzeler helped me learn football in a different way

The German was just 29 - the same age Afolayan is now - when he convinced the one-cap England C star to move to Hamburg.

"It's funny you say that... I've never actually thought of it like that. It's mental. I was 25 when I was leaving Bolton at the time," Afolayan said.

"I'd just flown over to Hamburg to see the facilities and to see the stadium, to meet the people there. Then, obviously, I had to meet the manager because he had the job, but he hadn't taken a game yet.

"He'd only had a few winter camp training games and stuff, which I'd watched. But yeah, the second I walked into the room with him, he basically told me everywhere that I could improve.

"Exactly how he wanted me to fit into his system. He had a full presentation on me, watching clips of Bolton, saying, 'You're good at this, but you can be so much better here and so much better.'

9 Hurzeler guided St Pauli back to the Bundesliga for the first time since 2011 Credit: Getty

9 Afolayan celebrated scoring twice and assisting another in the victory against VFL Osnabruck that confirmed Bundesliga status Credit: Getty

"He really sounded like he wanted to improve me and wanted to make me a better player.

"He was teaching me things that I'd never really thought about.

"As quite a thinker about the game, someone who likes to think football and tactically, and try and understand the game, obviously having him at that point in my career was the best thing that had happened to me.

"He helped me learn football in a different way, view things in a different way, and the mentality of how important the big focus is on training and how details are so important, and how training days are so important not to waste away and to make sure you're trying to be the best player every day.

"No matter whether you're 21 or a young kid coming through, or you're 30, and you're in your 30s, it's still just as important.

"After my meeting with him, I pretty much called my family and said I was going to go out there."

Afolayan's arrival in January 2023 coincided with St Pauli surging away from a potential relegation battle by winning ten successive matches.

That momentum continued into the next campaign, when Afolayan contributed nine goals in 31 games to help secure promotion.

9 Fans streamed on the pitch to mob Afolayan and his teammates after St Pauli confirmed their promotion Credit: Getty

Hurzeler left for Brighton that summer, with his former player following him back to England this year, thanks in part to the work of Blackburn's head of football operations, Rudy Gestede.

Now his career comes full circle when Rovers, who are just six points adrift of the playoffs, take on his former club West Ham - and their new manager Scott Parker - on Saturday.

'It means something playing West Ham'

"I had a great time at the club, and I really enjoyed my years there," Afolayan told talkSPORT. "It really helped me on my journey.

"Even though I didn't play many games, a lot of the people at the club taught me what it is to be a professional footballer, and to come in every game and to be honest and to work hard.

"I've got lots of friends who are back at the club still; it will be nice to see them and stuff. As the game comes, it's going to be pretty simple to block it out and focus on what we need to do.

"I think the game itself is going to be a great game because I think it's two teams that both want to play in the right way.

9 Afolayan will look to haunt his former club West Ham in a pivotal clash for his current side Credit: Getty

"It's a really good test for us because we obviously want to compete at the top end of the division.

"I think it's a good opportunity for us to go out and express ourselves and to show people what we're really about."

If anyone knows all about making the most of an opportunity when the time comes, it's Afolayan...

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel weighs up Cole Palmer England recall after bemoaning ‘missed opportunities’
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel is considering naming Cole Palmer in his upcoming England squad.

Palmer withdrew from the Three Lions squad in September with a minor muscle injury.



3 Cole Palmer has played 14 times for England since making his debut in 2023 Credit: Getty

This led to some question marks over his commitment to the national team.

The 24-year-old was controversially left out of Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad and has missed several international camps in recent times.

Tuchel had said Palmer had a point to prove and needed ‘to step up’ to ‘keep his shirt and justify the nomination’.



talkSPORT understands, as first reported by the Daily Telegraph, that Tuchel has made medical checks on the Chelsea star.

This is a usual process and by no means a guarantee that he will be included when Tuchel names his England squad on Friday at 10am.



What did Tuchel say on Palmer?

Despite five players withdrawing from the England squad, Palmer took the most flak.

The initial reason for the decision being stated as ‘load management’, but later detailed as a minor muscle issue.



"My understanding is that he is playing with discomfort and pain, and he cannot compete at the highest level with discomfort and pain. So he withdrew and informed us, and Chelsea informed us," Tuchel said in September.

"For sure. It is a missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I don't blame him for it. It is just a fact.

"He misses way too many camps with injuries, and I only want to rely on what I witness and see within in my team, and for that you have to be in camp.

3 Tuchel is set to name his England squad on Friday Credit: Getty



"And if you're not in camp, there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it when you are actually on the pitch with me. So yes, it is a missed opportunity."

Palmer's England commitment

talkSPORT's live football anchor Adrian Durham was not impressed with Palmer's withdrawal in September.

Durham raised question marks about whether the Chelsea star actually wants to put on a Three Lions shirt.

"I'm questioning his commitment to England," Durham said. "Does he really want to play for England? If you don't, tell the world you don't want to play for England.



"Because just picking and choosing when you want to play for England is actually disrupting other number 10s like [Nottingham Forest's] Morgan Gibbs-White, like [Fulham's] Josh King, who might want to play for England.

"We're all agreed Cole Palmer is a really good footballer. But, other than that goal in the Euro final, I've not really seen, on a consistent basis, any kind of quality or commitment from him.

3 Palmer has three goals and three assists in the Premier League this season Credit: Getty

"So let's have it from Cole Palmer. Do you want to play for England or do you not want to play for England?"



The England squad for their upcoming Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain will be announced at 10am on Friday.

England face Croatia at Wembley next Thursday before facing the world champions at the Metropolitano in Madrid with the Three Lions currently second in the group, three points behind leaders Spain.

Sports.title: Newcastle player Amar Dedic has bow and arrows seized by police after six-car chase
Sports.content:
Newcastle player Amar Dedic has bow and arrows seized by police after six-car chase

Newcastle defender Amar Dedic had six police cars on his tail after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrow in dramatic scenes in Northumberland.

The £30million Bosnia-Herzegovina international and a friend sparked alarm when seen holding the weapon near a reservoir in the countryside outside of Newcastle.

2 Dedic joined Newcastle from Benfica in the summer Credit: Getty

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the area in Harlow Hill with the Daily Mail reporting some were armed response units.

Dedic and his companion were intercepted round seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate and were subsequently questioned by officers.

The car was searched and the police seized the bow and arrows.

But in a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while the 24-year-old was being questioned. It's understood Gillsepie and Dummett were in the area by chance and offered assistance.

And after speaking to the two men, officers were satisfied Dedic and his friend were no threat to the public with the police believing the equipment was intended for recreational use.

Enquiries remain ongoing over the incident that happened on Wednesday with it being reported that Dedic and his friend fired arrows while in the countryside.

It remains unclear what they were firing at, however, hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in the UK.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: "Shortly after 1:55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

"Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows.

"At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing."

2 Dedic is not expected to be subject to any disciplinary action from Newcastle Credit: Getty

The Daily Mail's report adds that Dedic is not expected to face any disciplinary action from Newcastle as it's felt the player was naive to believe he was allowed to walk around the countryside with the weapon.

Amar Dedic's career at a glance

Full-back Dedic joined Newcastle from Benfica in a £30m deal in the summer.

The 24-year-old began his career in 2019 with Austrian outfit Red Bull Salzburg, claiming one Austrian Bundesliga winners' medal with them.

After six years at Salzburg, Dedic earned a move to Benfica, winning the Portuguese Super Cup on his debut.

He was only with the Lisbon-based side for a year before completing his move to Tyneside in the summer transfer window.

Dedic has settled in well at Newcastle having started six of their eight Premier League games this season, getting assists in wins over Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

The player has 31 caps for Bosnia's national team and played in three of their four matches at the World Cup earlier this year.

Sports.title: Conference League match stopped for eight minutes immediately after kick-off
Sports.content:
Conference League match stopped for eight minutes immediately after kick-off

Hearts' match against Thun was delayed by eight minutes as smoke billowed across the pitch.

The Conference League match in Switzerland had kicked-off, only for the home fans to let off a deluge of pyrotechnics.

2 The pitch was barely visible in Switzerland

The Hearts penalty area was engulfed in smoke and the referee called a temporary halt to proceedings.

Such was the thickness of the wave of smoke, it took eight minutes for it clear.

A Hearts statement on social media read: "Well, we did kick-off, but the game was almost immediately stopped, due to smoke from pyrotechnic devices let off in the home end.

"Should be back underway in the next minute or so."

Around 2,500 Hearts fans have travelled to Switzerland for the match.

A minute silence was held in honour of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who died in a Spanish second tier match this week.

Once play did resume, the only fireworks on the pitch were in the Hearts box.

Two dreadful errors saw Thun take a two-goal lead going into the half-time break.

Nine minutes were added on in total at the end of the first 45.

Thun added a third early in the second half before Stuart Findlay grabbed a consolation eight minutes from time.

Hearts verdict

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken outlined how he saw the game would play out when speaking ahead of the match.

2 Vrancken saw his Hearts side go down 2-0 in the first half Credit: Getty

“They have a good team, they have a lot of energy, they have a lot of intensity.

“They have a direct player who's going fast forward a lot of moments, with a lot of energy, good quality players also in front.

“We have to be spot on, we have to be on our level and to make the result. And the result is to try to get a win here.

“I'm confident in the players that they are mentally ready to play the game, because they showed it already a few times this season that they can bounce back and in performance.

“Concern (about the pitch)? No. We played Falkirk. I think it's similar with Falkirk. So we have to cope with it.

“We don't have to look for excuses in this way. We can now train on it and go full tomorrow.

“I'm not thinking about injuries. I'm just thinking about winning the game."

Sports.title: Aussie cricket star Chris Lynn's secret cocaine ban after drug binge following quarter-final victory
Sports.content:
Aussie cricket star Chris Lynn's secret cocaine ban after drug binge following quarter-final victory

Australian cricket star Chris Lynn served a one-month cocaine ban that has only now become public, after failing a drug test on the day he helped Northamptonshire win England's T20 Blast title.

The 36-year-old admitted to using cocaine over several hours following his side's quarter-final victory in July, with his suspension subsequently reduced after he completed a substance-abuse treatment program.

Lynn served the ban from July 31 to August 30. The sanction emerged publicly on Friday, months after he had completed it and amid reports linking him with a Big Bash League move to the Melbourne Renegades.

The former Australian international provided a urine sample during T20 Blast Finals Day at Edgbaston on July 18.

He scored 39 in the semi-final and four in the final as Northamptonshire claimed the trophy for the third time.

Analysis at a World Anti-Doping Agency-accredited laboratory in France detected benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

Chris Lynn served a one-month cocaine ban that only became public months after his suspension ended

The Australian batter, pictured with partner Karlie, tested positive after helping Northamptonshire win the T20 Blast title on July 18

Lynn's proposed three-month suspension was reduced to one month after he completed a substance-abuse treatment program

Lynn subsequently acknowledged taking the drug on July 15 and into the early hours of July 16, several days before the test.

Earlier on July 15, he had retired hurt during Northamptonshire's quarter-final win over Gloucestershire after being struck on the foot by a low full toss from Duan Jansen.

England's Cricket Regulator accepted evidence that Lynn's cocaine use took place out of competition and was unrelated to sporting performance.

After the Blast, Lynn travelled to Sri Lanka for the Lanka Premier League, making one appearance for Galle Gallants before being ruled out with a leg injury on July 29.

Two days later, the regulator notified him of his positive test and imposed a provisional suspension.

Lynn responded on August 20, admitting the cocaine use and supplying evidence about when it had occurred.

The regulator initially pursued two charges under the England and Wales Cricket Board's anti-doping rules.

One was subsequently dropped because the concentration detected in his sample fell below the minimum threshold required for that charge.

The former Australian international served his suspension from July 31 to August 30

Lynn, pictured with footy star Reagan Campbell-Gillard, accepted the sanction after the regulator dropped one of the two original anti-doping charges

The remaining breach carried a proposed three-month suspension. That was reduced to one month after Lynn provided confirmation he had completed a substance-abuse treatment program.

His suspension was deemed completed on August 30, with formal notice of the charges following on September 23. Lynn accepted the sanction.

Cocaine is prohibited in competition under the anti-doping rules and is also classified as a substance of abuse.

The regulator's acceptance that Lynn used it outside competition, without a connection to sporting performance, was central to the penalty imposed.

Lynn has not played professional cricket since his brief stint in Sri Lanka.

His playing future is now back in the spotlight after he reportedly agreed to join the Melbourne Renegades for the upcoming BBL season. The signing has not been officially announced.

One of Australia's most recognisable T20 power hitters, Lynn played four one-day internationals and 18 T20 internationals for his country, with his most recent Australian appearance coming in 2018.

Sports.title: How James McAtee became Nottingham Forest's tough-tackling 'quarterback': The heart-to-heart with Oliver Glasner, summer boot camp and an Adam Wharton blueprint
Sports.content:
Quarterback is not a word necessarily associated with somebody once dubbed the 'Salford Silva' but then James McAtee has changed immeasurably since leaving Manchester City 15 months ago. That moniker was handed down when the diminutive midfielder was much younger, effortlessly gliding through City’s academy, excelling in tight spaces, never losing possession. Scoring heaps, too. That is who Nottingham Forest thought they were purchasing for £30million in August 2025, a statement signing to play high up the pitch. And yet as last season unravelled, and the sackings piled up – four managers in all – McAtee mustered only two Premier League starts throughout the campaign. He was given four minutes across almost four months at one stage and was an unused substitute in both encounters with City. That will change on Saturday, McAtee one of the first names on the Forest team sheet, owing much to one conversation with Oliver Glasner that changed the course of his career at the City Ground. So to the quarterback. The most important position in a Glasner team. That was how the Austrian envisioned McAtee’s evolution, the path to regular matches, and within months he has become the heartbeat of a team that is deserving of significantly more points than the six they have amassed so far. Those who oversaw McAtee's development at City are not shocked by the calm use of possession and incisive passes through the lines yet did not predict him flying into challenges and blocks, only two midfielders in the division having completed more tackles than his 14 so far. He has turned into a terrier. James McAtee in his 'quarterback' role for Nottingham Forest, where he has become the heartbeat of the team At Manchester City he was dubbed the 'Salford Silva' and was more effective higher up the pitch

Your browser does not support iframes.

This has been a product of a full summer’s work on a rented pitch in Stockport, close to the family home. Forest's sporting director George Syrianos had made it clear that McAtee needed to become more physically robust and, after a five-day holiday, he spent a regimented two-and-a-half hours a day training, including 60-minute weight sessions in the afternoons. When he arrived back for pre-season, McAtee had put on just over 2.5kg of muscle and lost 1kg of fat. He turned up a new man and that served to rubber stamp Glasner’s idea of permanently moving him into the engine room. The Forest boss spoke to the 24-year-old about how he had developed Adam Wharton at Crystal Palace into an England international and that the plan here would be exactly the same. This month’s Nations League ties will come too soon for that yet there are those within the FA who are confirmed admirers of McAtee and expect him to earn future caps. That he skippered the Under 21s to last year’s European Championship title, was player of the match in the final against Germany and named in the team of the tournament holds real weight inside St George’s Park. Aesthetically, he is the picture of what the FA have wanted to create over the past decade: a nimble yet tough midfielder who guards the football with his life and wriggles out of trouble without fuss. And whose game understanding means he knows when to force the issue – McAtee has created the same number of chances as Rayan Cherki (18) this season. The only central midfielders to have attempted more passes into the box than McAtee’s 60 are Bruno Fernandes, Granit Xhaka and Pascal Gross. City will be some test on Saturday evening and there is plenty for him to prove, having worked under Enzo Maresca with the club’s Under 21s and a lingering feeling of what might have been at the Etihad Stadium. As for England, they are blessed with real quality coming through in central midfield, with Alex Scott at Bournemouth leading the charge to unsettle the axis of Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice. Scott could return from a thigh injury sustained during the last international break this weekend, a fitness problem that enraged his club. McAtee skippered the England Under 21s to last year’s European Championship title, was player of the match in the final against Germany and named in the team of the tournament The 24-year-old bulked up over the summer and is now able to mix it in the Forest engine room Beyond those three it is very much up for grabs. James Garner is a recent Thomas Tuchel favourite, largely owing to his work ethic, with Wharton overlooked for the World Cup. The man picked ahead of all those, Manchester United’s Kobbie Mainoo, was not afforded a kick in the United States. McAtee’s defensive and offensive stats this season outstrip the others in that chasing pack. They all know that there is definitely a claim to stake for somebody. It’s Rice, Anderson, Scott and another at this point. Whether McAtee can kick on beyond nine consecutive Premier League starts is up to him. Crucially, he is in control of his own destiny more than ever before. At City, he patiently waited for chances that barely came. In his debut year at Forest, players considered safer bets jumped the queue as the club battled relegation. But under Glasner, he has been harnessed, given the assurances that one sub-par performance does not mean a spell on the bench. McAtee has always been somebody who needs love to flourish and has finally found some.

Sports.title: 'Winning at the Emirates is very hard... but we were a team of warriors': Hull City hero GEOVANNI on his iconic goal against Arsenal, why it very nearly never happened and why the Tigers 'will always be in my heart'
Sports.content:
The greatest moment in Hull City's Premier League history began with Geovanni trying to go home.

'I was ill all night, I barely slept at all,' says Geovanni, who was gripped by a fever and thumping headache less than 24 hours before he was due to walk out at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium in September 2008. The Brazilian rang his wife from the team hotel to tell her he was coming home and planned to have someone pick him up.

Thankfully, his wife Roberta would not hear of it.

'God really used her that day,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'She said: "Geovanni, stay there, God will honour you. Hang on and tomorrow try to get a bit of sleep."'

When Hull staff came to his room the next morning, he asked to be left to sleep. He dosed up on medicine and went for lunch, but sat out the light pre-match training session with his temperature touching 38 degrees Celsius.

'And then I got to that game, which was so spectacular,' he says, 'and I was able to score and help Hull beat Arsenal.'

Geovanni unleashes a spectacular equaliser for Hull at the Emirates Stadium back in September 2008

The goal inspired a famous comeback win for the Tigers, who became only the second team to win away at Arsenal

It was Hull's first league meeting with Arsenal for 93 years, in the first top-flight season of the club's then 104-year history.

Arsene Wenger's side had started the day top of the table and Paul McShane's own goal put Arsenal ahead after 51 minutes. Most expected the floodgates to open.

But 11 minutes later up stepped Hull's brilliant Brazilian, a marquee signing from Manchester City in the summer of 2008 after the Tigers' unexpected promotion.

Geovanni cut inside Theo Walcott and sent a 25-yard rocket into Manuel Almunia's top corner. Daniel Cousin headed in a historic winner four minutes later and Hull became only the second side to beat Arsenal at the Emirates.

'Beating Arsenal at the Emirates is very hard, and we pulled it off,' says Geovanni, now 46, speaking from his home in Brazil. 'That was a team of warriors, great players, and we had a really good friendship. And that day we walked away with a great win.'

On Saturday, Hull return to the Emirates to face the champions and league leaders. The Tigers are 11th after nine games. It is a strong start that few predicted.

'Hull have to give 100 per cent, the maximum, be switched on the whole time,' says Geovanni. 'It's difficult, but it's not impossible, because Hull really did beat Arsenal.'

Eight days after the Emirates match, Geovanni did it again. A stunning 30-yard free-kick at White Hart Lane nestled into the top corner past his friend and compatriot Heurelho Gomes.

'We beat Tottenham with Gareth Bale, Luka Modric, all those players,' he says. 'For me, those two are top-drawer. They're two great players who left a mark on me.'

The win moved Hull into third and by the end of October they were level on points at the top. 'London 0 Hull 2' read the headline in the local paper, in reference to Hull band The Housemartins' 1986 album London 0 Hull 4, as the city revelled in its newfound fame.

Geovanni (centre) was part of another iconic Premier League moment, when Phil Brown gave his team a public dressing down at half-time of a loss at Manchester City

The Brazilian returned to Hull's MKM Stadium last year and received a hero's welcome

Geovanni took centre stage. Arriving on a free that summer after being released by Manchester City, he credits manager Phil Brown and assistant Brian Horton for giving him a second chance in the Premier League.

'They were very special people in allowing me to stay in England, which was my dream,' he says. 'And I learned a lot from both of them. Brian was a very experienced coach, he played for Hull, he managed there, so the affection and respect are huge. Whenever I can talk about them, I do.

'In the first year, Hull surprised a lot of people precisely because of the way we played. Sometimes we'd start in a 4-3-1-2, I played as the No10 behind two strikers. And if we were struggling to mark, I'd drop in to close down the left flank and we'd go back to a 4-4-2.'

The dressing room did the rest. Richard Garcia, an Australian winger with Uruguayan parents, helped translate team talks from English into Spanish and captain Ian Ashbee, Nicky Barmby and Bernard Mendy all made Geovanni feel welcome. 'I'm really happy about the friendships I made in that dressing room,' he says.

Geovanni was part of another of the Premier League's most iconic moments, when he and his team-mates received a public dressing down from his manager on the pitch at half-time of a 5-1 loss to Manchester City on Boxing Day 2008. Eleven months later, Jimmy Bullard scored a penalty before recreating the telling off in celebration.

'It was good for breaking the ice,' says Geovanni. 'From that day on the atmosphere got better too, because we can all make mistakes. The most important thing is to admit the mistake and move on.'

Geovanni's finest moment for Manchester City, with whom he spent one season after stints with Barcelona, Benfica and Cruzeiro, came in the Manchester derby, where he was called into the side by manager Sven-Goran Eriksson because Stephen Ireland was ill.

'He called me over and said, "Geovanni, this game... are you ready?". That was the best news I'd had all day, knowing I was going to start.' The day did, in fact, get better. Geovanni scored the only goal in a 1-0 victory.

Geovanni smashes home a winner for City in the Manchester derby, a year before his move to Hull

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages

He struck again against United in November 2008, in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages, while he also scored in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford in 2008.

'A player has to turn up in the big games,' he says. 'United were a machine back then: Giggs, Paul Scholes, Gary Neville, Anderson, Ronaldo, Rooney.'

Geovanni's greatest regret, though, remains that he didn't heed the advice of Barca boss Louis van Gaal, who wanted to turn the wannabe striker into a wing-back.

He reflects: 'If I could go back in time, I'd listen to what Van Gaal said, because it would have been easier for me to fight for a place at wing-back than as a striker, where there were great players: Javier Saviola, Rivaldo, Patrick Kluivert, Marc Overmars.'

Luiz Felipe Scolari, his coach at Cruzeiro, gave him his only senior Brazil cap, against Mexico at the 2001 Copa America. 'It was a dream for me: to leave a town of 4,000 people (Acaiaca) and one day represent Brazil,' he says. 'He (Scolari) was a father to me.'

These days Geovanni is a volunteer pastor in Belo Horizonte and runs a players' agency with his father-in-law and an old youth-team friend.

But Hull will always be in his heart. He has a picture of himself in a Hull shirt in his house and received a hero's return after heading back to the city last year.

'I love them (the fans). I have a very special affection for the Hull supporters,' he says. 'It was two years in which I gave everything. I went back there last year and was really well received, it was great: friends from my time there, the fans too.

Battling Blackburn's Damien Duff in a pre-season friendly in his Barcelona days. He spent only two seasons with the Catalan club, having left Cruzeiro to move to Europe

'I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart'

'And I know I left my mark on the club's history. Whenever people talk about Hull City, about Brazilians, they'll remember Geovanni, the time I spent there, the feats we achieved together.

'And I believe I gave those fans a lot of joy, in games that seemed impossible. God blessed me and I was able to score goals and bring joy to that city. I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart.

'My two years at Hull were perhaps the two most special years for me. The sweetest spell of my career.'

Sports.title: How England rebuilt Maro Itoje: Inside the 'magic' masterplan that got shattered captain back 'firing on all cylinders' - and kept him out of French clubs' clutches
Sports.content:
How England rebuilt Maro Itoje: Inside the 'magic' masterplan that got shattered captain back 'firing on all cylinders' - and kept him out of French clubs' clutches

Given the summer off for the first time in his 13-year rugby career, Maro Itoje made the most of it – jetting as far afield as Mauritius and Nigeria.

When he returned, a curious twist of fate saw him bump into his England coach Steve Borthwick and club and country team-mate Jamie George at Heathrow. It was a reminder that even as England and Lions captain, Itoje is just like everyone else in many ways: on holiday he bumps into all the same people he sees at home.

Now, Itoje has returned to the day job. Borthwick's leader of men is back in the saddle to take his country into a crucial autumn campaign which begins with his 103rd cap at home to Australia on Sunday.

‘He is moving really well,’ Borthwick said of Itoje, who should go past Courtney Lawes to take seventh place on England's all-time caps list this autumn. ‘He looks energised and refreshed. He is talking incredibly positively. I have been very impressed by him.

'Maro has an intensity in defence that is exceptional. His ability to win turnovers and make plays that have such a positive effect upon those around him is extraordinary. He is a leader. He looks good.’

As captain of England and after three tours with the Lions, Itoje’s status as one of the international game’s most decorated figures is undisputed – those 102 caps, three Six Nations titles including a Grand Slam, five PREM Rugby titles and three European Cups.

England captain Maro Itoje is back in the saddle to take his country into a crucial autumn campaign which begins with his 103rd cap at home to Australia on Sunday

As captain of England and after three tours with the Lions, Itoje’s status as one of the international game’s most decorated figures is undisputed

But sometimes even the very best start to struggle and that is what happened to Itoje in this year's Six Nations. England imploded as a collective, producing their worst Championship with just one win and a fifth-placed finish. Mirroring his team’s struggles, Itoje was nowhere near his best.

The constant grind and subsequent impact of 12 seasons of playing at the highest level had, understandably, caught up with Itoje. He has admitted as much. Itoje has regularly exceeded the stated 30-game-a-season limit for England’s top stars, and was also dealing the loss of his mother, Florence, who passed away in December 2025.

Something needed to be done, and club and country swiftly drew up a plan with a simple aim: let England's 32-year-old captain recuperate both mentally and physically, then be all guns blazing for the 2027 World Cup.

It was a first in English rugby and reflected the growing nature of collaboration between the RFU and PREM Rugby’s 10 clubs. Itoje missed the summer’s Nations Championship games with South Africa, Fiji and Argentina and – the chance meeting with Borthwick and George aside – was given the chance to completely switch off from rugby.

‘I’ve known Maro a long time,’ says England head of performance Phil Morrow, who also worked with Itoje at Saracens. ‘When we looked towards the World Cup and looked at all our key players, we knew this was an important season in particular.

'Maro has played a lot of rugby over a sustained period of time. He regularly plays 80 minutes for both club and country. He also had personal stuff going on last year. He was emotionally tired. People always talk about the physical aspect of rugby, but the psychological load and the pressures that go with that are just as significant.

'Guys like Maro are living out a lot of people’s dreams, and a lot of things come with that. But there's always a person behind the player. I think it's easy to forget that at times. All our players have mums or dads or wives or girlfriends who care about them. Everyone's got their own troubles.

'You can’t separate physiology and psychology because they both have a cost on people’s energy. Steve and I had a chat about Maro and we felt it would benefit him to have some proper time off, rest, spend time with his family and have a proper pre-season with Saracens.

Itoje and England endured a harrowing Six Nations, losing four of their five matches including to Italy for the first time

'He’s an older player now, but he’s got a fresh enthusiasm,' says Phil Morrow. 'I can see that in his body language, the work he’s doing, and the energy he’s bringing to training’

'He’s an older player now, but he’s got a fresh enthusiasm for the big year we have ahead of us. I can see that in his body language, the work he’s doing, and the energy he’s bringing to training.’

Saracens were involved every step of the way on Itoje’s management. Head coach Joe Shaw hailed his star player’s rest period as ‘magic’ and a ‘genius’ move.

‘I’ve given Maro some stick about being old,’ Shaw told Daily Mail Sport. ‘It was about what was best for Maro, best for Saracens and best for England and all the stars aligned. We told him he could have even more time off if he wanted, but he was in the building for the first day of pre-season which was huge for us. He wanted to help the youngsters.’

Itoje’s England and Lions commitments have previously always meant a late arrival back at Saracens, the only club he's ever known and where he has agreed a new deal. Part of the reason for doing so, and turning down more lucrative contract options in France, is because of his RFU-enhanced management.

As one of England’s top 25 players, Itoje is on an enhanced elite player squad contract, which gives Borthwick and Morrow greater control of his time and treatment. It would be surprising if other top stars don’t follow Itoje’s lead in the future, with one possible candidate for a period of rest being wing Tommy Freeman.

‘We’ve already seen the repercussions,’ said Shaw, whose side sit fourth in the PREM, level on points with second-placed Gloucester. ‘Maro has played so well. He’s been brilliant for us. I feel he’s had a freshness about him and he’ll go into the autumn Tests in good form.

‘We all want the England captain firing on all cylinders throughout the autumn, the Six Nations and the World Cup. If England are to do well, we’ve all got to work together.’

Itoje was also left out of Saracens’ last game before the Test break to give him even more time to rev up for England duty. He and his wife Mimi have had their first child and he has signed with WME Sports – the same agency as Keely Hodgkinson and Emma Raducanu.

‘Maro has played so well, he’s been brilliant for us,' says Saracens head coach Joe Shaw, whose side sit fourth in the PREM table after five rounds

Itoje's partnership with Under Armour saw him play basketball with Mikel Arteta, manager of his beloved Arsenal, last month

Itoje’s marketing ability remains clear, especially compared to other rugby players. His Instagram page is constantly used to promote partnerships with drinks and cosmetics brands, among many others.

One clip showed a three-hour trip to Amsterdam by private plane for an appearance for American sportswear company Under Armour, through whom he has also played basketball with Mikel Arteta, manager of his beloved Arsenal.

The enforced rest period, combined with his dedication and professionalism, means there is no reason why he can’t play for another four or five years. Should he do so, he would put himself in the frame to be England’s best ever player and would almost certainly become their most capped.

First, though, comes a crucial autumn. England need to win and win now. Having a revitalised Itoje can only help with that.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer's England lifeline: Three Lions ask Chelsea about star's fitness in clear sign Thomas Tuchel is considering calling him up after warning over last squad withdrawal
Sports.content:
England have privately asked Chelsea for the latest on Cole Palmer ahead of Thomas Tuchel revealing his squad for the Nations League clashes with Croatia and Spain. Palmer is under consideration for another call-up, having withdrawn from duty during the last international break with a minor muscular injury. Tuchel responded by appearing to question his desire to represent his country, warning he 'misses way too many camps' as the 24-year-old skipped all four England fixtures in September and October. Palmer had played a full 90 for Chelsea away at Bournemouth before that break, which he then used to fly abroad to the Caribbean with his girlfriend, Olivia Holder, after withdrawing from England duty. He was accompanied by a personal rehab coach on that trip, and was provided with an injury-specific training and recovery plan by his club. Palmer started in Chelsea's first fixture when the Premier League returned at home to Brentford with Blues boss Xabi Alonso insisting they were right to take care of their star player themselves. Chelsea star Cole Palmer is under consideration for England UEFA Nations League call-up He withdrew from the last squad, leaving boss Thomas Tuchel questioning his commitment Palmer, who was injured, went to the Caribbean with girlfriend Olivia Holder on the last international break It has been described as standard procedure for England to make medical checks on players with clubs. While it does not guarantee a call-up, it indicates how Tuchel has been weighing up offering Palmer another chance as he names his next squad on Friday morning. Palmer was not the only player to withdraw from England duty in the last break, with Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento among other dropouts. Yet Palmer's issue was a contentious topic after it represented a chance for him to return to England's thinking following his 2026 World Cup omission. His representative did not answer when asked whether he would happily accept another call-up after Tuchel's previous comments. Palmer has played an important role for Chelsea early in this season with three goals and three assists in the Premier League. He scored a penalty in their last win over Manchester United, which took him to 50 goals in 105 games in the top flight for the Blues. He has started every league game under Alonso this term with Sunderland at the Stadium of Light this Sunday.
