However the following year the new world champion fell out spectacularly with team mate Carlos Reutemann, who refused an order to let Jones win in the second race at Rio de Janeiro. While the atmosphere soured at Williams, Piquet took advantage, snatching the title from Reutemann at the final race.

Jones announced his retirement at the end of 1981. He may have come to regret the decision as Reutemann also quit the team in the off-season and Keke Rosberg, plucked from obscurity to fill Jones’ seat, took the 1982 title.

He clearly still had an appetite for racing. Arrows tempted him back for a one-off start in the 1983 Long Beach Grand Prix but could not agree terms for a full-time return. He made a one-off start in the CART IndyCar series substituting for Mario Andretti at Road America in 1985, taking a fine third place behind Jacques Villeneuve Snr and Michael Andretti.

The prospect of leading a new team with bespoke Ford engines and backing from US retail giant Beatrice tempted him back to F1 again with Haas (no relation of the current Haas team) the same year.

The Ford engines weren’t ready in time for the end of the season so Jones entered the final rounds in a single-car entry powered by a Hart motor. However the project faltered: Beatrice pulled out its funds and by the time the Ford engine came good, Haas had pulled the plug. Jones made his final start in his home race in 1986.

He went on to compete successfully in Australia’s popular touring car series, where he ran his own team. He was tempted back to race single-seaters in the short-lived Grand Prix Masters series, but pulled out mid-weekend citing neck pain after lapping off the pace. Jones also ran Australia’s A1 Grand Prix team, helping to promote the likes of future IndyCar champion Will Power.

Jones remarried and is survived by his partner Amanda and his six children Christian, Amber, Zara, Jack, Camilla and Emma.

Sports.title: Alan Jones, 1980 Formula 1 world champion, dies aged 80 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 world champion Alan Jones has passed away at the age of 80.

Jones was the first driver to win a world championship for Williams, clinching the title in the penultimate round of the 1980 season driving a Ford Cosworth-powered FW07B.

He scored his 11th and final grand prix victory the following year but announced his retirement from F1. He later returned with the original Haas team but left for good at the end of 1986.

Williams paid tribute to Jones, whose 80th birthday was on Monday.

“Everyone at Williams is deeply saddened to learn of Alan Jones’ passing,” said the team in a statement. “Alan was instrumental in making Williams what it is today, forming an extraordinary bond with Frank Williams and Patrick Head to become our first drivers’ world champion in just our fourth season in Formula 1.

“He set the standard for Williams champions: a fast, uncompromising racer with a challenger mentality who loved motor racing and dedicated his life to it. He is a true Australian icon and a Williams legend, and he will be dearly missed.

“We send our love and thoughts to the Jones family and all his friends.”

The Australian Grand Prix promoters issued a statement saying they received the news of Jones’ death “with great sadness.” Jones won the race in 1980 when it was held as a non-championship event at Calder Park and was chiefly contested by Formula 5000 machinery plus two Formula 1 cars, one of which Jones drove.

“As a Formula 1 world champion and one of Australia’s greatest racing drivers, Alan holds a special place in the history of our sport,” the statement continued. “His 1980 world championship inspired a generation of Australian motorsport fans, while his victory at the Australian Grand Prix that same year remains the last time an Australian driver has won their home grand prix.

“He leaves an extraordinary legacy in Australian motorsport and will be deeply missed by the motorsport community around the world.”

Sports.title: A home debutant and another Mercedes title? Six Brazilian GP talking points | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Brazilian fans unexpectedly have two home drivers on the grid this weekend. Here are the talking points for Formula 1’s trip to South America.

Brazil’s new generation

For the first time in 10 years, two Brazilian drivers will line up on the grid at Interlagos this weekend.

Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara will make his grand prix debut earlier than expected. Haas will put the Ferrari junior driver into the seat formerly occupied by Esteban Ocon, which he was not due to take over until next year.

He will join Gabriel Bortoleto, who impressed in his debut season last year and is on course to end the season ahead of experienced team mate Nico Hulkenberg in the standings.

It’s an exciting time for Brazilian motor racing talent. But spare a thought for the sadly overlooked Felipe Drugovich, who spent years testing for Aston Martin after winning the F2 title, came close to making his F1 debut at the beginning of 2023, but now appears unlikely to get another chance.

All over for Ocon?

Also at this race 10 years ago, Ocon put in an under-rewarded performance for Manor, finishing just one-and-a-half seconds outside the points in streaming wet conditions.

His sensational and as-yet unexplained ousting by Haas in the middle of the last race weekend looks like being the end of his time in F1. It was not a career he came by easily, and one he almost lost at the end of 2018, when Lawrence Stroll bought Racing Point and dropped Ocon to create a vacancy for his son to fill.

With few opportunities elsewhere on the grid remaining, it’s hard to see how the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix winner can come back from this.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Ferrari fall-out

There were testy moments between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc before last weekend. But the Mexican Grand Prix was by far the clearest example of them costing each other a win.

In 2024 Leclerc claimed victory at Monza by capitalising on the feuding McLarens at the start. Two years on, will Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur react the way his rivals did, by imposing stricter conditions on how his drivers race each other?

The other championship

How well Ferrari perform this weekend will have a strong bearing on whether Mercedes clinch the constructors’ championship or have to wait until Las Vegas.

Mercedes arrive in Brazil 126 points ahead of Ferrari, the only team that can still beat them to the title. If their lead is at least 129 points when the chequered flag falls on Sunday, Mercedes will regain the crown they last won in 2021.

McLaren respond to Red Bull

Mexico was the sixth consecutive weekend in which Red Bull out-scored McLaren. The two teams are separated by 17 points in their scrap for third place, but McLaren intend to respond this weekend.

McLaren will introduce changes to their front and rear wings this weekend, plus a modification to their floor. Will that improve the performance of the car – or at least make it easier for Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri to extract the best from it?

The final act?

While Formula 1 races in Brazil, at least some of Moto GP’s teams are due to race in Qatar. Only some, because Yamaha has already confirmed it won’t send its teams due to concerns over the threat to the event from the war in Iran.

America resumed strikes on Iran on Wednesday and it remains to be seen what steps it will take following yesterday’s midterm election results. Many in F1 will be anxiously monitoring the situation and whether Moto GP presses ahead with its plan to race in Losail.

Sports.title: Cracked sump almost put Antonelli out of Mexican Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes has revealed Andrea Kimi Antonelli came close to retiring from the Mexican Grand Prix.

The team discovered the new world champion’s car had developed a fault in its power unit in the final laps.

Mercedes’ deputy team principal Bradley Lord described it as “a sign of the fact that this is Kimi’s year and things are rolling with him.”

“We got the car back after the race, took the floor off the bottom, [and found it was] covered in oil,” he told High Performance Racing. “Sump cracked.”

Antonelli was already detecting signs of trouble from his Mercedes power unit. “Kimi said he thinks about four laps from the end he could start to feel the engine just starting to struggle. So [he was] right on the edge of retirement [from] that race and yet it held together.”

The Mercedes driver lost almost two seconds on the final lap of the race, though he said that was because he was crying. He would still have clinched the title had his engine failed, but a retirement would have robbed him of the iconic photograph with Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton he wants to put on his wall.

Lord also shed more light on the loss of power George Russell suffered on the run to turn one at the start of the race, which allowed several of his rivals to overtake. “He’s taken the lion’s share of these technical problems and quirks and we had another one on Sunday,” said Lord.

“He was in prime position for going for the lead into turn one and then [has] a de-rate out of nowhere because of one of the complex bits of the energy rules mean he’s back in P5, P6 and caught up in the [mess] with Hadjar.

“It was a little bit like Spa, the start of the race there where he was so well positioned and then it just became that collision at turn four.”

Sports.title: Stats: Hirakawa is sixth one-off starter to score a world championship point | 2026 Mexican Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen won the race and the new world champion finished third: this year’s championship-deciding race resembled last year’s, though the similarity was superficial.

There may have been three drivers still in contention but this wasn’t a down-to-the-wire nail-biter: Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s coronation was virtually assured before he even set foot in Mexico.

Third place ensured Antonelli succeeds Lando Norris as F1’s second new world champion in as many years. That hasn’t happened since 2010 when Sebastian Vettel became the fourth new world champion in a row, following Kimi Raikkonen, Lewis Hamilton and Jenson Button.

Norris’s reign as world champion therefore lasted less than a calendar year. At 329 days, this is the sixth-shortest individual duration as champion. However others who had short spells as champion won the title more than once, giving them longer reigns:

Shortest reigns as world champion (days)

*Died before winning the championship

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Antonelli’s championship success produced several notable statistics which were previously covered here:

Lewis Hamilton became the oldest driver to claim pole position for a grand prix in his lifetime. At 41 years and 297 days old he is the most senior pole-winner since another Ferrari driver, Mario Andretti, took pole position for the 1982 Italian Grand Prix. Hamilton is the fifth-oldest driver ever to claim a pole position in F1.

Oldest F1 pole-winners

Driver Race Track Age Giuseppe Farina 1954 Argentinian Grand Prix Buenos Aires 47y, 78d Juan Manuel Fangio 1958 Argentinian Grand Prix Buenos Aires 46y, 208d Jack Brabham 1970 Spanish Grand Prix Jarama 44y, 16d Mario Andretti 1982 Italian Grand Prix Monza 42y, 195d Lewis Hamilton 2026 Mexican Grand Prix Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez 41y, 297d

Hamilton’s pole position was his first for over three years. That’s well short of the longest spell between consecutive pole positions: Raikkonen went 3,262 days (over eight years) between his pole positions in the 2008 French Grand Prix and 2017 Monaco Grand Prix.

That record-extending 105th pole position for Hamilton was a close thing: he beat George Russell by just nine-thousandths of a second. But that was three times the scale of his last pole-winning margin. Hamilton beat Verstappen to pole by just three thousandths of a second in Hungary three years ago.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Unexpectedly, 17 places behind Hamilton on the grid was Ryo Hirakawa, who arrived in Mexico only expecting to take part in the first practice session. However Haas’s shock decision to replace Esteban Ocon after Friday’s running handed Hirakawa his grand prix debut at the age of 32 years and 239 days. That made him the oldest debutant since Andre Lotterer made his one-off appearance for Caterham in the 2014 Belgian Grand Prix – he was older by 39 days.

It’s not uncommon for a driver to take part in practice and then be replaced due to illness or injury. Occasionally, teams swap drivers between garages if damage leaves them with only one car available, as happened with Logan Sargeant and Alexander at the 2024 Australian Grand Prix.

But it is very unusual to see a healthy driver begin a race weekend with a team and then be replaced someone else. The last time something akin to Ocon’s substitution happened was when Ensign attempted to run Ricardo Londono-Bridge in the 1981 Brazilian Grand Prix.

The race moved to Jacarepagua that year and the Colombian driver took part in the then-customary pre-event acclimatisation session for the new circuit on Wednesday. However the FIA refused to grant him a superlicence, so Ensign replaced him with Marc Surer.

Hirakawa’s surprising weekend continued as he scored a point despite originally taking the chequered flag in 13th place. Penalties for Oscar Piastri and both Alpine drivers meant Hirakawa, like Arvid Lindblad earlier this year, finished his first grand prix inside the points.

As it stands, Hirakawa will not take part in any more races – Rafael Camara will take over in Brazil. F1’s rules only allow Haas to use a total of four drivers all season, unless they get a dispensation, and the team has an obvious reason to keep Camara in the season as he will drive for them next year.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hirakawa therefore stands to join the tiny group of drivers who scored a point in their only start. Just six drivers can claim this unusual feat, and only one – Neville Lederle – did it driving solo in a race run to Formula 1 regulations:

Single-start points-scorers

Driver Race Position Points Notes Joie (George) Chitwood 1950 Indianapolis 500 5th 1 Shared car with Tony Bettenhausen Dorino Serafini 1950 Italian Grand Prix 2nd 3 Shared car with Alberto Ascari Eric Thompson 1952 British Grand Prix 5th 2 Formula 2 regulations Oscar Galvez 1953 Argentinian Grand Prix 5th 2 Formula 2 regulations George Amick 1958 Indianapolis 500 2nd 6 Neville Lederle 1962 South African Grand Prix 6th 1

It remains to be seen whether Ocon will return to start another race. At the beginning of the season the Mexican Grand Prix was due to be his 200th career start. Without him, the number of race-winning drivers on the grid has fallen to 12.

Finally, Verstappen’s sixth win at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez makes it the venue he’s scored the most wins at. He could equal that with a sixth win at Yas Marina next month – if the race takes place.

Sports.title: On This Day: Penske makes final CART appearance as longest season ends | Brief
Sports.content:
The end of CART’s longest-ever season, 25 years ago today, marked a watershed moment in the series’ battle with the rival Indy Racing League, formed by a split five years earlier.

Cristiano da Matta won the 21st and final event of the 2001 campaign at the Fontana superspeedway. However the season was marked by rows over technology, the controversial cancellation of a race in Texas on safety grounds and the appalling Lausitzring crash which almost claimed the life of Alex Zanardi.

Significantly, the 2001 finale saw the last appearance of the powerhouse Penske team before it defected to the IRL. Over the coming years rival engine manufacturers followed them and CART fell into bankruptcy. The two series reunited in 2008 and Roger Penske’s organisation purchased the merged IndyCar series in 2019.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Needs to Stop Living in the Past to Sell Liam Paro Clash
Sports.content:
Devin Haney is digging into his past, using his victories over George Kambosos to hype his December 19 unification clash with Liam Paro at Chase Center. Dominating Kambosos secured undisputed status at lightweight, but rehashing those nights won’t fire up crowds to see him chase another belt.

“My resume speaks for itself,” Haney stated. “I’ve never been afraid to go into a champion’s backyard and put my record on the line. I went to Australia, took George Kambosos’ belts, and became undisputed lightweight champion of the world. Now I’m bringing another Australian world champion, Liam Paro, into my backyard. This time, I plan to take his belt and become a unified welterweight world champion right here at home.”

Rehashing those wins now doesn’t elevate Liam Paro; it just reminds everyone how limited Kambosos actually was. The problem is that nationality is not a fighting style. Paro earned his IBF junior welterweight belt by traveling to Puerto Rico and physically outworking Subriel Matias, a dangerous puncher who was supposed to run through him.

If Haney truly understood how to build a fight, he would talk about Paro traveling to Puerto Rico to derail Subriel Matias or how Paro will actually bring a fight to him. Instead, he defaults to his old comfort blanket because self-promotion has never been his strong suit.

Paro is a tougher, more durable, and fundamentally different stylistic threat than Kambosos ever was. By presenting Paro through the Kambosos lens, Haney actually diminishes his own opponent while making the matchup sound like an easy rerun.

Devin needs to stop pretending the fans only care about belts. Haney should focus on the homecoming angle by promising a style change from his normal pure boxing approach. If he speaks openly about having to stand his ground against Paro’s physical, brawling style, he gives people a reason to watch for drama rather than just waiting on the judges’ scorecards.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Says Usyk Discussed March Trilogy Fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury claims Oleksandr Usyk signaled he could be ready to step into the ring again in March. That float keeps the door ajar for a third encounter, even with the Ukrainian holding two clear victories over him. Fury must handle Anthony Joshua first, yet he is already floating Usyk’s name for his next move.

Fury says the conversation happened when the Joshua matchup still hung in the balance. No paperwork exists for a trilogy, and Fury leaves crucial blanks, starting with whether March remains realistic once he steps out against Joshua.

“I actually spoke with Alexander to say, like, if he doesn’t fight, then we’ll do it. And he said he’s busy. He’s going on holiday with his family, but he could do a fight in March. So, maybe we do that in March. I don’t know yet. One fight at a time,” Fury said to Fighthype.

Booking the pairing again guarantees immense global interest, yet justifying it on merit gets tricky after back-to-back Usyk wins. Fury commands massive crowds, but he cannot claim unsettled business in the ring, no matter how vigorously he disputes the scorecards.

He still speaks as if the two losses solved nothing. When asked about those bouts, he doubled down on his claim that the judges got them wrong.

“I thought I won both fights,” Fury insisted. “I’m not bitter towards Alexander. He’s a good man. Like, he’s a God-fearing family man. I wish him all the luck in the world. But when he looks in that mirror every day, he knows he didn’t beat GK.”

That stance gives him an obvious marketing angle. He can insist he got robbed twice, promising to finish the job inside the distance next time. Spectators who watched Usyk take both contests will need stronger proof to believe a third chapter goes any differently.

Joshua might shatter this entire timeline anyway. Fury must defeat AJ and emerge unscathed for March to stay viable. A grueling war would instantly derail such a tight turnaround.

Fury also brushed aside talk about Usyk dropping down to cruiserweight to face David Benavidez, arguing that a Usyk trilogy offers the premier commercial draw.

“He just wants a big payday, and I’m his man to give him that,” Fury stated.

However, Saudis almost certainly pass on financing a third meeting, and outside of Riyadh, nobody else has the appetite to write those checks. Turki Alalshikh cares about global prestige and spectacle rather than standard event profit and loss, but he avoids financing fights that feel settled or stale. When one man has already collected 24 rounds of undisputed evidence across two fights, the storyline vanishes.

Alalshikh wants legacy events that captivate the sporting world, not expensive reruns where the outcome feels foregone. Unless Tyson Fury delivers an explosive, career-altering win that makes fans demand it again, Alalshikh will look to put his budget behind fresh pairings.

If the Saudis say no, the fight essentially dies right there. Here is why neither traditional promoters nor major streaming platforms would step into that breach:

Traditional promoters like Frank Warren’s Queensberry or Bob Arum’s Top Rank operate strictly on commercial reality. To stage Fury vs. Usyk 3 without Saudi site fees, they would have to fund massive eight-figure guarantees entirely through ticket sales, sponsorships, and pay-per-view buys.

The first two fights showed that pay-per-view numbers alone struggle to justify astronomical purses without state subsidies. Putting together $80 million to $100 million in combined purses on a pay-per-view model for a 2-0 rivalry would be financial suicide for any standalone promoter.

Netflix has entered live combat sports, but its entire strategy relies on massive cultural events and spectacle that drive mainstream global viewership without pay-per-view barriers. A technical chess match between two pure boxers, where the Ukrainian has already dominated the series, does not fit the kind of mass-market spectacle Netflix targets.

If Netflix is going to spend tens of millions on a live boxing broadcast, they will chase crossover draws or a massive domestic clash like Fury against Anthony Joshua, not a redundant third bout between Fury and Usyk.

Sports.title: De La Hoya Says Huge Paydays Hurt Boxing
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya makes a legitimate point about the fallout from boxing’s oversized paydays. The moment an elite fighter lands an exorbitant purse, putting together another significant fight becomes an uphill battle.

A wealthy champion can comfortably afford to stay on the sidelines, waiting around for another monster payday rather than risking a world title against an unheralded, high-risk challenger for standard money.

This dynamic leaves skilled contenders with smaller fanbases stranded. They climb the ranks and secure mandatory status, yet they still struggle to bait a titleholder into the squared circle. Defeating an unheralded contender offers minimal commercial value to an established champion, while an upset defeat destroys their future earnings.

“Fighters are ducking their mandatories and taking forever to fight the very best opponents. Why is that? Because Turki’s paying for this,” De La Hoya argued during his latest Clap Back Thursday broadcast.

De La Hoya aimed his remarks directly at Turki Alalshikh, alleging the Saudi investor overpays competitors who fail to deliver in the ring. While that view concentrates blame on a single financier, the broader problem reaches far beyond whoever signs the checks.

A massive purse quickly morphs into an athlete’s baseline demand. Normal market offers suddenly appear insulting, even when those figures match actual gate receipts and broadcast revenue. Flush with cash, the fighter holds all the leverage to decline fights and sit idle.

The sport simply lacks enough marquee rivals capable of producing record-setting revenues on demand. When several elite boxers freeze their careers chasing the same small pool of opponents, extended layoffs turn into the standard routine. Top contenders get told to stay busy, taking on all the danger while the biggest names bide their time for optimal terms.

The classic rationale of high danger and low reward makes fiscal sense to managers, but fans have grown exhausted hearing about it. Holding a world championship should demand more than cherry-picking matchups that deliver maximum profit with minimal physical jeopardy.

Canelo Alvarez facing the choice between Hamzah Sheeraz and Osleys Iglesias highlights this exact problem. Facing Hamzah Sheeraz guarantees strong ticket sales and broadcast numbers, while Osleys Iglesias poses a dangerous stylistic nightmare that only dedicated purists recognize. The avoided challenger gets passed over precisely because he possesses the skill set to score an upset.

Riyadh Season bankrolling could ideally bridge that gap. If conventional promotional companies cannot guarantee the money required to finalize tough bouts, an ultra-wealthy investor holds the power to make them happen. Throwing massive capital at famous names accomplishes little for the sport unless the matchmaking forces champions into genuine danger.

When fighters realize giant checks arrive regardless of opponent quality, they have zero incentive to accept severe stylistic challenges. Convincing them to take tough fights for less money later turns nearly impossible.

The sanctioning bodies share substantial blame for enabling this cycle. When titleholders receive continual exemptions, mandatory challengers pay the price in lost prime years. Owning a championship belt must carry an ironclad duty to defend it against legitimate contenders, regardless of how many pay-per-view buys those challengers command.

Boxers take immense physical punishment and deserve every dollar they generate. De La Hoya’s point reminds everyone that financial compensation must remain tied to competitive matchmaking. Whenever excessive wealth allows champions to freeze divisions and avoid elite threats, the entire sport suffers long after the money gets spent.

Boxing has reached a state where capital is subsidizing inactivity. In past eras, financial pressure kept fighters active. A fighter made a living by entering the ring three or four times a year. If a champion held a belt, sitting idle cost real money, which meant dangerous mandatory challengers actually got their shot.

Contenders could leverage their number one ranking because champions could not afford to take an eighteen-month vacation waiting for an imaginary windfall. Once an unbacked financial bubble enters the ecosystem, the entire risk calculation collapses. A fighter walks away from one evening with forty or fifty million dollars.

From that moment on, their market value in their own mind is anchored to that unnatural number. An honest domestic or network promoter offering four million dollars to defend against an undefeated, dangerous mandatory looks like an insult, even if four million is the maximum revenue that gate and television rights can actually support. Because the champion is already rich beyond imagination, they hold all the leverage to say no.

They pack their bags, hit the gym casually, post workout clips on social media, and wait by the phone for the next massive check from a sovereign wealth fund or a deep-pocketed financier. The consequences for everyone else in the sport are brutal. Entire divisions freeze due to this problem. When three or four top names in a weight class are all parked on their couches waiting on the same financial patron to call their number, nobody fights each other. The pipeline stalls.

You end up with prime athletes fighting once every twelve to sixteen months, burning away their athletic peaks in hotel lobbies and negotiation rooms instead of under the lights

The fighters who actually take the hit are the avoided, high-skill contenders. A guy who worked his entire life to become a mandatory challenger suddenly finds himself in an impossible trap. The champion will not fight him for realistic money because the contender does not bring casual pay-per-view buys. At the same time, the champion demands absurd money from outside backers to take on the stylistic hazard. The contender is told to stay busy, fight other dangerous guys for modest purses, and hope the superstar eventually runs out of soft alternatives.

It rewards marketability and name recognition while actively punishing ring ability. The sanctioning bodies completely capitulate, allowing it to happen. Belts exist to mandate competitive fights. Yet because sanctioning bodies take a percentage fee off the total purse, their financial allegiance lies with the massive check, not the integrity of their own rankings.

They gladly grant continuous medical exemptions, voluntary defense allowances, and special championship designations to mega-earners while stringing along the real number one contenders with interim straps. If the four sanctioning bodies had the spine to strip a wealthy champion the second an ordered mandatory defense deadline passed, this holdout culture would vanish overnight.

Boxing used to be built on hungry fighters needing to prove their dominance to sustain their livelihoods. Today, mega-purses have allowed elite fighters to operate like part-time consultants who only show up when the payout is absurd, and the opponent poses minimal threat to their brand.

Until the belts lose their marketing power or the infinite money well dries up, the sport will stay stuck in this loop of extended layoffs, ducked contenders, and synthetic events.

Sports.title: Devin Haney vs Liam Paro Faces A Tough PPV Sell
Sports.content:
Devin Haney’s first fight in more than a year will cost viewers extra. His December 19 bout with Liam Paro at Chase Center in San Francisco is officially a DAZN PPV, with Haney’s WBO welterweight title and Paro’s IBF belt at stake.

The belts give the fight a sporting purpose. Selling it is a different matter. Paro has earned his place, but he has a limited profile among American viewers, and a win over him would leave Haney with two of the division’s four major titles.

“I’ve never taken the easy road. I went to Puerto Rico and took the title off Matias in front of his own people. Devin’s a great fighter, and I respect that. But I’ve been the underdog plenty of times, and I’ve made history before. December 19, I’m coming to unify the division and make more history,” said Paro.

Placing a pay-per-view sticker on this card is going to be a tough sell. The entire model depends on casual interest or high-octane stylistic matchups, and this lineup offers neither to American buyers.

Haney sitting on the shelf for an entire year completely killed whatever tiny ripple of momentum he had after beating Norman Jr. Everyone remembers that bout as a safety-first wrestling match where Haney got on his bicycle, jabbed, and initiated clinches the second they got close. Purists might appreciate the ring IQ, but paying audiences want fireworks, especially when asked to drop extra cash on top of an existing subscription.

Paro is practically an unknown quantity to mainstream U.S. fans. His victory over Subriel Matias showed real grit in Puerto Rico, but casual viewers never saw it. His split-decision loss to Hitchins six months later only reinforced the perception that he is vulnerable to movers who control range. Sticking him in front of a San Francisco crowd against another defensive-minded boxer smells like another distance fight decided by jabs and positioning.

Then you look at the co-feature. Norman Jr. is fighting for redemption after losing his belt to Haney, but matching him against Abel Ramos is pure standard cable fare. Ramos is tough as nails, yet he has six losses and three draws on his ledger. Putting a former champion against a proven gatekeeper over ten rounds belongs on a regular DAZN Friday night stream, not on a premium broadcast that expects people to pull out credit cards six days before Christmas.

Unless Top Rank and Devin Haney Promotions pull off a miracle PR blitz or load the remaining two unannounced fights with genuine killers, this looks destined to struggle mightily at the box office.

“Now I’m bringing another Australian world champion, Liam Paro, into my backyard. This time, I plan to take his belt and become a unified welterweight world champion right here at home,” said Haney.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Climbs Rankings After Barely Surviving Wallace
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker holds the mandatory rankings to demand a world title shot right now, yet his shaky finish against Wallace shows he is nowhere near ready for that step up. Owning two top spots does not prove he can last twelve rounds with Dmitry Bivol. Wallace had him out on his feet and clinging for life in the closing seconds, exposing flaws that an elite operator would punish without mercy.

Whittaker is now ranked at #1 WBO, #1 IBF, and #3 WBC at light heavyweight. Promoter Eddie Hearn suddenly holds multiple paths to steer his fighter toward a strap. The problem is those gaudy rankings build up heavy expectations that Whittaker simply failed to justify against Wallace.

He won the October 3 IBF final eliminator by scores of 117-111, 116-112 and 115-113, building his lead behind the jab before Wallace hurt him late. The way Whittaker fell apart physically in the later rounds showed that he’s not ready for Bivol or Artur Beterbiev.

Hearn is targeting February or March for Whittaker’s return, with Anthony Yarde and the winner of Joshua Buatsi against Willy Hutchinson among the possibilities.

The problem is that the blueprint is out on how to beat Whittaker. In the 2020 Olympics in Tokyo, Arlen Lopez and Imam Khataev exposed the flaws by walking through the flash, cutting off the ring, and roughing Whittaker up on the inside. Conor Wallace didn’t invent anything new in the late rounds; he just dusted off the same heavy-pressure game plan.

Every solid light heavyweight contender watched Whittaker gas out and resort to clinging once his legs stiffened up. Marinating the Bivol matchup only works if Hearn can keep matching him against fighters who lack the punch or the engine to execute that exact strategy. One slip against a live underdog with a sturdy chin, and the entire cash-out plan evaporates before Bivol even enters the conversation.

Hearn has twelve to eighteen months at most to let the fight marinate. The calendar is working against him far quicker than Matchroom wants to admit.

Whittaker turns 30 next summer. He entered the pros with an Olympic pedigree, but his physical peak as an agile, Reflex-reliant fighter is happening right now. Waiting three or four years completely destroys his own physical advantages. Once his hand speed drops half a step or his legs fade five minutes earlier, he will not have the inside game or the durability to fall back on.

Waiting also assumes Bivol falls off a cliff overnight. Bivol turns 36 in December, but his style is built on footwork, distance management, and textbook fundamentals. Those attributes age far better than reliance on raw athleticism. A 37-year-old Bivol who has lost half a step will still possess the discipline and the tight combinations to pick apart a gassing Whittaker.

The real danger in stalling is the contender pool. Keeping Whittaker busy with fringe contenders or domestic rivals to run out the clock carries massive risk. The light heavyweight division is full of heavy-handed pressure fighters who took copious notes during the Wallace bout. If Hearn matches him with someone who has the engine to walk him down and the power to test his chin in rounds eight through twelve, Whittaker gets clipped before he ever sees a world title purse.

Hearn’s realistic window is late 2027. He can afford two tune-ups to work on conditioning and ring generalship under heavy fire. After that, he has to cash in the ticket, win or lose, before an ambitious contender beats him to the punch and ruins the entire investment.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Responds To Tyson Fury Injury Rumors
Sports.content:
Frank Warren says he knows nothing about Tyson Fury picking up an injury in camp, leaving Frank Bruno’s recent claim completely unbacked ahead of the Anthony Joshua fight.

Warren seemed surprised when asked about the talk surrounding Fury’s preparation for the December 11 date in Cardiff. He gave no support to the injury talk, though he stopped short of officially declaring Fury totally fit.

“That’s news to me. That’s news to me. Absolute news to me,” Warren repeated to the media today when asked about Bruno’s comments.

Bruno spoke publicly about hearing whispers that Fury suffered a setback in training. That remains unconfirmed, with no specific injury mentioned or verified. Casual gym talk happens all the time, and it is a long way from something serious enough to derail a massive bout.

Warren being Fury’s promoter means people naturally pay attention to his words, but observers need to look at the whole picture. Saying he has not heard anything bad is not the same as checking in directly with the trainers or getting an official update from a doctor. Nobody followed up by asking if he had spoken to the gym.

After waiting years for Fury and Joshua to finalize a deal, boxing followers get nervous at the slightest rumor. The bout took ages to put together, so nobody wants to see another delay. Still, nothing Warren said points to the Cardiff date being at risk.

The promoter kept right on talking up the event, including the addition of Deontay Wilder against Jai Opetaia on the undercard. He also fielded a question about Fury’s next move, with Daniel Dubois brought up as a possible future opponent.

“When Tyson wins the fight, he’ll make his choice what he wants to do,” Warren said.

That keeps Fury’s plans after Joshua completely open. Warren made no promises about facing Dubois or going after other champions, which makes sense before his fighter gets through the biggest domestic night of his career.

Right now, the focus is on whether any real facts emerge from the gym. Bruno’s standing ensures the story gets attention, but his name alone does not prove what is taking place in camp. Warren’s surprise does not completely shut down the conversation either.

Until Team Fury comes out with something concrete, there is no real basis for an injury crisis. Warren pushed back on the talk; the fight stays locked in for Cardiff, and the rumor simply lacks the substance to treat it as a done deal.

Sports.title: Vasiliy Lomachenko Signs Top Rank Deal, Chases Undisputed at 130
Sports.content:
The three-division champion plans to fight in early 2027 after signing a multi-year co-promotional deal through Loma Power Promotions.

Vasiliy Lomachenko is coming out of retirement and dropping back to super featherweight. The former IBF lightweight champion will return in early 2027 under a multi-year agreement between Top Rank and his newly formed Loma Power Promotions.

The comeback takes him back to 130 pounds, where he held the WBO belt before moving up to lightweight. Top Rank did not name an opponent, a fight date or a broadcaster in its November 5 announcement.

“I thought I would never step back into the ring again as a boxer,” Lomachenko said. “But our Lord Jesus Christ had other plans for me. I’m happy to be living this boxing life once again.”

Lomachenko Chases Undisputed at Super Featherweight

Lomachenko retired in June 2025 as IBF lightweight champion. He had stopped George Kambosos Jr. for the belt in May 2024, a year after losing his bid for the undisputed 135-pound championship against Devin Haney.

That chase now moves to 130. Top Rank chairman Bob Arum and manager Egis Klimas both identified an undisputed championship as the goal of the comeback.

“He’s accomplished so much, but he’s determined to become undisputed,” Arum said.

Lomachenko returns with an 18-3 record and 12 knockouts. The two-time Olympic gold medalist won his first professional title in his third bout and had claimed belts in three divisions by his 12th, when he stopped Jorge Linares to win a lightweight title in May 2018.

Top Rank has promoted Lomachenko since his professional debut in 2013. This time, his own promotional company will share the bill with the outfit that handled his rise through the divisions.

Lomachenko credited Klimas with pushing for a return after he had decided his fighting days were over.

“Special respect and gratitude to Egis, who, despite my firm belief that my boxing career was over, never stopped believing that we would step into the ring again. He put in a tremendous amount of work and effort to get us back in the race.”

Sports.title: IBF Orders Osleys Iglesias Defense As Canelo Weighs Options
Sports.content:
The IBF just handed Osleys Iglesias a mandatory defense against Malik Zinad at the worst possible time, with Canelo Alvarez still deciding on an opponent for a rumored February return. The Cuban holds a belt that makes him a legitimate unification target, but sanctioning body bureaucracy just dumped an unwanted roadblock in his way.

Iglesias was always an outside shot to get picked by Canelo, but holding the IBF super middleweight title legitimately placed him in that conversation. That makes this ruling sting even more. The IBF is forcing him into a matchup with Zinad, a challenger whose recent resume gives zero indication that he can compete at this level.

The sanctioning body officially ordered the fight, according to Mike Coppinger, who reported that The Ring obtained the IBF letter. Coppinger also highlighted that Iglesias is rated No. 2 by the publication at 168 pounds, meaning an eventual clash between Canelo and Iglesias would crown a new Ring champion.

A fight with Iglesias offers legitimate credibility rather than just another easy paycheck on the calendar. Unifying the division actually means something at 168 pounds. Canelo taking on a heavy-handed southpaw who presents actual danger is another question entirely.

The mandatory order does not mean a unification is dead in the water. Without an official ruling on a proposed Canelo fight, declaring Iglesias unavailable would be jumping the gun. What this ruling actually does is force the Cuban into tedious talks with Zinad while Canelo takes his sweet time sorting through his options.

The timing is worth a close look, but not as proof of backroom coordination. A champion who already faced steep odds to land the division’s golden ticket now has another unwanted complication thrown directly in his path.

Looking at Zinad, this is a glaring mismatch on paper. The 32-year-old challenger has only one career defeat, coming when Dmitry Bivol stopped him in six rounds during their June 2024 light heavyweight title fight. There is no shame in getting stopped by an elite operator like Bivol, but failing at 175 pounds is hardly a valid qualification for a mandatory title shot down at 168.

His recent schedule reveals the real issue. Zinad collected two bounce-back wins against Haris Dzindo and Ante Bilic. BoxRec lists Dzindo as an inactive cruiserweight. Bilic is 43 years old, listed at super middleweight, and currently sits at No. 285 in the BoxRec rankings. Neither victory provides a convincing reason to expect Zinad to give Iglesias an ounce of trouble.

Those bouts padded a record, plain and simple. They do virtually nothing to establish that a fighter deserves to stand at the very front of the line for a world championship.

Iglesias packs one-punch power behind a stinging southpaw jab and an awkward, concussive right hook that obliterates second-tier opposition. Zinad boasts a shiny record on surface inspection, but stripping away the numbers exposes empty padding against overmatched opposition.

The IBF has every right to call its mandatories. Still, handing out a world title shot to a fighter with this level of opposition demands real scrutiny, especially when it disrupts talks for the biggest fight in the division.

Iglesias gets tied up with Zinad while Canelo plays waiting games and takes his time. For a champion trying to turn his belt into life-changing money against the sport’s cash cow, getting derailed by a mandatory nobody wanted is a raw deal.

Ghana News.title: Accra’s disturbing potholes endanger motorists
Ghana News.content:
This picture shows the current situation at the Abeka Lapaz

Some major roads and highways in Accra have developed serious potholes, making driving on those roads dangerous for motorists and other road users.

Motorists who use these roads frequently indicated that their repeated calls to the authorities to fix the potholes have fallen on deaf ears, leaving them to navigate the damaged stretches at their own risk.

Abeka Lapaz

A visit by MyJoyOnline to some of the affected areas showed the extent of the problem and the daily struggle drivers go through to avoid damage to their vehicles or accidents.

At the Abeka Lapaz interchange, a portion of the busy outer lane had developed a deep pit.

Drivers say the pothole keeps breaking car axles and forcing them to swerve suddenly into other lanes, a situation that could easily cause accidents, especially during rush hours.

On the UPSA road

On the UPSA road, near the University of Ghana Business School, several potholes have also developed.

The road, which is used by students, lecturers, and residents, has become difficult to drive on, with motorists slowing down to avoid the damaged portions.

At East Legon, on the American House main road, there are also potholes.

The area is one of the busiest commercial and residential zones in Accra, and drivers say the potholes cause heavy traffic congestion as vehicles queue to dodge them.

At the Sakaman Junction traffic light, on the Accra-Kasoa Highways, there is another dangerous pothole.

Motorists say the pothole is particularly risky because drivers who stop at the traffic light are forced to move over it when the light turns green, causing damage to tyres and suspensions.

Similar potholes were also found at the New Bortianor and West Hills Mall area, where drivers say the road has deteriorated badly and needs urgent attention.

Many motorists who spoke during the visit expressed frustration over the state of the roads.

East Legon

They said they spend huge sums of money repairing their vehicles due to damage caused by the potholes, while others expressed fear for their safety, especially when driving at night or rainy days.

The potholes are filled with water and are difficult to identify when there is a downpour.

They are therefore appealing to the Ghana Highway Authority, the Department of Urban Roads, and the Accra Metropolitan Assembly to urgently repair the potholes before they cause serious accidents and loss of life.

Ghana News.title: Prof Beyuo takes responsibility for medical bills of 12 injured in Hamile unrest
Ghana News.content:
Lambussie MP Professor Titus Beyuo has offered to pay the hospital bills of 12 people injured in the violence that erupted in Hamile following a deadly explosion in the Upper West Region.

The injured residents are receiving treatment at different health facilities, with two requiring surgery for fractures sustained during the disturbances. The other 10 are said to be stable and awaiting medical reviews to establish whether they are fit for discharge.

The injuries followed confrontations between some residents and security personnel after tensions rose over allegations that civilians had been shot. The situation reportedly escalated into protests targeting the Ghana Immigration Service.

During the unrest, some protesters allegedly destroyed an Immigration Service checkpoint, damaged about three vehicles and moved towards the service’s office, prompting security personnel to secure the facility.

Warning shots were reportedly fired during the confrontation, leaving 12 people with injuries. Ten sustained puncture wounds, while two suffered fractures. A bullet was subsequently removed from the limb of one of the injured residents. The two patients with fractures were transferred to the regional hospital after nearby facilities were found unable to provide the required treatment.

Speaking on Citi FM on Thursday, November 5, 2026, Prof. Beyuo said he had visited the injured residents and informed their families and the hospitals that he would settle the cost of their treatment.

“I’ve informed the hospitals where they are, visited them, and I’ve informed the doctors there to give all the care and then forward the bills to me to settle,” he said.

The MP said the incident had created an unexpected situation for the affected families and assured them of his support as the residents receive medical attention.

Ghana News.title: Education Ministry, Gates Foundation consider partnership to boost Ghana’s malaria research
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Education and the Gates Foundation are exploring areas of collaboration to strengthen Ghana’s capacity to develop and deploy locally driven solutions in the fight against malaria.

The discussions centred on building local expertise in emerging malaria-control technologies, particularly research into the development of malaria-free mosquitoes, alongside technology transfer and institutional capacity building.

The commitment was reaffirmed by the Minister of Education during a meeting with a delegation from the Ghana National Research Fund (GNRF), led by its Board Chairman, Prof. Eric Yirenkyi Danquah, and the Gates Foundation, led by its Deputy Director for Malaria, Mr Bruno Moonen.

Prof. Gordon Awandare, Pro Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ghana, underscored the need to equip Ghanaian researchers with the technical expertise and resources required to develop and adapt such technologies locally.

The Education Minister said sustained investment in research, talent development and strong local institutions would be critical to advancing the proposed collaboration.

He said the broader objective was to strengthen Ghana’s research ecosystem, reduce malaria transmission and support the country’s ambition of eliminating the disease.

Ghana News.title: Opoku-Agyemang calls for prosecution of perpetrators of sex-for-jobs abuse
Ghana News.content:
Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has called for prompt investigations into sexual exploitation allegations in workplaces and educational institutions, stressing that anyone found guilty must be appropriately sanctioned.

She warned that demands for sexual favours in exchange for employment opportunities or academic grades were damaging to Ghana’s development, depriving institutions of talent, weakening productivity and undermining public trust.

The Vice President made the call at the 2026 Sex for Jobs Conference in Accra, where she described the practice as an abuse of authority that violates personal dignity and compromises the integrity of workplaces and educational institutions.

“The exploitation known as sex for jobs in workplaces and sex for grades in academic and training institutions constitutes an abuse of power, an erasure of bodily autonomy, and a breach of institutional integrity,” she said.

Professor Opoku-Agyemang said the consequences went beyond the immediate harm to victims, noting that such misconduct also carried significant economic and social costs.

“Beyond the moral injury, these are economic and social costs, including lost productivity and wasted talent. Every instance of abuse that forces people into silence erodes public trust in the institutions established to serve those people,” she added.

She said government acknowledged the scale of the problem and its responsibility to ensure that allegations were properly addressed.

She further advocated independent and confidential reporting mechanisms to protect complainants, particularly in cases where the accused persons wield authority over victims’ recruitment, promotion or academic progression.

Ghana News.title: Assafuah rejects Mahama’s invitation to World Cup visa probe committee
Ghana News.content:
Member of Parliament for Old Tafo and Ranking Member on Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee, Vincent Ekow Assafuah

Member of Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee Ranking Member, Vincent Ekow Assafuah, has rejected an invitation to appear before a committee set up by President John Dramani Mahama to investigate alleged irregularities in the 2026 FIFA World Cup visa acquisition process.

The MP says he will not participate in an investigation whose independence he questions, insisting that the allegations should instead be examined by an independent commission of inquiry.

At a press conference on Thursday, November 5, Mr Assafuah disclosed that the invitation was conveyed to him by the President through his presidential advisers.

He argued that the president's involvement in the process raised concerns because the investigation could involve ministers serving in his government.

“I have respectfully boycotted that invitation. I did so on principle. The president cannot be seen to be investigating his own ministers. You cannot be a judge in your own cause,” he said.

Mr Assafuah also faulted the committee for what he described as a lack of openness, questioning why its membership, terms of reference and proceedings had not been made public.

“That committee is shrouded in complete opacity. Its terms of reference are not public, its members are unknown, and its sittings are held behind closed doors,” he said.

He disclosed that he had petitioned the Office of the Special Prosecutor and the President to establish an independent commission to investigate the alleged visa and fundraising irregularities.

According to him, such a commission should operate transparently, have the power to compel the production of evidence and make its findings available to the public.

“What Ghana needs is not a secret in-house cover-up committee. What Ghana needs is a public, transparent, independent commission of inquiry with powers to subpoena, to publish evidence and to hold persons accountable openly,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Mahama sets monthly review of road crash data to measure TraffiTech results
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama

President John Dramani Mahama says the government will use monthly road accident figures to determine whether the newly introduced TraffiTech system is reducing crashes and preventing deaths on Ghana’s roads.

He said accident data recorded after the system became operational on November 1, 2026, would be compared with figures from the corresponding months last year to establish its impact.

Addressing a meet-the-press session at Jubilee House on Thursday, November 5, the President appealed to motorists to observe speed limits, particularly the 50-kilometre-per-hour limit in urban centres, as the government steps up automated traffic enforcement.

Mr Mahama said the technology was intended to improve compliance by replacing manual speed checks by police officers with an automated system that detects speeding and provides evidence of offences.

He expressed confidence that the intervention would help reduce road fatalities, citing 2,151 people killed in road crashes in Ghana last year. Of that number, 474 were pedestrians knocked down by vehicles, with schoolchildren returning from school accounting for a significant proportion of the deaths.

The President said excessive speed makes it difficult for drivers to respond quickly when pedestrians cross roads unexpectedly, increasing the likelihood of fatal collisions.

“I can assure you, if we bear with this TraffiTech system, when you see the results of reduction in accidents at the end of the year, because it started November 1st, we’ll do a month-to-month comparison with last year,” he said.

“And you yourself will be surprised at the number of lives this TraffiTech system will save.”

He reiterated that motorists in urban areas, including Accra, must not exceed 50 kilometres per hour, adding: “The general speed limit in any urban centre, including Accra, is 50. And so you are not supposed to go above 50.”

Mr Mahama also clarified that the speeding detection component is the only part of the TraffiTech system currently in operation.

Ghana News.title: Car dealers block Kwashieman footbridge walkway, exposing pedestrians to danger
Ghana News.content:
Roadside car dealers have blocked the pedestrian walkway leading to the Kwashieman footbridge in Accra, making it difficult for pedestrians to cross the N1 highway.

The dealers, who have been operating alongside the highway, have now extended their activities onto part of the walkway to the footbridge.

They have displayed cars for sale to cover almost half of the path, forcing pedestrians to struggle for space as they walk to and from the footbridge.

The situation has forced pedestrians to cross the busy George Walker Bush Highway, where speeding cars pass almost every minute.

The walkway was constructed to give pedestrians safe access to the footbridge and to protect them from the fast-moving vehicles on the N1. However, with cars now parked on the walkway, pedestrians are being pushed closer to the main road, exposing them to danger.

Some pedestrians who use the footbridge daily say the situation is worrying, especially during rush hours when many people use the route to cross to the other side.

According to residents, schoolchildren, the elderly and persons carrying loads are the most affected because they find it difficult to manoeuvre through the narrow space left by the parked cars.

They are appealing to the Accra Metropolitan Assembly, the Ghana Highway Authority and the law enforcement agencies to intervene and remove the cars from the walkway.

They say if the dealers are not stopped, they will completely take over the walkway and permanently force pedestrians onto the highway, which could lead to accidents and loss of life.

The pedestrians are calling for regular enforcement to keep the walkway clear and safe for its intended purpose.

Ghana News.title: Chinese malls taking 60% of Ghana’s retail market – GUTA laments
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Union of Traders’ Associations (GUTA) has raised concerns over the rapid expansion of Chinese-owned shopping malls in the country, claiming that they are taking an estimated 60 per cent share of the market and putting pressure on local businesses.

The association says the growing presence of the malls, including those operating within established trading centres, is having a negative impact on Ghanaian traders and has urged the authorities to investigate the trend.

The President of GUTA, Clement Boateng, said although the general business environment had shown signs of improvement, the expansion of the Chinese malls remained a major concern for local operators.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Thursday, November 5, he said key macroeconomic indicators were pointing in a positive direction, a development he believed should support trading activities.

However, he said the increasing number of Chinese shopping malls was creating a difficult environment for domestic businesses.

“If you all look at the microeconomic indices, one will say that they are all pointing to a very positive direction and definitely supposed to have a bearing on whatever activities that, as traders, we perform,” he said.

Mr Boateng said the expansion of the malls was particularly worrying because of the market share they were allegedly commanding.

“These Chinese shopping malls are springing up, and these shopping malls are taking about 60 per cent of our market share, and we think it is having a very negative impact as far as local businesses are concerned,” he said.

He called on the relevant authorities to examine their operations and assess the implications for Ghanaian-owned businesses.

Mr Boateng also raised concerns about the movement of profits generated by the malls outside the country, arguing that stronger local businesses would allow more of the earnings from commercial activities to remain in Ghana.

“These Chinese malls will repatriate their profits away. But if businesses, local businesses are doing well, definitely all the monies will remain here,” he said.

His comments add to GUTA’s concerns about the competitive pressures facing local traders as foreign-owned retail outlets expand their presence in the Ghanaian market.

The association is calling for attention from the authorities, although Mr Boateng did not outline specific regulatory measures he wants the government to introduce.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
