World.title: Ex-Air Force spokesperson identifies ‘flaw’ affecting Nigeria’s multi-trillion naira defence budget
World.content:
A former Nigerian Air Force spokesperson, Sadeeq Shehu, has faulted Nigeria’s defence budget structure, stating that poor planning and governance, rather than inadequate funding, are weakening the country’s security operations.

Mr Shehu, a retired group captain, made the assessment during an interview on ARISE News, monitored by PREMIUM TIMES, on Thursday, while examining the federal government’s special security interventions and defence allocations between 2023 and 2026.

He said that increasing military expenditure would not necessarily improve Nigeria’s security situation unless the government addressed how available resources were planned, allocated and utilised.

The retired officer said Nigeria was spending a reasonable proportion of its resources on defence but was failing to translate the expenditure into commensurate operational capacity.

“If you ask me, proportionate to what Nigeria is earning from its foreign trade and everything from petrol, I think we are spending right as far as amount is concerned. The problem is the plan and where do we put the money. The problem is also a governance issue,” he said.

His assessment comes on the heels of sustained security challenges across the country, including insurgency, banditry and other forms of violent crime, despite substantial government allocations to the defence and security sectors.

Mr Shehu identified the composition of the 2026 defence budget as evidence of the problem, saying an overwhelming proportion of the allocation was committed to personnel expenses at the expense of critical military requirements.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the N3.154 trillion defence allocation provides N2.4 trillion, representing 75.9 per cent, for personnel costs, while overhead expenditure accounts for 9.4 per cent, or about N297 billion.

He questioned how the military could adequately provide equipment, maintain existing platforms, train personnel and modernise its operations when such a substantial proportion of its budget was absorbed by personnel costs.

“This is where the major problem is. And I do not see either the executive branch or even the legislature attacking this,” he said.

The former air force spokesperson argued that Nigeria’s defence budget needed a more detailed classification to reveal how much was being committed to specific military requirements.

He said the existing practice of grouping expenditure under personnel, overhead and capital costs obscured the actual funding available for equipment procurement, maintenance, training, military infrastructure and research.

He maintained that more detailed defence budgeting systems provide clearer expenditure categories, enabling governments to identify operational gaps and direct resources towards priority requirements.

“What global best practice has shown us is that the only thing that comes out from this budget is personnel cost. You will wonder, where is equipment? Where is maintenance? Where is training? A paltry less than 25 per cent is allocated to the two of them. This is not good enough,” he said.

Mr Shehu warned that without proper planning, Nigeria could continue spending substantial amounts on defence without adequately addressing the military’s most pressing operational needs.

He said a poorly structured budget could leave essential requirements unfunded while directing scarce resources towards less critical areas.

“If you don’t plan your defence budget properly, you are likely to leave things that are essential and put money where they are not essential. That is the point I want to make,” he said.

He also questioned the capacity of the presidency and the National Assembly to effectively scrutinise defence expenditure, arguing that the existing budget structure did not provide sufficient details for informed oversight.

According to him, lawmakers and government officials need a clearer understanding of the military’s operational requirements to ensure that budget allocations reflect actual security priorities.

“If you just leave it into these three, you know, three subheads, personnel, capital and overhead, you will never get the proper picture. And I can assure you from my research, the National Assembly and even the presidency, they do not have really a clear picture of what the defence budget is all about,” he said.

Mr Shehu’s position suggests that Nigeria’s challenge may be beyond how much it spends on defence, but whether the expenditure is structured to deliver the equipment, training, maintenance and operational capacity required to confront the country’s security threats.

He maintained that improving defence planning and governance, rather than merely increasing military allocations, should be central to efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security operations.

World.title: Six journalists begin six-month fellowship to scrutinise development efforts in Niger Delta
World.content:
Six journalists from media organisations across Nigeria have begun a six-month fellowship to investigate development interventions, economic opportunities and efforts to address longstanding challenges in the Niger Delta.

The programme, launched on 2 November by the Foundation for Partnership Initiatives in the Niger Delta (PIND) and the School of Media and Communication (SMC), Pan-Atlantic University, is designed to strengthen development journalism and encourage more evidence-based reporting on the oil-rich region.

The initiative comes as development organisations, governments and private-sector actors continue to implement interventions in the Niger Delta, where continuous unemployment, insecurity, environmental degradation and limited economic opportunities have shaped public discourse about the region.

However, PIND said media coverage has often given limited attention to solutions, innovations and measurable development outcomes emerging from communities across the region.

The fellowship, known as the PIND Media Fellows Programme for Narrative Change in the Niger Delta, will combine specialised training, field immersion, access to development evidence and editorial mentorship.

It is expected to equip participating journalists to independently examine interventions in areas including peacebuilding, agriculture, youth employment, renewable energy and economic inclusion.

The programme opened with a five-day residential Impact Journalism Academy at SMC in Lagos, running from 2 to 6 November. The training covers development reporting, solutions journalism, impact storytelling, ethical interviewing, multimedia production and evidence-based reporting.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PIND Executive Director, Sam Daibo, said the initiative was conceived to address the limited attention given to development solutions and progress in the region.

“The Niger Delta’s challenges must be reported honestly, but they should not be its only story. Across the region, communities, businesses and development partners are advancing solutions in peacebuilding, agriculture, youth employment, renewable energy and economic inclusion. This fellowship will help journalists examine those efforts critically, independently and with the depth they deserve,” Mr Daibo said.

He stressed that the programme was not intended to influence editorial decisions or encourage favourable coverage of PIND’s activities.

“Our role is to give journalists greater access to evidence, communities and development practice while respecting their editorial independence. Credible development reporting must remain rigorous, balanced and accountable to the public,” he added.

Ikechukwu Obiaya, dean of SMC, said the partnership would help journalists move beyond reporting activities to examining whether development interventions were delivering tangible results.

“Development journalism requires more than reporting activities. Journalists must be able to interrogate evidence, understand systems, centre community voices and determine whether interventions are producing meaningful change,” he said.

He said the training would combine development journalism skills with practical reporting tools that participants could apply in their newsrooms and field assignments.

PIND’s development interventions

The fellowship draws on PIND’s longstanding development interventions across the Niger Delta, particularly its economic development and peacebuilding programmes.

Established in 2010, the organisation works across the region’s nine states through partnerships with governments, businesses, civil society organisations and communities.

Under its economic development programme, PIND supports agricultural value chains, youth employment, access to finance and renewable energy.

The organisation says its interventions have reached more than 598,000 farmers and microenterprises with improved agricultural practices and market linkages, trained more than 11,000 young people in vocational skills and facilitated access to clean energy for more than 14,000 households and businesses.

Its peacebuilding programme also supports grassroots conflict prevention, community peace structures and initiatives aimed at strengthening collaboration among stakeholders.

An impact evaluation of PIND’s interventions conducted by international consulting firm Dalberg in 2023 found that the organisation’s economic development and peacebuilding activities had facilitated 86,713 jobs and helped mitigate 1,469 conflicts in the Niger Delta. The evaluation examined interventions implemented since 2016.

Some of its recent interventions include partnerships to expand solar mini-grids in underserved communities, support climate-smart agriculture, improve youth employability and strengthen agricultural markets.

In August 2026, PIND, Okomu Oil and ETIN Power commissioned a solar mini-grid in Gbelebu community, while the organisation has also supported solar-powered cold storage facilities to reduce post-harvest losses among farmers in Bayelsa State.

READ ALSO: Group calls for withdrawal of charges against Kaduna journalist

The fellowship will give journalists opportunities to examine such interventions, interact with programme beneficiaries and technical experts, and independently assess their outcomes.

Following the academy, the fellows will undertake field immersion, develop reporting pitches and receive editorial mentorship during the production of their stories.

The six journalists selected for the inaugural cohort are Ekemini Simon of PREMIUM TIMES, Ann Godwin of The Guardian, Isaac Eranga of The Nigerian Observers, Joseph Kunde of TVC News, Kpono-Abasi Jackson of Akwa Ibom Broadcasting Corporation and Jennifer Orugbo of Delta Broadcasting Service.

Beyond the initial six-month programme, PIND and SMC said they intend to establish successive cohorts and build a network of journalists committed to rigorous, balanced and evidence-driven reporting on the Niger Delta.

The initiative marks an attempt to move beyond occasional media engagements towards sustained investment in journalists’ capacity to interrogate development interventions and communicate their actual impact.

World.title: Peter Obi blames APC for court judgement sacking Atiku, David Mark
World.content:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has faulted the court judgement that sacked the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and nullified the candidacy of all its aspirants for the 2027 elections. Mr Obi also accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being responsible for the court ruling.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday declared as illegal, the David Mark-led Caretaker Committee, which conducted the ADC’s presidential primary that produced ex-Vice President Atiku Abubakar as its flag bearer.

The court also sacked the entire national officers of the party, including National Secretary Rauf Aregbesola, alongside all the candidates the party presented to the Independent National Electoral Commission for the 2027 elections.

‘Surprising and unsettling’

Reacting in an X post on Thursday evening, Mr Obi said he received the report of the court judgement with “shock.”

“This is unsettling and surprising,” he said of the judgement.

The NDC candidate said that while he did not dispute the court’s ruling, he was concerned that the development had occurred just months before the 2027 general elections.

“The court of law is constituted to determine disputes according to the law. My concern is that three months before a general election, it is in the public interest to have certainty.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“It is not good to have too many uncertainties about candidates and parties a few weeks before a presidential election,” he said.

The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for 16 January 2027, while governorship elections and state assembly polls are billed to be held on 6 February the same year.

‘APC engineered it’

Mr Obi accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of “engineering” the court ruling and leadership dispute in the ADC.

“This instability is obviously engineered by the ruling party, just as they have done against me in the Labour Party and continue to do so to close down civic space for a robust campaign.

“It is also from the same rulebook that manufactures violence against us in our campaigns,” he claimed without evidence.

Mr Obi was the presidential candidate of the Labour Party in 2023.

PREMIUM TIMES recalls that the Labour Party had suffered an intense leadership crisis shortly after the 2023 election, which many believe resulted in Mr Obi’s defection to the ADC in December 2025.

‘Don’t undermine democracy’

In the post on X, Mr Obi suggested that the ruling party was clamping down on opposition parties and called for the protection of democratic principles, warning against any attempt to undermine voters’ freedom to freely and fairly choose their preferred candidates.

“One mark of democracy is that at all times, it is voters and not courts that choose leaders.

“The sustenance of democracy in Nigeria, in the midst of encroaching military rule in West Africa, should strengthen our resolve to protect opposition politics and not stamp out opposition parties,” he said.

The NDC candidate stressed that it was because of the importance of opposition to democracy that he promised to ensure that opposition parties and their candidates were not persecuted out of electoral contests.

“This is a time to strengthen our democracy by allowing the opposition to thrive,” he said.

APC reacts

When contacted by PREMIUM TIMES on Thursday night, the spokesperson of the APC, Felix Morka, rejected Mr Obi’s claim that the ruling party engineered the court ruling and the crisis in the ADC.

“How come every time that a court gives a decision that’s unfavourable to them, they blame APC, but when it’s in their favour they hail the rule of law and extol the judiciary,” Mr Morka said.

The APC spokesperson stressed that if the judgement was in favour of the ADC, opposition politicians would not have been blaming the ruling party for the court’s decision.

“Tomorrow, I’ll issue a statement on this (allegation),” he added.

World.title: EFCC investigates ex-banker over alleged N515 million diversion
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) is investigating a former bank operations manager, Obinna Nwaobi, over the alleged diversion of N515 million from an account belonging to a customer, DAHUA Paper Company.

According to a statement from EFCC spokesperson Dele Oyewale on Thursday, the commission received a petition at its Enugu zonal from the bank on 22 June, alleging that the money was withdrawn from the company’s Debt Service Reserve Account (DSRA) without authorisation.

The withdrawals, according to the petition, were made in three transactions of N200 million, N150 million and N165 million on 17 July 2024.

The bank alleged that the transactions were processed at its Okpara Avenue branch in Enugu using forged documents and authorised by Mr Nwaobi, who was then its head of operations.

It said the account had been reactivated in June 2024 but was not placed on a Post No Debit (PND) restriction, which should have prevented withdrawals.

The EFCC stated that preliminary investigations showed that the account was opened for the repayment of a Bank of Industry loan and was not meant for ordinary transactions.

It said withdrawals or transfers to third parties from such accounts require approval from the account officer, regional manager and credit monitoring team. The commission alleged that the N515 million transactions were carried out without the required approvals.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The investigation comes as Mr Nwaobi is also facing trial on charges of diverting $510,000 belonging to another customer of Access Bank, Lantern Gate Nigeria Limited.

He was arraigned before the Federal High Court in Enugu in November 2025 on nine charges of forgery and criminal diversion.

The EFCC alleged that the money was transferred to six different accounts without the customer’s approval. One of the charges accused Mr Nwaobi of inducing the bank to transfer the funds on the false pretence that Lantern Gate had authorised the transactions.

He pleaded not guilty to the charges. The court granted him bail in the sum of N250 million, with three sureties in like sum, and adjourned the case to 10, 11 and 12 March 2026 for trial.

The EFCC did not name the bank involved in the latest N515 million allegation, although it said the transactions were processed through its Okpara Avenue branch in Enugu.

The commission said Mr Nwaobi would be charged in connection with the latest allegation after investigations are concluded.

World.title: 2027: Ekiti PDP, SDP, APM, others unite for Tinubu
World.content:
By Rotimi Ojomoyela & Omeiza Ajayi

ADO-EKITI — President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign received a boost in Ekiti State yesterday, as governorship candidates of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Social Democratic Party. SDP, and Allied Peoples Movement, APM, declared support for his second-term bid.

The opposition politicians made their declarations at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally in Ado-Ekiti, where Governor Biodun Oyebanji pledged that the state would deliver at least 90 per cent of its votes for Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

Represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, the President urged Ekiti residents to improve on the 201,495 votes secured by the APC in the state in the 2023 presidential election, when the party won in all 16 local government areas.

Dignitaries at the rally included; Ondo State Governor, Dr Lucky Aiyedatiwa; Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu; Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele; and former Ekiti governors, Ayodele Fayose, Kayode Fayemi and Niyi Adebayo.

Shettima said the support of opposition candidates and former governors demonstrated the growing political strength of the APC in the state.

He also recalled that Oyebanji secured 85.74 per cent of the votes in the June governorship election, expressing optimism that the party could garner between 90 and 95 per cent in the presidential poll.

“With a total registered vote of 1,028,000, it is our hope, prayer and aspiration that from January 16, 2027, APC will garner 90 to 95 per cent of the votes cast in Ekiti State,” Shettima said.

Oyebanji promises 90%

Oyebanji described the rally as a demonstration of political unity, saying the support of former opposition candidates and former governors had strengthened the APC ahead of the presidential election.

He recalled that Tinubu, during his 2022 campaign, had urged Ekiti residents to vote for both him and Oyebanji, promising federal support for the state if elected.

According to the governor, the President has fulfilled that promise through what he described as unprecedented federal interventions in Ekiti since its creation 30 years ago.

Oyebanji pledged that the state would improve on its previous electoral performance and deliver at least 90 per cent of its votes for the President.

APC targets 800,000 votes

Also speaking, Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, challenged Ekiti to deliver 800,000 votes for Tinubu, representing about 90 per cent of the votes expected from the state.

He said: “Out of 1,080,000 votes, and PVC collected over 900,000, this is my request, and by extension, of course, of the President to you. We are looking for 800,000 votes, representing about 90 per cent.”

North firmly behind Tinubu — YARI

“We in Northern Nigeria, Bola is more of us than you in Ekiti, than you in Ondo, than you in Oyo, than you in Osun, than you in Lagos. Bola Ahmed supported our children, supported our people to become number one citizens in this country up to three times. So, we in the North, we are ready for Asiwaju 2027 and we are going to deliver him from A to Z,” he said.

APC lists reforms, projects

The APC National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, urged Nigerians to re-elect Tinubu, describing him as a performer and reformer.

He said his responsibility at the rally was to present the party’s candidates, from the President to the National Assembly and Ekiti State House of Assembly.

“We have a road from here to Akure constructed by Mr President. Our governor was elected on the basis of his performance. So also was the President,” he said.

He defended the administration’s tax reforms, saying small businesses and individuals earning below N100 million annually had been exempted from tax.

“Today, all those small ‘mama puts’ in the market, people who earn less than 100 million Naira per annum, don’t pay tax. Freeing legitimate money being earned by the lowest people in society,” he said.

Former Edo State Governor and Senator, Adams Oshiomhole, also canvassed support for Tinubu, citing interventions in education, workers’ welfare and security. He listed the expansion of educational institutions, student loans, additional support for workers and recruitment into the military and other security agencies.

Oshiomhole challenged opposition parties to explain what they would do differently, insisting that the administration’s policies were beginning to address the country’s economic challenges.

The PDP governorship candidate, Oluyede, said Oyebanji’s performance had brought political stakeholders together, adding that former opposition members were prepared to support Tinubu.

He urged Ekiti residents to vote for the President in January, saying Tinubu had been kind and generous to the state.

The SDP and APM governorship candidates, Isaac Alade and Chief Joseph Anifowose, respectively, also declared support for the APC presidential ticket.

Energy summit 2026: Lagos plans power reforms, infrastructure upgrade

Lagos State Government said the 2026 Lagos Energy Summit will focus on addressing structural challenges in the energy sector and developing practical solutions for stable, reliable and sustainable power supply across the state.

Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Biodun Ogunleye, disclosed this yesterday, during a press briefing on preparations for the summit, scheduled for November 10 to 12, 2026, with the theme, “Lagos Energy Evolution: Transforming the Future.”

Ogunleye, who was accompanied by the Permanent Secretary in the Ministry, Mrs Ibilola Kasumu, said the summit would bring together government officials, private investors, energy experts, innovators, academics and other stakeholders to develop strategies for improving the state’s energy landscape.

He said discussions would cover electricity sector reforms, energy efficiency, renewable energy, metering solutions and development of alternative energy sources.

Ogunleye also highlighted the growing importance of clean transportation, particularly adoption of Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, and electric vehicles, as Lagos explores cleaner and more sustainable urban mobility options.

Ogunleye added that the summit would showcase youth-led clean energy innovations, including sustainable projects and prototypes developed by secondary school students, providing an opportunity for engagement with industry stakeholders.

He added that discussions were ongoing between the federal and state governments to clarify regulatory responsibilities and strengthen Lagos State’s control over its energy infrastructure.

Ogunleye expressed optimism that the engagements would accelerate the state’s energy reforms and improve electricity access for residents and businesses.

Kasumu,in her address, said the summit would move beyond conventional discussions to address practical challenges confronting the energy sector.

“This summit is going to be different from the last one. It is not just going to be a talk shop. We are going to bring real problems to the table and look for solutions from different experts in this sector,” she said.

Kasumu explained that the gathering would involve stakeholders across the energy value chain, including regulatory agencies, electricity distribution companies, resellers and suppliers, to develop workable solutions to the state’s power challenges.

According to her, “the objective is to establish pathways towards reliable, round-the-clock electricity supply in Lagos, with the possibility of providing a model that could be replicated across the country.”

World.title: Terrorists abduct 10 in Ogun, demand 25m ransom
World.content:
Inspector General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu

By Adeola Badru

Families of 10 travellers, including a former member of the National Youth Service Corps NYSC, Olusoji Adedapo, have raised the alarm over their abduction at Ijebu Awa, a boundary community between Ogun and Oyo states, with the kidnappers demanding N25 million for their release.

Although unconfirmed reports indicated that some of the passengers were serving corps members, the police said none of those abducted was a corps member.

The 24-year-old Adedapo, reportedly completed his national service in Edo State last week and was travelling to Ibadan when the incident occurred on Tuesday.

His cousin, Adeseye Timilehin, who disclosed this, said the family had been thrown into distress, particularly as the kidnappers had issued a 24-hour deadline for payment of the ransom.

He explained that Dapo (Adedapo) had been updating the family about his journey until he sent a video showing the traffic situation on the road, which turned out to be their last communication.

Timilehin said the family learnt of the abduction shortly after 7pm on Tuesday, when one of the passengers reportedly escaped and contacted another family member.

He explained that Dapo was travelling with a friend, Tunde, with whom he had served during the NYSC programme, informing that Tunde was the only passenger who managed to escape the attack and alerted the family.

According to him: “On Tuesday morning, my cousin left Benin City, Edo State. He was posted to Edo State for NYSC and did his Passing-Out Ceremony last week. So, he was on his way back to Ibadan.

“He was still giving us updates about his journey. At some point, he posted that there was traffic in Benin. I have the videos of the traffic jam on my phone. By the time they were able to get out of the traffic, it was already 3pm.

“They kept telling the driver that it was already late and that they should return to Benin and continue the journey the following day, but the driver insisted on going. By the time they got to Ijebu at about 7pm, they were attacked by the bandits.”

He noted d that Tunde told him the driver had swerved into the bush and stopped immediately after the gunmen appeared in front of the vehicle, forcing the passengers to flee for safety.

“He told me that when the driver swerved into the bush and stopped, the bandits immediately jumped in front of their bus. He had to hide in the bush while the rest ran for safety and were captured. He was able to escape, but my brother and the others were taken away,” he said.

Timilehin said the family subsequently established contact with Tunde, who provided further details of the incident and confirmed that police officers had arrived at the scene, rescued him and taken him to a police station, where he spent the night.

He said the survivor also informed the family that a search party had been deployed into the surrounding forest that same night to locate the abducted passengers, but the operation did not yield any positive result.

Timilehin explained that on Wednesday morning, Dapo’s mother, his aunt and a family friend travelled from Ibadan to Awa-Ijebu, where they proceeded to the police station to obtain information about the whereabouts of the victims.

According to him, the family was informed that police officers and local vigilantes had launched a search operation in the forest immediately after the incident, but expressed concern that the operation had yet to yield any breakthrough.

He said the family was subsequently advised to return home and await contact from the kidnappers, while Dapo’s luggage was handed over to his relatives.

However, the family received its first call from the abductors while returning to the motor park, with the gunmen demanding N20 million as ransom.

Timilehin said Dapo’s mother broke down in tears during the conversation, pleading with the kidnappers that the family could not afford such an amount.

He said the family was also allowed to speak briefly with Dapo, thereby confirming that he was still alive.

“My aunt started crying and pleading with them that there was no way we could raise that amount of money. We were also able to speak with Dapo, and that was when we confirmed that he was still alive,” he said.

Timilehin said that shortly after they returned to Ibadan, the abductors called again and increased their demand from N20 million to N25 million.

He said the kidnappers ended the conversation after communicating the new amount and switched off the telephone number, leaving the family without further contact until Thursday morning.

He said: “The first call we received on Thursday was to Dapo’s mother, asking whether we had raised the money. They said, ‘If you don’t find the money, that means you have already released Dapo to us’, and then they ended the call.”

Timilehin further disclosed that the abductors later allowed Dapo to speak directly with his mother, during which he appealed to her to contact his elder brother and ask him to reach out to his friends for financial assistance.

He said Dapo subsequently called his telephone number directly, pleading with him to mobilise support from friends and other well-wishers to raise the ransom.

According to him, he explained to Dapo that the family was already making efforts to raise the money but had yet to secure any substantial amount.

“I told him that we were already trying to raise money, but that it had not amounted to something substantial. He dropped the call and called me again a few minutes later to ask how much I had been able to raise.

“I told him that we had only been able to raise N700,000. His voice was shaking throughout the conversation as he pleaded with me to contact everybody I could to help us raise the money,” he said.

The family said they received another call from Dapo later on Thursday evening, during which he again asked how much money had been raised. Timilehin said he told him that no additional funds had been secured since their previous conversation, prompting Dapo to end the call immediately. He added that the abductors subsequently called Dapo’s mother, asking her the same question.

The repeated calls have reportedly heightened the family’s distress, as they struggle to meet the huge ransom demand while anxiously hoping for their son’s safe return.

Timilehin, who described Dapo as both his cousin and elder brother, explained that they shared a particularly close bond because Dapo’s parents were his immediate siblings.

He said the family was making frantic efforts to mobilise financial support from friends, relatives and other well-meaning Nigerians, but the amount raised so far remained far below the kidnappers’ demand.

“The family is therefore appealing for urgent intervention to secure the release of Dapo and the other victims, particularly as the abductors have continued to contact us over the ransom without any indication that they are prepared to reduce their demand,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Ogun State Police Command has said investigation into the abduction is ongoing.

The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaeyi Ogunnaike, said the command was investigating the incident, adding that efforts were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and secure the release of the abducted victim

World.title: High Court Ruling: ADC heads to Appeal, insists Mark, Aregbesola remain party leaders
World.content:
By Clifford Ndujihe, Henry Umoru, Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Omeiza Ajayi, John Alechenu & Luminous Jannamike

The 2027 presidential election campaign was thrown into fresh controversy, yesterday, as a Federal High Court in Abuja sacked the Senator David Mark-led National Working Committee of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, declared its emergence illegal and nullified all actions taken by the leadership, including the nomination of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s presidential candidate.

The judgment by Justice Peter Lifu, has triggered reactions, with the ADC vowing to challenge the decision at the Court of Appeal, Atiku alleging a calculated attempt by the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, to cripple the opposition, and other political parties warning against actions capable of undermining democratic competition.

While the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, SAN, hailed the ruling as justice well served, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr. Peter Obi, urged the judiciary to protect democracy and ensure certainty in the electoral process.

The Coalition of United Political Parties, CUPP, accused the APC of using the judiciary to foist a one-party state on Nigeria, while the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and other opposition figures expressed concern over what they described as attempts to weaken political alternatives ahead of the polls.

The judgment came a day after Atiku held a campaign rally in Sokoto State, where thousands of supporters welcomed him as he began mobilising for the January 16, 2027, presidential election.

Atiku, whose name had earlier been published by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, as the ADC presidential candidate, has already picked former Rivers State governor, Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate.

The ruling, however, has cast uncertainty over the party’s leadership and presidential ticket, raising fresh questions about the legal and political battles that could shape the countdown to the general election.

Court upholds Gombe’s suit

Justice Lifu upheld the suit by Nafiu Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman (North-East) of the ADC, who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the party.

Gombe had argued that following the resignation of the former National Chairman, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he was entitled to assume the party’s leadership.

He consequently asked the court to nullify the actions of the Mark-led leadership and restrain Mark and Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola from parading themselves as National Chairman and National Secretary, respectively.

The suit listed the ADC, INEC, Mark, Aregbesola and Nwosu as defendants.

The plaintiff maintained that the emergence of the Mark-led leadership violated the party’s constitution and provisions of the Electoral Act.

Justice Lifu upheld his claims and granted the reliefs sought, declaring the Mark-led Caretaker Committee illegal and invalidating its actions.

The decision effectively invalidated the process through which the committee organised the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate.

The ADC has rejected the judgment and announced plans to appeal. Its National Welfare Secretary, Nkemakolam Ukandu, who was joined in the case as an interested party, said the party would challenge the verdict at the appellate court.

Atiku alleges plot to weaken opposition

Reacting in a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku accused the APC of exploiting the judgment to frustrate his presidential ambition and contain the ADC’s growing influence ahead of the 2027 elections.

He questioned the timing of the ruling, coming barely a day after the party’s rally in Sokoto, and alleged that it was intended to weaken his support base in the North and disrupt the opposition’s national mobilisation.

Atiku, however, insisted that the judgment would not derail his campaign or diminish his political appeal across the country.

“The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning. The people of Kebbi will have their say, and so will Nigerians across the country as our campaign moves forward,” he said.

Rejecting attempts to portray his candidacy as a Northern project, he said: “My roots are in Northern Nigeria, but my candidacy belongs to all Nigerians. There is a difference between being from the North and being a candidate only for the North. Hunger and hardship do not respect regional boundaries. Nigerians across the country are suffering under this government, and they deserve a leader with a credible plan to make life affordable again.

“The timing of this judgment is no coincidence. It is part of a strategy to weaken my support in the North and frustrate a campaign whose message is resonating across the country. But the ruling party’s greatest miscalculation is to assume that my support ends in the North. What we saw in Sokoto, what we will see in Kebbi and across the country, is the strength of a national movement,” he said.

He questioned why the leadership dispute had been reopened despite an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the Federal High Court, Abuja, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025.

According to him, “Why, after that judgment, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute? This is a calculated attempt to circumvent a subsisting judgment. We will challenge this judicial manoeuvre at the Court of Appeal.

“Our journey to rescue Nigeria from the hardship imposed by the APC government is a long one. Our Affordable Life campaign will continue because Nigerians deserve relief from this crushing cost-of-living crisis,” he said, adding “there is no shaking.”

Judgment cannot sack Mark, Aregbesola – ADC Campaign Council

The ADC Presidential Campaign Council also rejected the judgment, insisting that it could not override an earlier decision of a court of coordinate jurisdiction which, according to it, affirmed the emergence of Mark and Aregbesola as the party’s leaders.

In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the council recalled that Justice Liman had examined the leadership dispute and upheld the transfer of leadership from Nwosu to Mark.

It said the July 2, 2025, stakeholders’ meeting preceded the party’s National Executive Council meeting of July 29, 2025, at which Mark and Aregbesola emerged as National Chairman and National Secretary, respectively. The meeting, it added, was monitored by INEC.

“The leadership question has already been subjected to judicial scrutiny by a court of coordinate jurisdiction. It is, therefore, untenable to suggest that a subsequent pronouncement can simply erase or displace an existing judicial decision without due regard to the principles governing judicial authority and the administration of justice.

“The ADC legal team is already taking steps to seek appropriate interim relief, including a stay of execution where legally applicable, and will subsequently pursue an appeal against the judgment.

“Rather than confront the ADC politically and through the ballot box, the APC appears increasingly desperate to deploy every available instrument to frustrate the opposition and undermine its growing electoral momentum,” it alleged.

It also recalled that an earlier judgment by Justice Lifu declaring the ADC deregistered was subsequently set aside by the Court of Appeal, raising concerns about what it described as pressure and political interference in the latest proceedings.

“We consider it imperative that the independence, impartiality and integrity of the judiciary must never be compromised or sacrificed on the altar of partisan political interests,” Ologbondiyan said.

The council urged party members, candidates and supporters to remain calm, insisting that the legal setback would not stop its campaign.

“The ADC is not distracted. The campaign continues. The struggle for a better Nigeria remains unstoppable,” it declared.

ADC warns APC against setting Nigeria on fire

The ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, also accused the APC of using the judiciary to cripple opposition parties and undermine democratic competition.

In a statement, the party said: “We have reasons to believe that the judgment had long been written on this case. The Sokoto rally was simply a trigger that stampeded its delivery.

“Do these people understand what they are playing with? This is not about Atiku Abubakar or David Mark. It is about the democratic rights of Nigerians to freely choose their own leaders. It is about the rights of thousands of candidates to participate in a democratic process,” the statement said.

Don’t undermine democracy, Obi urges judiciary

On his part, Obi expressed concern over the judgment, urging Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive.

In a statement posted on his X platform, the NDC presidential candidate said he respected the authority of the courts to determine disputes but was concerned about the uncertainty the ruling could create with the 2027 elections approaching.

“I do not challenge the ruling of the court. The court of law is constituted to determine disputes according to the law. My concern is that three months before a general election, it is in the public interest to have certainty,” he said.

Obi warned that uncertainty surrounding political parties and their candidates close to an election could undermine the electoral process and restrict the space for opposition campaigns.

It’s justice well served – Keyamo

However, Keyamo welcomed the judgment, declaring that the law had taken its course and dismissed allegations that the ruling was politically motivated.

In his reaction, the minister said: “You cannot invade a political party owned and built by Nigerians, hijack it with the connivance of a so-called National Chairman without a prior meeting and approval of a mini National Convention or the National Executive Committee.”

He accused those behind the takeover of attempting to blame the ruling party for problems arising from their actions.

Keyamo added, “Sorry, but the law is decided on facts and evidence, rather than sentiments and outrage by a group of people.”

Dismissing concerns that the judgment threatened democracy, he said the ADC remained a political party with other members and leaders.

“It is not only when a certain Atiku Abubakar contests the Presidency that democracy is not in danger. The ADC as a party is well and alive and populated by people and original leaders who are no less Nigerians than a David Mark and his illegal band of marauders,” he added.

CUPP alleges plot to impose one-party state

The Coalition of United Political Parties condemned the judgment, describing it as part of what it called a coordinated attempt to eliminate viable opposition parties and impose a one-party state.

In a statement by its spokesperson’s office, CUPP accused the APC-led establishment of using judicial technicalities to disqualify opposition candidates and overturn party leadership structures.

It said: “CUPP views this controversial judgment not as an isolated legal dispute, but as part of a well-choreographed, state-sponsored onslaught aimed at wiping out viable opposition parties and turning Nigeria into a one-party state.

“It is deeply tragic that sections of the judiciary have seemingly abandoned their role as the last line of defence for the common man, choosing instead to act as accomplices in this daylight robbery of the electorate’s mandate.”

Ameh cautions opposition against division

The NDC senatorial candidate for Kogi East, Chief Peter Ameh, cautioned opposition politicians against celebrating the judgment, arguing that political division would ultimately benefit the APC.

He said the ruling party would be pleased to see opposition parties fighting one another instead of concentrating on the task of challenging it at the polls.

“The APC who is the ultimate beneficiary of this judgment will be happy keeping any party in the opposition weakened, they do not care which party logo you wave. They want us fighting each other so we never notice the real game being played against all of us,” he said.

Ameh added: “Before anyone starts dancing, remember: today’s victory for one camp is tomorrow’s weapon against another. The same forces that can erase one candidate or one leadership structure can just as easily turn on yours when it becomes convenient. Political affiliation is not a shield.
