World.title: Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh
World.content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — High Chief Peter Ameh, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) senatorial candidate for Kogi East, has warned opposition parties against celebrating the court judgment that sacked the David Mark-led National Working Committee of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and nullified Atiku Abubakar’s candidacy.

Ameh said the ruling should not be seen as a victory for any political camp, warning that the All Progressives Congress (APC) stood to benefit from divisions within the opposition.

He spoke in Abuja on Thursday, urging opposition parties to resist attempts to turn the judgment into an opportunity for political infighting.

According to him, the APC would be comfortable with any opposition party being weakened, regardless of the party’s identity or political affiliation.

“The APC, which is the ultimate beneficiary of this judgment, will be happy keeping any party in the opposition weakened. They do not care which party logo you wave. They want us fighting each other so we never notice the real game being played against all of us,” he said.

Ameh cautioned that what might appear to be a victory for one faction today could become a tool against another political group tomorrow.

“Before anyone starts dancing, remember: today’s victory for one camp is tomorrow’s weapon against another. The same forces that can erase one candidate or one leadership structure can just as easily turn on yours when it becomes convenient. Political affiliation is not a shield,” he said.

He added: “Stay alert. This is not a win for any side. It is a warning.”

The NDC candidate urged opposition parties to channel their energy towards demanding free, fair and credible elections, rather than engaging in disputes over political leadership and candidacies.

He also criticised the APC-led administration, accusing it of failing to deliver good governance to Nigerians over the past 11 years.

“For 11 years, this APC government has failed to provide good governance to Nigerians. We must collectively work to bring an end to its rule. APC is the problem,” Ameh declared.

World.title: UN, EU, Germany woo investors to Borno
World.content:
…Zulum pledges business-friendly reforms

By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

The United Nations (UN), European Union (EU), German Government and other development partners are supporting efforts to attract private investment to Borno State to create jobs and help displaced families rebuild their livelihoods.

At the third Borno State Private Sector Engagement and Investment Roundtable in Abuja on Thursday, representatives of the UN, EU and German Embassy pledged continued support for the state’s recovery through private sector investment.

The Governor Babagana Zulum-led administration initiated the roundtable series with a meeting in Lagos, focusing on financing bankable projects and supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

The second edition was held in Kano, with emphasis on agriculture, livestock, fisheries and infrastructure.

More than 50 prospective investors attended the Abuja roundtable.

The representative of the UN Resident Coordinator’s Office in Nigeria, Thembekile Dube-Nanbe, urged development partners to translate the investment initiative into concrete action.

“Let us identify viable investment opportunities, mobilise capital, establish lasting partnerships, and commit to measurable results,” Dube-Nanbe said.

The EU Head of Human Development, Laila Ben Amor Mathieu, said the Union had supported Borno through its most difficult years by providing humanitarian assistance and backing stabilisation and recovery efforts.

“Grants and public budgets alone will not finance recovery at the scale Borno needs. Private capital must play its part, and the role of us partners is to make that possible,” Mathieu said.

She said investors could support the proposed Borno State Durable Solutions Trust Fund or pursue commercially viable projects backed by incentives, including access to land, industrial hubs and tax measures.

Mathieu urged businesses to identify projects for further consideration, partner with local companies and create opportunities for women and young people.

“Borno is becoming an investment story. The European Union is proud to be part of it,” she said.

The Head of Development Cooperation at the German Embassy, Dr Karen Jansen, commended Governor Zulum for restoring communities, rebuilding infrastructure and public services, and opening the state’s economy to investors.

She urged investors to sustain their commitments as the economy grows, assuring the state of Germany’s continued support.

“Mobilising private sector investment, including through blended finance, will be essential to complement development cooperation and support Borno’s sustainable reconstruction,” Jansen said.

Governor Zulum, who was represented by his Chief of Staff, Dr Babagana Mustapha Mallumbe, urged private investors to take advantage of business opportunities in the state, assuring them of government support and simpler administrative procedures.

He said improvements in security and ongoing reforms were helping Borno move from emergency humanitarian assistance towards economic recovery.

The governor invited businesses to invest in commercial farming, livestock production, fisheries and manufacturing, while encouraging financial institutions to expand credit facilities for small businesses.

“Government’s role is to build the foundation, establish the security, and create the regulatory framework. But the private sector is the ultimate engine of wealth creation, job opportunities, and lasting prosperity,” he said.

Zulum said the Borno State Investment Promotion Agency was simplifying procedures for investors, supported by land administration reforms, fiscal incentives and public-private partnership frameworks designed to protect investments.

World.title: Benue SEMA raises alarm over rising snakebites, treats two IDPs
World.content:
Snake

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The Benue State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA) has expressed concern over rising cases of snakebites across the state, warning that the incidents are increasingly affecting farmers, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable residents.

The concern followed two recent snakebite incidents involving a 35-year-old man, Isaac Shula, and a 19-year-old girl, Mbapuun Tyoshio, both residents of Daudu 1 IDP camp in Guma Local Government Area of the state.

The victims were reportedly bitten by snakes while working on their farms and have since been referred to the Benue State University Teaching Hospital (BSUTH), Makurdi, where they are receiving medical attention under the care of Benue SEMA.

The agency’s Health Focal Person, Dr Amos Dzungwe, said snakebite cases had continued to increase across the state, affecting not only displaced persons but also farmers and other vulnerable populations.

He said the agency had received numerous requests for medical intervention from different parts of the state, reflecting growing concern over the incidents.

According to him, two snakebite patients were successfully discharged within the last two weeks, while others remained on admission and were receiving treatment.

Dzungwe warned against delays in seeking medical attention, stressing that late presentation at health facilities could result in severe complications and poor health outcomes.

He urged members of the public to seek immediate medical attention at appropriate health facilities whenever snakebite incidents occur.

Meanwhile, Benue SEMA has urged the public to disregard what it described as misleading reports and politically motivated narratives surrounding snakebite incidents in the state, particularly those involving IDPs.

The agency maintained that health emergencies and the lives of vulnerable citizens should not be subjected to political manipulation.

It reaffirmed its commitment to providing timely medical assistance to snakebite victims and others affected by emergencies, irrespective of their status or location.

World.title: LASTMA inducts 100 volunteers to tackle Yuletide traffic
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) has inducted more than 100 volunteers into its LASTMA Mayors traffic advocacy network to support efforts to manage anticipated traffic congestion during the Yuletide and year-end ‘Detty December’ celebrations.

The investiture and induction ceremony, held at the agency’s headquarters in Lagos, was part of efforts to strengthen community participation in traffic management, promote voluntary compliance with traffic regulations and support enforcement officers along busy roads.

Speaking at the event, LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, said managing traffic in Lagos required collective responsibility rather than reliance on government enforcement alone.

He said the newly inducted volunteers would strengthen public enlightenment campaigns and support field operations through grassroots advocacy, voluntary interventions and targeted sensitisation.

“Sustainable mobility governance relies on collective ownership, shared accountability, and the active participation of every citizen.

“The enlistment of these LASTMA Mayors will substantially reinforce our public enlightenment architecture and augment field operations through voluntary interventions, grassroots advocacy, and targeted sensitisation,” Bakare-Oki said.

He described the volunteers as community ambassadors whose closeness to residents, commercial transport operators and market associations would help promote road discipline, particularly during the festive season.

The LASTMA boss also appealed to Christian and Islamic leaders to use their platforms to reinforce road safety messages among their congregations.

“We are soliciting the strategic partnership of religious leaders to deploy their moral authority towards amplifying our road safety campaign.

“Clerics, imams, and pastors should consistently incorporate messages of responsible motoring, pedestrian awareness, and strict adherence to traffic laws into their sermons and fellowship gatherings,” he said.

Bakare-Oki cautioned motorists against dangerous practices, including driving against traffic, popularly known as one-way, excessive speeding, reckless overtaking and indiscriminate parking.

He also urged vehicle owners to ensure proper maintenance of their brakes, tyres, steering systems and lights before embarking on journeys.

“The commercial excitement and social festivities associated with December must not degenerate into traffic indiscipline or preventable road tragedies,” he said, urging motorists to exercise patience and restraint.

Also speaking, LASTMA’s Director of Traffic Advocacy and Special Mayors, Mr Awoyemi Jimmy, assured residents that the agency would sustain operational surveillance and strategic deployment of officers along critical traffic corridors throughout the holiday season.

The Coordinator of the State Mayors of Traffic (SMT), Mr Tajudeen Othman, pledged that the newly inducted volunteers would discharge their responsibilities with integrity and discipline, using their community networks to complement the state’s traffic management efforts.

World.title: Soludo seeks partnership with pharmacists to strengthen healthcare
World.content:
By Nwabueze Okonkwo

ONITSHA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for a strategic partnership between the state government and the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) to strengthen the healthcare system and improve access to quality pharmaceutical services.

Soludo made the call on Wednesday while declaring open the ongoing four-day 99th Annual National Delegate Conference of the society in Awka, stressing that pharmacists played a critical role in building an effective healthcare system.

Describing the gathering, tagged ‘Ijele 2026’, as historic, the governor said his administration had prioritised human capital development, education and healthcare.

He cited the introduction of free education from kindergarten to Senior Secondary School Three (SS3), as well as free antenatal care in government hospitals, as part of his administration’s interventions in the sectors.

Soludo also said his government had revamped the state’s primary healthcare system, disclosing that more than 250,000 expectant mothers had benefited from zero-cost antenatal care, while over 950 free Caesarean Section operations had been performed.

“To further solidify Anambra’s position as the nation’s premier pharma hub, let me also inform you that work on the development of the state-of-the-art Pharmaceutical Hub in Oba, alongside the upcoming Coordinated Wholesale Centre slated for delivery early next year, is currently ongoing in the state,” he said.

The governor urged the PSN leadership to work closely with the state government to enforce safety standards in pharmaceutical operations and tackle the circulation of counterfeit drugs.

He also challenged the society to address unethical practices within the profession, particularly the activities of illegal drug outlets operating under the guise of licensed pharmacies.

Earlier, the President of the PSN, Pharm. Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, expressed appreciation to Soludo for his support for the pharmaceutical profession and the decision to host the society’s flagship national conference in Anambra.

Ibrahim said the conference, themed, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact”, was designed to strengthen collaboration among stakeholders and promote the contribution of pharmacy to national development.

He commended the governor’s vision and leadership, recalling that his earlier prediction of Soludo’s electoral victory had come to pass.

World.title: FHC’s Lifu Overrules FHC’s Lima, Voids 1,503 ADC Candidates; Who Will INEC Obey?
World.content:
*Sacks David Mark-led exco

*Atiku: It’s panic from Sokoto rally

Chuks Okocha, Alex Enumah, Sunday Aborisade in Abuja and Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano

In a ruling that has shocked the whole country and put democracy in obvious danger, Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, yesterday, sacked the Senator David Mark-led Exco of African Democratic Congress (ADC), some 71 days to the presidential election.

By the ruling, Lifu effectively voided the candidacies of no fewer than 1,503 people, including the presidential candidate of ADC, Atiku Abubakar, for the sake of one man, Nafiu Bala Gombe.



Interestingly, on July 2, 2026, Hon. Justice Musa S. Liman also of the Federal High Court (FHC) in Abuja delivered a judgment in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025 (Hon. Leke Joseph Abejide v. African Democratic Congress & 4 Ors.) regarding the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

Justice Lima had dismissed the suit then, determining the court lacked jurisdiction over an internal party affair and that the plaintiff lacked standing and failed to exhaust internal remedies of the party.



Justice Lima then directed INEC to recognize the party leadership and engage with them, while awarding costs against the plaintiff.

Justice Lifu, by his judgment yesterday is effectively overruling Justice Lima’s (worthy of note is both Justices are of equal and coordinate jurisdiction) July judgment which declared David Mark led Exco as legitimate, valid and directed INEC to recognise it.

Four months after Justice Lima’s directive to INEC to recognise Mark-led Exco, Justice Lifu has declared that same Exco as existing in contravention of the party’s constitution.



Atiku in his immediate reaction, said the latest case raised serious legal concerns: “Why, after that judgment, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute?

Before Justice Lifu’s ruling, ADC had on its list 28 governorship candidates, 108 senatorial hopefuls, 352 House of Representatives standard bearers, and 1,015 Houses of Assembly picks for the 2027 general election.

However, with the Lifu ruling, especially against its timing, the fate of 1,503 people have been affected in the most egregious manner, leaving them in a quandary, and the entire nation in speculation over what might happen next as the country inches towards the 2027 elections.



The bigger question on the lips of the public is: which of these two conflicting judgments will INEC now comply with?

Lifu, in the judgement, held that the emergence of Mark as National Chairman of ADC as well as the other members of his executive violated the constitution and the guidelines of the party.

A former National Deputy Chairman of ADC, Gombe, had approached the Federal High Court, Abuja, to challenge the emergence of the Mark-led executive of ADC.



The plaintiff in the suit marked: FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, claimed that following the resignation of former National Chairman of ADC, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he (Gombe) was qualified to assume the party’s leadership.

He specifically prayed the court to restrain the Mark-led executive from parading themselves as leaders of the party, on the grounds that the process that produced them violated constitutional provisions as well as ADC’s guidelines.

Those sued included ADC, Mark, Rauf Aregbesola, Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), and Nwosu, as first to fifth defendants, respectively.



However, the defendants asked the court to dismiss the suit for being incompetent and lacking merit, explaining that the suit as constituted fell within the internal matters of a political party, and therefore outside the jurisdiction of the court.

Delivering judgement in the matter, yesterday, Lifu disagreed with the defendants, holding that their emergence as executives of ADC did not follow the due process of the law.



The judge subsequently granted the reliefs sought by the plaintiff and declared as unconstitutional, unlawful, null and void, all actions and decisions taken by the Mark-led executive on behalf of the party.

The ruling came with grave implications, as the congresses and convention that produced former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and other candidates vying for elective offices both at the state and federal levels were conducted by the Mark-led national executive.

Atiku: It’s Panic from Sokoto Rally

Atiku condemned the court judgement that removed the Mark leadership of ADC, saying it is a panic response to Wednesday’s Sokoto rally by ADC, which attracted a massive crowd of supporters.

Describing it as a calculated attempt to weaken ADC and frustrate his candidacy, Atiku, in a statement by Director of Strategic Communication of ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, said the timing of the judgement was telling.



According to the statement, “It came barely a day after a mammoth crowd turned out in Sokoto to welcome him and attend the launch of the ADC campaign.

“The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again.

“What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning. The people of Kebbi will have their say, and so will Nigerians across the country as our campaign moves forward.”



Atiku stated, “My roots are in Northern Nigeria, but my candidacy belongs to all Nigerians. There is a difference between being from the north and being a candidate only for the north.

“Hunger and hardship do not respect regional boundaries. Nigerians across the country are suffering under this government, and they deserve a leader with a credible plan to make life affordable again.



“The timing of this judgement is no coincidence. It is part of a strategy to weaken my support in the north and frustrate a campaign whose message is resonating across the country.

“But the ruling party’s greatest miscalculation is to assume that my support ends in the north. What we saw in Sokoto, what we will see in Kebbi and across the country, is the strength of a national movement.”



Atiku said the judgement also raised serious legal concerns, stressing, “Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court had already dismissed the challenge to the David Mark-led leadership in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025.

“The court upheld the defendants’ objections on jurisdiction, standing and the failure to exhaust internal party remedies, and resolved the substantive issues in their favour.



“Why, after that judgement, was another case filed to reopen the same dispute? This is a calculated attempt to circumvent a subsisting judgement. We will challenge this judicial manoeuvre at the Court of Appeal.”

Atiku urged ADC supporters to remain calm and law-abiding and not to let the judgement weaken the momentum generated in Sokoto, saying the campaign train is already in Kebbi and would continue across the country.



He stated, “Our journey to rescue Nigeria from the hardship imposed by the APC government is a long one. Our Affordable Life campaign will continue because Nigerians deserve relief from this crushing cost-of-living crisis.

“We urge our supporters to remain resolute, take our message from house to house and door to door, and stay peaceful and focused. There is no shaking.”

ADC: APC Wants to Set Nigeria on Fire



ADC described yesterday’s judgement by Lifu as another desperate attempt to cripple the opposition and deny Nigerians the right to choose their leaders in the forthcoming general election.

The party asked its members to remain calm as the court judgement would be appealed

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, ADC said the timing of the judgement, barely 24 hours after the massive turnout at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Sokoto, exposed the growing desperation of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).



Abdullahi stated, “We have reasons to believe that the judgement had long been written on this case. The Sokoto rally was simply a trigger that stampeded its delivery.

“Yesterday, Nigerians came out in their hundreds of thousands to demonstrate their support for the ADC and our promise of making life affordable for them.



“Today, they are being told that the party that they support and the candidates that they have supported at all levels could be erased by the stroke of a reckless judicial pen.”

ADC questioned whether those behind what it called a flawed judgement had considered its far-reaching implications for the country, warning that the attempt to invalidate the party’s leadership could affect thousands of candidates contesting elections at the local, state and federal levels.



Abdullahi stated, “Do these people understand what they are playing with? This is not about Atiku Abubakar or David Mark. It is about the democratic rights of Nigerians to freely choose their own leaders. It is about the rights of thousands of candidates to participate in a democratic process.”



ADC maintained that the judgement was legally indefensible and would be challenged through every available judicial process.

It explained, “Our objection is particularly anchored on the subsisting judgement of Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, delivered on 2 July 2026 in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025, which affirmed the legitimacy of the David Mark-led NWC and directed INEC to recognise the leadership.



‘’It is a settled principle of Nigerian jurisprudence that a court of coordinate jurisdiction cannot sit on appeal over, review, vary or nullify the subsisting judgement of another court of equal jurisdiction.

“The ADC, therefore, rejects any consequential orders founded on a determination that appears to disregard these fundamental legal principles. However, we await the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the said judgement to ascertain its precise terms, scope, and operative orders.



“We have seen this script before. When they are scared that the opposition is gathering steam, they use their judges in the courts to influence legally indefensible judgements.

“But the millions of Nigerians that are hungry and waiting for them at the ballot box see right through them and will not sit down in silence while our democracy is taken away by the courts.”



ADC warned APC against pursuing a dangerous attempt to eliminate political competition through judicial controversies.

Abdullahi told THISDAY last night that the party would file for stay of execution of the judgement and also file appeal to the Court of Appeal against it, while reassuring that efforts to frustrate ADC would continue to fail.

Kwankwasiyya: Democracy at Risk

The Kwankwasiyya Movement expressed concern over the Federal High Court judgement, saying democracy is at risk.

In a statement by the spokesman of the group, Dr. Habeeb Mohammed, in Kano, it lamented the court ruling, including the process that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 elections.



The movement said while it recognised the constitutional authority of the judiciary to adjudicate disputes, persistent legal battles over opposition party leadership and candidate nominations were creating uncertainty for opposition parties ahead of 2027.

According to the statement, Nigeria’s democracy must be built on political pluralism, institutional independence, equal treatment before the law, and protection of citizens’ rights to associate and participate in the electoral process.



The Kwankwasiyya Movement acknowledged ADC’s intention to appeal the judgement and urged all parties to pursue legal remedies peacefully, allowing the appellate process to determine outstanding questions without intimidation or political interference.

It further warned that uncertainty around the ADC leadership and nominations should not lead to disenfranchisement of party members and millions of Nigerians expecting a competitive 2027 election.



The statement said, “Democracy cannot thrive where political competition is weakened by institutional uncertainty, selective application of the law or the perception that state institutions are being deployed for partisan advantage.

“Our democracy must be protected. Opposition voices must be respected. The rule of law must prevail.”

CD: Nigeria Drifting Towards Dictatorship

Campaign for Democracy (CD) warned that Nigeria risked sliding into dictatorship, describing the court ruling sacking the ADC leadership as a serious threat to opposition politics and democratic competition.

The organisation, in a statement, alleged that the judgement, coming barely 72 days before the January 16, 2027 general election, could effectively undermine the participation of opposition candidates and deny Nigerians the opportunity to make meaningful choices at the polls.



It expressed concern that the ruling, represented a dangerous development for Nigeria’s multiparty democracy.

CD questioned the implications of a situation in which disputes involving opposition parties could have far-reaching consequences for their participation in an imminent general election.



The organisation queried, “Is this still democracy? Is this still a country where the people choose? Or have we now entered the season where presidents are selected in courtrooms and the ballot box is only for show?”

The group stated that the credibility of any government should be determined by its performance and its willingness to submit itself to the judgment of voters rather than by developments capable of weakening its political opponents.



It challenged President Bola Tinubu and the ruling APC to allow Nigerians to assess his administration at the ballot box, insisting that electoral competition should not be compromised by controversies surrounding opposition parties.

It asked, “Why are you afraid of Atiku? Why are you afraid of the ADC? Why are you afraid of a free contest?”

Group Cautions Judiciary, APC Against Endangering Democracy Through Courts

A coalition of Atiku Abubakar friends under the auspices of United Friends of Atiku Abubakar cautioned the judiciary and APC against endangering democracy through the courts.

Addressing a press conference at the ADC national secretariat in Abuja, the national coordinator of the group, Alhaji Aliyu Audi, said they were moved by the court judgement by Lifu, despite a subsisting court order.



According to Audi, “We are of the belief that we are all witnessing a dangerous escalation of the absurd in our nation.

“We are issuing a stern and unequivocal warning: if this blatant institutional takeover by the incumbent administration continues, we can see that we are staring at the imminent breakdown of democracy in Nigeria.

“Our intervention today is not a declaration that political parties, leaders, or candidates are above the law, neither is it an argument that the judiciary has abdicated its responsibility to adjudicate disputes. Rather, it is a solemn declaration that the administration of justice is being weaponised to execute a political agenda.



“We must ask a fundamental, grave question:

What is the value of an election if the options available to the electorate can be sustainably predetermined before election day through engineered institutional and judicial controversies?”

World.title: Tinubu Departs Abuja Today for Two-state Visit to Akwa Ibom, Rivers
World.content:
* Ekiti promises 90% votes for president at rally

Deji Elumoye, Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja and Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado Ekiti

President Bola Tinubu will depart Abuja today, November 6, for a two-state visit to Akwa Ibom and Rivers states. This was announced in a release by the presidential Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga.

The announcement came as Vice President Kashim Shettima, yesterday, said Tinubu had kept faith with his promise to rebuild Nigeria through bold and necessary economic reforms.



Shettima spoke in Ado-Ekiti, the Ekiti State capital, during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally, where the people declared that 90 per cent of their votes would be for the president.

Onanuga stated, in the release, that Tinubu will first visit Uyo, the Akwa Ibom State capital, to inaugurate landmark projects completed by the Governor Umo Eno administration, and attend a political rally.



To give the president a rousing reception, Eno declared today a work-free day in the state.

Among the projects Tinubu is scheduled to inaugurate in Uyo are the new International Terminal Building, the International Airport Hospital, and the Ibom Aviation Village, all located at the Victor Attah International Airport.

The president will also inaugurate the Airport-Okopedi Road in Nsit Atai and Okobo local government areas, and Ring Road 3, linking Idoro Road to Ikot Ekpene Road through Uyo and Ibiono Ibom.



Other projects include the AKWA-GIS Office Complex, Command and Control Centre, and ARISE Palm Resort.

On Saturday, Tinubu will leave for Port Harcourt to take part in the APC rally.

The rally will be his third, out of the proposed 12, since he flagged off the re-election campaign in Kaduna last month.

The visits will give the president the opportunity to engage with political stakeholders, party members, and supporters, while emphasising unity, political stability, and a shared commitment to national progress.

Shettima: Tinubu Has Kept His Promise of Rebuilding Nigeria Through Bold Reforms

Shettima, yesterday, said Tinubu had remained faithful to his promise to rebuild Nigeria through brave and crucial economic reforms.

That was as the people of Ekiti State declared that 90 per cent of the total registered voters in the state would be delivered for the president in the forthcoming presidential poll.



Meanwhile, opposition figures in the state, including the candidates of Social Democratic Party (SDP), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the last governorship election, declared their support for the president, citing the positive impact of the federal government’s interventions in Ekiti.

Shettima acknowledged the sacrifices made by the citizens, saying the people are already reaping the benefits of the administration’s tough decisions.



He stated that while the commitments were being fulfilled, the Tinubu government had returned to account for the work already done as well as the tasks ahead.

He said, “We know the sacrifices you have made, and we are beginning to reap the benefits of those difficult decisions. His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has remained faithful to the commitments we made to you.



“We have begun to fulfil those commitments, and we have returned to account for the work already done and the tasks that remain. We have come to seek the renewal of your mandate, to continue the partnership we began and to finish the work you entrusted to us.”

The vice president appealed to the people of Ekiti to replicate the mass support they gave the president in the 2023 presidential poll, assuring them that the administration’s commitment to their welfare “extends to healthcare and electricity, two necessities upon which the dignity of everyday life depends”.



He cited the conversion of the former State Specialist Hospital in Ikole-Ekiti into a Federal Medical Centre to complement the Federal Teaching Hospital in Ido-Ekiti, as part of efforts by the Tinubu administration to revamp healthcare.

On electricity, Shettima said, “We have also turned our attention to your electricity needs. Equipment has arrived for the substations at Ilupeju and Ijesa-Isu, alongside ongoing work on the Ikere switching station.



“We have approved additional electricity distribution lines and transferred regulatory authority over your intrastate electricity market to Ekiti State. We understand what these interventions mean to you.”

He lauded the transformation of Ekiti State into an electoral powerhouse, stating that the state “has become a litmus test for elections in Nigeria”.



Shettima added, “You lead the nation in speaking with a voice that deserves respect and reflection. We have returned to acknowledge that voice and thank you for your warmth.”

He justified his observation with the recent re-election of Governor Biodun Oyebanji under the APC platform.

Shettima also spoke on efforts by the Tinubu administration to build roads in the state, stating that work has proceeded on the Akure–Ikere–Ado-Ekiti road, while reconstruction has begun on the Itawure–Aramoko–Ado-Ekiti road.



“Other federal road interventions, from Aramoko and Ijero to Ifaki, Oye, Ikole and Omuo, are at different stages,” he stated.

He added, “Our duty is to see the work through. Every unfinished road is a responsibility awaiting fulfilment.”

On education, the vice president stated that the Federal University of Technology and Environmental Sciences was established in Iyin-Ekiti, while students at Ekiti State University and Bamidele Olumilua University received education loans through NELFUND.



Recalling the new ICT Experience Centre inaugurated at Ekiti State University through TETFund support, Shettima said the obligation of the Tinubu administration “is to make sure that poverty does not shut the classroom door against any child”, especially in Ekiti, the land of professors.



He listed other federal government interventions in the state, including agricultural input programmes that have brought fertilisers and planting materials within the reach of participating farmers.

Shettima restated the commitment of Tinubu to rebuilding the country, pointing out, however, that “the authority to continue with it rests with the Nigerian electorate”.

He stated, “We seek your mandate to complete the work we have begun, fulfil the commitments we have made and carry this mission to its conclusion.”



Shettima departed Ado-Ekiti with a clear and emphatic message from the people, who declared that 90 per cent of their votes will be for Tinubu in the forthcoming election.

They attributed their support to massive infrastructure projects embarked upon by the federal government across the state, saying they have transformed lives and communities, creating a strong case for a second term for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket.



In a significant show of bipartisan solidarity, the governorship candidates of PDP, APM, and SDP in the last governorship election in the state pledged their support for the president.

In separate remarks, the opposition candidates affirmed that they would mobilise their supporters behind APC to ensure the victory of Tinubu.



They emphasised that their commitment went beyond party lines and was rooted in the unity and continued progress of Ekiti State.

Oyebanji described the decision of opposition figures in the state to declare support for Tinubu as clear evidence of the positive impact of the federal government’s interventions in Ekiti.



He said the people of Ekiti would reciprocate the president’s efforts by delivering an overwhelming mandate in the next general election.

The governor declared, “We will use our votes to say thank you to a president who has given approval for so many federal roads and other critical projects in Ekiti State. The people of Ekiti will return the president with no less than 90 per cent of registered voters.”

APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, said at the rally that Tinubu’s achievements deserved to be rewarded with a second term.



Yilwatda stated that the administration had eased the burden on small business owners who previously struggled under the weight of unaffordable taxes.

He said, “Unlike in the past, when small business owners were being strangled by taxes they could not afford, the coming of President Tinubu has checked that excess.



“The NELFUND student loan scheme, the construction of roads, the establishment and upgrading of federal institutions, and other interventions are clear manifestations of the President’s goodwill and his determination to improve the lives of Nigerians.”

Director-General of the campaign council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, urged the people of Ekiti to mobilise full support for the president’s re-election.



Yari stated, “President Bola Tinubu has promised to bring even greater development to Ekiti State if given the opportunity to serve a second term. The people of the South-west must demonstrate their love and support by voting massively for him.

“Interestingly, many in the north already regard President Tinubu as one of their own, more than a southerner. The South-west must not be left behind in showing appreciation.”

World.title: US Midterms: Rubio Weighs Leaving Trump Administration as Oil Price Slumps
World.content:
Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja and Sunday Ehigiator in Lagos

United States Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, is considering leaving President Donald Trump’s administration following the Republican Party’s crushing defeat in the midterm elections, as political uncertainty in Washington and prospects of a diplomatic resolution to the war with Iran weigh on global oil prices.



People familiar with the matter said Rubio and his advisers were reviewing options for his political future, although he had yet to make a final decision on whether to resign from his positions as America’s top diplomat and national security adviser.

According to Bloomberg, which first reported the development, Rubio had spoken with officials at the White House about stepping down but was asked to remain in the administration. There is, however, no timetable for any possible departure.

The White House and State Department dismissed the report, describing it as false.

Assistant Secretary of State for Global Public Affairs, Dylan Johnson, said, “This is complete and total fake news based on the word of anonymous sources, befitting a tabloid.”



Johnson added that Rubio had not discussed leaving his position and would continue serving in Trump’s administration.

Similarly, White House spokesperson, Beni Rae Harmony, described the report as a fabricated story, insisting that Rubio remains committed to Trump and the Make America Great Again movement.

Rubio’s reported consideration of an exit comes after Republicans suffered significant losses in Tuesday’s midterm elections, with Democrats securing control of both chambers of Congress in a development that could constrain Trump’s legislative agenda and intensify investigations into his administration.



The electoral setback has also raised questions about the future of the administration’s foreign policy, particularly the US-Israeli war against Iran, which has generated domestic political pressure and uncertainty in international energy markets.

A departure by Rubio before January could enable Trump to nominate a replacement before Democrats assume control of the Senate, potentially making confirmation easier than it would be under the new congressional arrangement.

Democrats are expected to investigate several administration initiatives, including operations against alleged drug-smuggling vessels in the Caribbean Sea, in which Rubio was involved.



The former Florida senator has emerged as one of Trump’s most trusted officials, having transformed from a rival during the 2016 Republican presidential primaries into a key member of the president’s inner circle.

Rubio and Vice President JD Vance have also frequently been mentioned as possible contenders to succeed Trump as the Republican Party’s presidential candidate in 2028.



However, his reported consideration of leaving the administration has raised questions about whether he wants to distance himself from the politically damaging Iran conflict and position himself for a future political comeback.

Rubio has consistently defended the decision to launch military attacks against Iran, although he has also sought to maintain some distance from the conflict.



He has concentrated on implementing Trump’s Venezuela policy, including the operation that resulted in the capture of President Nicolas Maduro and subsequent engagement with his successor, Delcy Rodriguez, over efforts to unlock the country’s oil reserves.

He has also overseen increased economic pressure on Cuba as Washington seeks to weaken the Communist Party’s decades-long hold on power.



Some people close to Rubio reportedly believe he could return to the private sector and consider his political options after the 2028 election cycle. Others have suggested he may prefer to avoid a potentially divisive contest within the Republican Party, particularly if Vance decides to seek the party’s nomination.



Meanwhile, the consequences of the Republican defeat have extended beyond Washington, with international oil markets reacting to expectations that Trump could face pressure to reconsider his military strategy against Iran.

Crude oil prices fell for a fourth consecutive day yesterday, with Brent crude and West Texas Intermediate extending losses amid growing expectations that the administration could pursue diplomatic options to end the conflict.



Brent crude futures fell by as much as 8.6 per cent to $94.66 per barrel, while US benchmark WTI dropped to $88.08, extending a four-day rout that reflected concerns about the potential easing of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

Earlier trading data showed Brent futures down 97 cents, or 1.03 per cent, at $93.65 per barrel, while WTI declined $1.14, or 1.29 per cent, to $86.98.



The declines followed an over eight per cent plunge on Wednesday that pushed both benchmarks to their lowest levels since August 31.

However, subsequent data from OilPrice.com showed some recovery, with Brent crude futures trading at $97.94, up 3.51 per cent, while WTI rose to $90.27, representing a 2.44 per cent increase. The S&P Energy Index, however, declined 4.77 per cent to 976.18.



Market analysts attributed the initial sell-off largely to political developments in the United States, particularly the Democratic victories in the midterm elections and the possibility that the Trump administration could come under pressure to end the war.

Trump, in an interview with Fox News, attributed the Republican losses partly to rising petrol prices, saying: “I think it’s the gasoline price.”

He had earlier told the Financial Times that there were no immediate plans to strike Iran.

Vance also linked the Republican defeat to the conflict, writing on X, “The reason we lost is the war. Any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.”

In a separate interview with CNN, the vice president said both he and Trump were optimistic about the possibility of a negotiated settlement.



“The president and I both feel really good about the prospect of potentially coming to a negotiated settlement,” he said.

Rubio had similarly indicated on Sunday that Trump preferred a diplomatic resolution to the Iranian conflict rather than continued military action.



Meanwhile, Qatar has continued to mediate negotiations between Washington and Tehran in an effort to prevent further escalation.

Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed that a delegation from the Gulf country had held discussions in Tehran as part of efforts to reach an agreement.



Reports by Qatari news outlet Al-Jadeed suggested significant progress in the negotiations, including possible concessions by Iran on its nuclear programme and the release of frozen assets.

However, a senior Iranian official swiftly dismissed the reports, contributing to a partial recovery in oil prices.

In another development, Iran announced exemptions for some of its major trading partners from restrictions on shipping through the strategic Strait of Hormuz.



Vice Chairman of the Iranian Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, Ahmad Hayat-Moghaddam, told the Iranian Student’s News Agency that India, China, Iraq and Qatar had been exempted from the transit restrictions.

“We have currently exempted India, China, Iraq and Qatar from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Ships from these countries pass freely,” Hayat-Moghaddam said.



He explained that the exemptions were based on mutual interests and specific considerations. He stated that India’s exemption was intended to facilitate medicine imports into Iran, while China’s was aimed at securing political support from Beijing.

The development came amid mounting pressure on Iran’s oil export operations following the prolonged US naval blockade, while attacks on commercial vessels have continued to heighten security concerns across the Gulf.



The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre reported at least four attacks on commercial vessels since the beginning of the month across the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf of Oman.

The Houthis also claimed to have targeted Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, although Saudi authorities did not confirm the reported attack.



For Nigeria, Africa’s largest oil producer, the decline in international crude prices presents mixed implications for the economy.

Lower crude prices could reduce Nigeria’s oil export earnings and government revenue, given the country’s heavy dependence on petroleum exports for foreign exchange and public financing.

Crude oil remains a major source of Nigeria’s foreign exchange earnings and accounts for a substantial proportion of government revenue. A sustained decline below $95 per barrel could narrow fiscal buffers, weaken external reserves and increase pressure on the naira.



However, cheaper crude and petroleum products in the international market could potentially provide some relief through lower domestic petrol and diesel prices, with possible positive implications for transportation costs and inflation.

The outlook for oil prices remains uncertain, with developments in Washington and the outcome of Qatar-mediated negotiations expected to influence market direction.



A resumption of US military operations against Iran could trigger another surge in crude prices, potentially pushing benchmarks above $110 per barrel, while a successful diplomatic agreement could sustain downward pressure and keep prices below $90.

World.title: Simbiat Asiru: The Global Vanguard of Contemporary African Luxury
World.content:
When Simbiat Asiru stitched her first dress under Simbby House of Fab in 2011, she wasn’t just making clothes; she was laying the foundation for a global movement. Fourteen years later, that small Lagos dream has been reborn as TÀBÍRA Studio, a contemporary womenswear label that has travelled from Abu Dhabi to Nottingham, from Instagram feeds to international runways, selling out as it goes. Now a global vanguard of contemporary African luxury, Asiru is proving that African design is not just part of the world’s fashion conversation, rather, it is leading it, MARY NNAH writes

I n the ever-shifting world of contemporary womenswear, where trends rise and fall with the season, true staying power belongs to designers who offer something deeper than fashion; they offer identity.

That is the story of Nigerian designer Simbiat Asiru, the fashion designer, stylist and creative director who has quietly built one of Africa’s most formidable fashion success stories.



Asiru first founded Simbby House of Fab in 2011. For over a decade, she honed her craft, her clientele, and her commercial instincts. Then, in a bold, strategic move in 2025, she rebranded the business as TÀBÍRA Studio -a contemporary ready-to-wear womenswear label.

The rebrand was more than a name change. It was a declaration: a new chapter, a highly sophisticated global outlook, and her emergence as an international leader in the contemporary fashion design sector.

More Than Clothes: A Methodology

Asiru’s design methodology extends far beyond conventional garment construction. To watch her work is to watch a rigorous exploration of expressive silhouettes, distinctive prints, and the intricate interplay of fabric, colour, and form.

Her unique approach brings traditional cultural influences into a seamless conversation with contemporary luxury design, creating high-character collections that completely bypass fleeting trends. These are not just clothes to be worn; they are statements of confidence, individuality and timelessness.

A Proven Track Record of Global Market Expansion

What truly distinguishes Asiru’s journey is not just creativity, but commerce – a sustained track record of building a fashion infrastructure with true international reach.

As early as 2017, long before many of her peers looked beyond Nigeria, she successfully expanded her commercial presence into the competitive United Arab Emirates market, marking a major milestone with a high-profile launch in Abu Dhabi.



Today, that early ambition has blossomed into a truly borderless commercial entity. TÀBÍRA Studio now serves an active, premium customer base across the United States, Canada, Europe, Australia, and Africa. For Asiru, international growth is not simply about taking a brand into new markets; it is about engineering a distinct, recognisable aesthetic that commands commercial viability and resonates deeply with women across diverse global cultures; from a buyer in Toronto to a woman in Lagos.

Bringing ATUNBÍ II to the UK Runway

In 2026, Asiru brought TÀBÍRA Studio’s creative vision to the European stage with her critically acclaimed collection, ATUNBÍ II: The Rebirth Edit, showcased at Culture Fashion Show UK 2026.

The collection was widely praised by fashion critics for its distinctive approach to contemporary luxury, masterfully uniting sculptural silhouettes and vivid custom prints. Among the standout moments was the Olori Ara Dress, a highlight design that captured the collection’s soul.



Under the creative direction of Gemma Hall, Founder and Creative Strategy Director, the presentation served as a headline showcase on a premier platform celebrating high creativity, culture, and leading international design talent. Through ATUNBÍ II, the collection’s themes of renewal and transformation perfectly mirrored Asiru’s own career trajectory – continually scaling and refining her design foundations to meet the highest global standards.

Beyond the Runway: TÀBÍRA Studio’s Nottingham Commercial Success

If the runway proved TÀBÍRA’s creative power, what happened next proved its commercial power.

In July 2026, TÀBÍRA Studio bridged the gap between runway presentation and direct retail by hosting a highly successful physical fashion exhibition at the historic Oakleigh Lodge Social Club in Nottingham (NG6 9DD).

The exhibition represented a major commercial milestone for the brand’s expansion into the United Kingdom ecosystem. Moving beyond digital retail, the physical setting allowed UK buyers and brand enthusiasts to engage directly with the label’s tailoring and textiles; to touch, feel, and truly experience the quality.



The response was emphatic. The event resulted in an exceptional commercial response, with a significant volume of the collection selling out directly on the floor – proving a robust, immediate market demand for Asiru’s work within the competitive UK fashion economy. It was validation that British women wanted what TÀBÍRA was offering.

Defining the Future of Contemporary Luxury

Beyond her exceptional creative output, Asiru holds a Master of Science degree in Project Management from the University of Northampton. This academic background heavily complements her decade of entrepreneurial experience, bringing a rare, highly structured operational perspective to production schedules, international logistics, and brand scalability – the often-invisible engine behind any global fashion house.



Her vision for TÀBÍRA Studio remains rooted in individuality, confidence, and timeless design.

As TÀBÍRA Studio permanently develops its international footprint from Abu Dhabi to Nottingham, from runway to retail, Simbiat Asiru stands as a prime example of modern fashion leadership: an independent designer achieving global growth without ever losing sight of her creative vision. She is not just following the global conversation on contemporary luxury. She is leading it.

World.title: N70,000 Transport Allowance: TUC Insists on Sustainable Salary Increase
World.content:
Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The Trade Union Congress (TUC) has reaffirmed its demand for a sustainable salary increase as alternative to another wage award, insisting the N70,000 transport allowance agreed between federal government and Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) is not enough to address workers’ hardship.

In a communique issued at end of its emergency National Administrative Council (NAC) meeting held on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, TUC said a salary increase offers a more meaningful intervention to improve purchasing power and living standards.

The communique signed by Secretary General, Comrade Nuhu Toro, said NAC reaffirmed its position as stated in its press release of October 21, 2026, emphasizing that minimum wage is a statutory floor and not a ceiling on workers’ earnings.

TUC said it is demanding salary increase and not another wage award, particularly in view of federal government’s failure to fully implement wage award palliative agreed on October 2, 2023, which was intended to run until new minimum wage was signed into law on July 29, 2024. Under that agreement, workers received an average of only three months out of ten months agreed upon.

“The Council maintained that a sustainable salary increase offers a more meaningful intervention to improve workers’ purchasing power and living standards,” it said.

The NAC also acknowledged positions of some of its public-sector affiliates – SSAUTHRIA, NUAHP and SSASCGOC – noting they are consistent with earlier position of Congress.

It stressed workers’ welfare cannot be advanced by disregarding collective bargaining rights of affected unions or undermining their legitimate representation.

It reaffirmed TUC as a recognized trade union centre with legitimate mandate to represent, defend and negotiate for members in line with ILO Conventions 87 and 98, and resolved to pursue constructive and result-oriented engagement with government towards implementing resolutions of its October 8 meeting in Abuja.

The Council noted TUC is on path of long-term institutional renewal under leadership of Comrade (Engr.) Festus Osifo, acknowledging such journey is not without distractions and resistance, but resolved to remain resolute and consolidate gains through collective decision-making.

On accountability, TUC reaffirmed its accountability to National Executive Council (NEC), highest decision-making organ between Delegates’ Conferences, saying it has acted in accordance with NEC directives and Constitution.

It therefore resolved leaders should refocus efforts on securing salary increase by engaging stakeholders and refraining from public exchanges on matter, stressing Congress believes in purposeful, result-oriented leadership that delivers tangible benefits rather than distractions or unsustainable interventions.

World.title: Education Minister, Alausa Unveils 26 Education Reforms, Disburses N372.6bn in Student Loans
World.content:
Sunday Ehigiator

The Federal Government has highlighted 26 education initiatives introduced under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, covering university reforms, student financing, teacher development, technical education, research, digital learning and infrastructure.

The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, outlined the initiatives in an A–Z document titled From Reform to Results, which he shared on his X account recently.

The document, which covers the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI), highlighted programmes designed to expand access to education, strengthen institutions, promote research and innovation, and equip young Nigerians with practical skills.

Among the major interventions is the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, which has processed 1,659,853 applications, with a total of ₦372.62 billion reportedly disbursed to beneficiaries across 319 institutions.

The fund comprises ₦192.89 billion paid as institutional fees and ₦179.73 billion disbursed as upkeep allowances.

The government also highlighted its agreement with the Academic Staff Union of Universities, which provides for a 40 per cent increase in academic staff remuneration, alongside revised allowances and improved welfare provisions.

Under the Campus Mobility Initiative, the government said it had deployed 780 electric tricycles across 48 universities to improve transportation within campuses.

The Diaspora BRIDGE programme, designed to connect Nigerian experts abroad with local institutions, has recorded 1,141 registered experts, with 16,675 students benefiting across 107 tertiary institutions.

On teacher development, the document disclosed that 53,553 teachers had registered on EduRevamp, while 51,794 registrations were recorded for the first cohort of the Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway.

It added that the government had invested ₦2 billion in the programme, which targets 250,000 teachers by 2027.

The administration also listed its Free Technical Education initiative, which provides tuition, boarding, textbooks and uniforms to students in federal and selected state technical colleges.

According to the document, 38 federal and state technical colleges have been rehabilitated to improve facilities for practical skills training.

On girl-child education, the government reported that 7.19 million girls were benefiting from direct interventions across 21 states under the Adolescent Girls Initiative for Learning and Empowerment, while 3.7 million girls were enrolled in junior and senior secondary schools.

It added that more than 422,720 girls had completed life-skills programmes, while over 10,000 schools had benefited from improved classrooms, water, sanitation and hygiene facilities, as well as teaching and learning materials.

Another major intervention is the HOPE-Education programme, supported by $552 million in World Bank funding, which targets 29 million children, more than 500,000 teachers, 65,000 public schools and 10,000 non-formal learning centres.

The ministry also highlighted the Inspire Live! initiative, which provides live online lessons for pupils from Primary One to Senior Secondary School Three, supported by certified teachers and artificial intelligence-assisted question-and-answer services.

On tertiary admissions, the government said it had removed the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination requirement for admission into National Certificate in Education programmes and reviewed entry requirements for selected National Diploma programmes.

To promote research and innovation, the administration introduced Research, Innovation and Commercialisation Committees in universities to encourage the transformation of academic research into practical solutions, businesses and employment opportunities.

The initiative also includes a National Laureate Prize with an annual award fund of ₦365 million to recognise excellence in research and innovation.

The document further disclosed that annual nursing enrolment had increased from 28,000 to 115,000, while medical and dental enrolment rose from 5,000 to 12,000.

Pharmacy enrolment also increased from 3,644 to 7,419, while ₦110 billion had been committed to the rehabilitation of 24 medical schools.

On efforts to tackle out-of-school children, the government reported that more than one million children had been reintegrated into the education system, while 200 bilingual learning centres had been established and 1,400 Tsangaya teachers trained.

It also listed 13,000 classrooms for construction or rehabilitation.

Similarly, the Tertiary Institutions Staff Support Fund provides financial assistance of up to ₦10 million to academic and non-academic staff in public tertiary institutions for housing, transportation, medical needs, education and other welfare requirements.

The government said ₦28 billion had been disbursed to 15,000 workers across 153 public tertiary institutions under the programme.

Other initiatives include the reintroduction of the National Learning Assessment, a new national curriculum featuring Nigerian History and stronger emphasis on Civic and Heritage Studies, as well as renewable energy projects for universities and teaching hospitals.

Under the renewable energy programme, solar mini-grids had been installed in 37 federal universities and seven teaching hospitals, while 20 federal and state universities had been equipped with compressed natural gas refuelling stations.

The Student Venture Capital Grant, another initiative highlighted, attracted 30,639 registrations from 404 tertiary institutions, with 65 finalists selected.

The document stated that more than ₦2.5 billion had been disbursed to 45 student entrepreneurs, with each beneficiary receiving up to ₦50 million in equity-free funding.

The Technical and Vocational Education and Training programme also recorded more than 2.8 million applicants and 156,446 verified trainees.

It added that over ₦65.7 billion had been disbursed in stipends and start-up support to verified trainees, while ₦30.2 billion was paid to training centres.

The government also highlighted efforts to strengthen university financial autonomy through revenue diversification, improved governance, research commercialisation and partnerships with the Nigeria Higher Education Foundation.

On digital access, the ministry reported that more than 40 million learners and 215,000 schools had been mapped through the National Education Data Infrastructure to improve education planning.

It also disclosed that 16,000 learners had enrolled in the first cohort of the Digital Technical Academy, while 1,000 smart boards had been deployed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

Additionally, 111 tertiary institutions had been onboarded onto AWS Academy.

The government said 58 of 63 federal universities, 37 of 41 federal polytechnics and 27 of 29 federal colleges of education had been onboarded onto the Federal Tertiary Institutions Governance Portal.

More than four million learners had also been assigned Learner National Identification Numbers, against a target of 40 million by 2027.

Other programmes include the Entrepreneurship, Innovation and Business Incubation Certification initiative, currently being implemented in 14 federal universities, and the Zero-Rated Education initiative, which seeks to make approved educational platforms accessible to learners at reduced or no data costs.

The ministry said the initiatives collectively formed part of the administration’s broader efforts to improve education delivery, strengthen institutional capacity and expand opportunities for Nigerian students and educators.

World.title: Opposition Parties Plan Single Situation Room for 2027 Polls
World.content:
*SDP warns members against participating in APC’s rainbow colalition

*Condemns sack of ADC candidates, sack of party’s leadership

Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja

The National Chairman of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Prof Sadiq Gombe, has disclosed that the opposition parties would have a single situation room for the 2027 general elections, even as he foreclosed the party’s involvement in the All Progressives Congress (APC) rainbow coalition.

He stated this at the party’s strategic discussions with its Governorship Candidates Forum (GCF), at the party’s national headquarters in Abuja on Thursday.

According to Gombe, all the opposition political parties will have a single situation room to monitor the 2027 general elections.

“We have a situation whereby our agents will come together, will train together. We have common situation room so that we will be our own INEC at the polling unit. We will be our own security at the polling unit, to make sure that there must be free, fair and credible elections come 2027,” he said.

He also cautioned the party candidate against joining the APC rainbow coalition. He said, “We are not into any rainbow coalition whereby we will be candidates here and we will be professing for APC presidency.

“We have taken a stand that as much as we are not part of anything to do with any rainbow coalition, if at all any member of our party engages in that, we have told the national and the party to discipline any member that goes into any rainbow coalition.

“I want to assure you that SDP as a political party we don’t have anything to do with rainbow coalition. SDP is along with other political parties in the opposition doing everything possible to rescue our dear country in a coalition of the Nigerian people, to make sure that we have some kind of understanding and alliances whereby we make sure that we have free, fair and credible elections.

“As you are aware the sitting government, when it realizes that it lost touch with the Nigerian people based on bad governance and record in all areas of power and governance in this country, they resorted to something they call rainbow coalition.

“But they are going around trying to find how they will infiltrate some political parties to cajole their members in a so-called rainbow coalition so that they can break our ranks.”

He also stated that the SDP was not a party to those calling for the postponement of the general elections.

“We want to assure Nigerians that we are not part of any attempt whatsoever of shifting the elections as a result of whatever. We are ready. We are doing everything possible to win the election at the national level and most of the states of the federation, down to the states houses of assembly.”

On the failure of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish the names of his party’s candidates, he said, “We are still following the matter in court where they refused to publish the names of our candidates despite the fact that we followed all due process as enshrined in the Electoral Act, the constitution of the land and the constitution of our party, and party nomination that is exclusive to the internal affairs of the party,” he said.

He also raised issues with the high court ruling that sacked the African Democractic Congress (ADC) leadership led by David Mark and all the candidates.

Gombe said, “We condemn everything possible towards the so-called disqualification of the ADC candidate, Atiku Abubakar. This is a democracy. We want Nigerians to be allowed to freely exercise their franchise.

“We will not allow anything that will truncate our democracy because we have come a long way in this journey. And the president and the party in power are the product of democracy. We will not allow that in a democracy to have an emperor and a dictator that will lead to the collapse of our democracy.

“We are calling on the judiciary to be up and doing to play neutral; equally the security agencies and INEC as an umpire. It has to show equity, it has to show that it has all it takes to be able to usher in free, fair and credible election.”

According to him, “There are issues around register of voters. There are issues around creation of some polling units and so on. SDP condemns all those issues and we want to assure Nigerians that we are going to do everything possible along with sister political parties to resist anything that will truncate our democracy.”

In his remarks, the Chairman, SDP Governorship Candidates Forum and the Nasarawa State SDP governorship candidate, Mohammed Adumu said, “We are here to have discussions with the national working committee on some of the strategies we put in place and what we need to do to make sure that we win in the fortcoming elections in the country.

“Not only for the governors, but right from the presidential election to the house of assembly. And we have exchanged ideas based on the different experiences that we got from the different states, just to cover the gaps that we feel exist, so that we don’t give the opposition the chance to shortchange us or make any impact, because we know right from now or this period that Nigerians are tired of the ruling party and they need change. And the only alternative is SDP, because SDP cares for the masses.”

He also noted that the SDP was taking the interests of the masses at heart, so as to alleviate their living condition.

World.title: NJC Recommends Appointment of 28 Judicial Officers
World.content:
– Directs Imo Judicial Service Commission to shortlist Acting CJ for interview

– Hands down one year suspension without pay to three others

Alex Enumah in Abuja

The National Judicial Council (NJC), has recommended the appointment of a Grand Kadi for Plateau State and 27 other candidates as Judicial Officers.

Meanwhile, the NJC has also recommended the suspension of three judges for one year without pay, over various infractions.

The body, took the decision at its 112th meeting held on November 3, 2026, under the Chairmanship of the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN) Hon. Justice Kudirat Motonmori Olatokunbo Kekere-Ekun.

According to a statement by the NJC’s Deputy Director (Information), Kemi Babalola-Ogedengbe, 24 out of the 28 candidates recommended for appointment as Judges came from the High Courts of Kano, Ebonyi, Edo, Adamawa and Ogun States.

“One candidate was recommended for appointment as Grand Kadi of the Plateau State Sharia Court of Appeal, while another was recommended as Kadi of the Adamawa State Sharia Court of Appeal.

“Two others were recommended for appointment as judges of the Adamawa State Customary Court of Appeal”, the statement read in part.

Those recommended includes; Hon Kadi, Tijjani Jibrin Zololo, as Grand Kadi, Plateau State Sharia Court of Appeal; while those recommended for appointment as Judges for the Kano State High Court are; Nafisah Yusuf Hassan; Halima Yahuza Ahmad; Abdullahi Abdulsalam Bature; Musa Ibrahim Umar.

While Amaga Dickson Edmund was recommended as a judge of the Ebonyi State High Court, the following were recommended for Edo State High Court; Osawaru, Benson Osagie; Omoruyi, Taiye Osayanmon; Adamaigbo, Dorothy Ibhade Usiobaifo, Festus Osagie; Oiwoh, Pius Idemudia; Amune, Majebi Samuel; and Imuekemhe, Emike Jessica.

Adamawa State High Court has Sa’ad, Aminu; Musa, Ibrahim Ulenda; Giwa, Sadiq; Mijinyawa, Musa Bala; Ibrahim, Japhet; Bakari, Aliyu and Ahmadu, Yakubu.

For Ogun State High Court, the following were recommended: Oke, Olakulehin Luqman Abiola; Obienu, Adebimpe Folusho; Daudu, Fatimat Adeola; Kadiri, Rafiat Bolanle; and Osho, Oludotun Olaniyi.

While Abubakar Ishaku was recommended as a judicial officer in the Adamawa Sharia Court of Appeal, Elshama Gwama Dimas; and David Benjamin Pembi are to be appointed as Judges of the Adamawa Sharia Customary Court of Appeal.

According to the statement, all recommended candidates are expected to be sworn-in by their respective State Governors without delay.

Meanwhile, the NJC has directed the Imo State Judicial Service Commission to include the name of the most senior Judge of the State High Court, the Acting Chief Judge, Hon. Justice Ijeoma Agugua, in the list of candidates for appointment as substantive Chief Judge of the State.

“The decision followed the consideration of a petition dated June 11, 2026, by Mr. Bob Kay Njemanze, who challenged the exclusion of Justice Agugua from the shortlist submitted by the Imo State Judicial Service Commission.

“In considering the petition, Council noted that although the State Judicial Service Commission has the constitutional responsibility to advise the NJC on suitable candidates for appointment as Chief Judge, the Council retains the authority to determine the suitability of persons presented to it.

“It consequently directed its Secretariat to formally request the Imo State JSC to include the name of Hon. Justice I. O. Agugua in the shortlist”, the statement added.

Meanwhile, it disclosed that in the area of discipline, the council considered nine investigation reports concerning petitions against judicial officers over their handling of cases, and subsequently approved the recommendation of one-year suspension without pay for three judicial officers as well as additional restrictions on the elevation of two of those suspended.

The suspended Judicial officers are: Hon. Justice Hannatu Mohammed Kabir, Nasarawa State High Court; Hon. Grand Kadi Mohammed Sani Salihu, Jigawa State Sharia Court of Appeal and Hon. Justice Sobere Biambo of the Rivers State High Court.

World.title: 90% passing accuracy: Relebohile Mofokeng helps USG win away in Spain
World.content:
Relebohile Mofokeng plays for Royale Union Saint-Gilliose in the UEFA Europa League. Image: UEFA media

Relebohile Mofokeng, better known as President Yama 2k, delivered another mature performance. He diplayed his technical quality, wit and creativity against difficult opposition on Spanish soil.

The 22-year-old forward proved to be a standout creative outlet for the Belgian champions. He consistently carried the ball at speed into dangerous areas and unlocked Vigo’s guard.

RELEBHOHILE MOFOKENG WINS PENALTY IN IMPRESSIVE EUROPEAN DISPLAY

He started in an attacking role and remained on the pitch for 86 minutes before making way for a substitute.



Despite receiving a 6.5 Sofascore rating, Mofokeng made several important contributions, including winning a penalty for Union SG.

Mofokeng, linked with German clubs Bayer Leverkusen and SC Freiburg, registered 44 touches and demonstrated impressive composure in possession. The Sharpeville-born star completing 26 of his 29 attempted passes for an outstanding 90% passing accuracy.

His distribution was particularly impressive in advanced areas. The Bafana Bafana attacker completed 21 of 22 passes in the opposition’s half while also recording 16 successful passes into the final third.

Furthermore, Mofokeng completed all two of his attempted layoffs, connected with two of his three progressive passes and created three key passes for his teammates.

FULL STATISTICS AGAINST CELTA VIGO

The South African winger also showed his willingness to take on defenders and make things happen in the final third.

He registered two shots, although neither found the back of the net, with one going off target and the other being blocked.



Mofokeng also recorded nine carries into space, demonstrating his ability to drive Union SG forward and put the opposition under pressure.

Although he lost possession nine times, he contributed three defensive actions to help his team out of possession.

Overall, it was another encouraging European outing for the former Orlando Pirates sensation, who continues to gain valuable experience against top-level opposition.
